calls.title: Collection 2026 - Decode Gallery
calls.description: Decode Gallery's open-theme exhibition — no themes, no limits. At least 26 images selected. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ultra Premium Luster paper, museum-quality framing and matting handled by the gallery. 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to all skill levels. Exhibition August 1–29, 2026 in Tucson, AZ. Juror: Holly Hart, Decode Gallery founder.
jury: Holly Hart, Conceptual Fine Art Photographer & Decode Gallery Founder
calls.summary: Open-theme show — no themes, no limits. 26+ selected. Free pro printing on Epson + museum framing. Tucson, AZ.
prose: Decode Gallery is a Tucson, Arizona photography gallery founded by conceptual fine art photographer Holly Hart, who also serves as juror for the gallery's calls. "Collection 2026" is the gallery's open-theme exhibition — no themes, no subject restrictions, no limits beyond technical quality.

The selection structure is generous: at least 26 images are selected for the physical exhibition. What's unusual: the gallery covers all professional printing on Epson printers with Ultra Premium Luster paper, plus museum-quality framing in 22×22 inch white frames with precut white mats — the artist provides only the high-resolution JPEG. Prints are retained in the gallery's flat files for two years after the exhibition for further promotion and sales.

Sales terms split commission 50/50 between artist and gallery. Selected work is also promoted across Decode's website, social media, and editorial publications. The 2026 exhibition runs August 1 through 29 in Tucson.

Entry fee is $40 for up to 5 images. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers at all skill levels. The deadline is June 27, 2026; selected artists are notified within two weeks of the deadline.

calls.title: SE Center for Photography — The Art of Architecture
calls.description: Virtual juried exhibition seeking architectural photography in all forms — urban or rural, B&W or color, analog, digital or antique processes. Juror Michael Pannier (fine art photographer based in Greenville, SC) selects 35–40 images for the virtual gallery. Selected artists receive a portfolio review with the juror. 0% commission on sales. All photographers regardless of location, age, or skill level.
calls.summary: Virtual show on architectural photography — urban, rural, analog or digital. Juror: Michael Pannier. Portfolio review.
prose: The Southeast Center for Photography (SEC4P) is a Greenville, South Carolina photography organization (104 S Main St, Suite 841) that runs themed virtual juried exhibitions. "The Art of Architecture" is the center's open call for architectural photography in all forms — urban or rural, black-and-white or color, analog, digital, or antique processes.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Michael Pannier, a Greenville-based fine art photographer with thirty years' practice. Selection takes 35 to 40 images for an approximately one-month virtual gallery, with social media promotion across SEC4P's Facebook, Instagram, and X channels and an archived online slideshow plus video walkthrough. Selected artists also receive a portfolio review with the SEC4P director.
Entry fees: $35 for non-members for up to 5 images ($6 each additional, max 15), or $28 / $5 for SEC4P members. There is no sales commission.

Eligibility is open to all photographers regardless of location, age, or skill level. Work previously exhibited at SEC4P within the prior two years is ineligible. The 2026 deadline is July 1; results are announced July 15.

calls.title: Ethereal
calls.description: Seeking images that explore the intangible — works that evoke lightness, transience, and the space between what is seen and what is felt. Both traditional and experimental photographic processes welcome. Juror: John Horowitz, photographer and curator whose work resides in Purdue University's permanent collection. Exhibition June 5 – July 1, 2026 at A Photographer's Place in Raleigh, NC. Opening reception June 5, 7–9 PM.
calls.summary: Images that explore the intangible — lightness, transience, the space between seen and felt. Juror: John Horowitz.

calls.title: Critical Mass 2026
calls.fee: $65 early bird / $75 regular; +$200 if Top 200 finalist
calls.description: Photolucida's annual program connecting photographers with the international photography community. Submit 10 images for pre-screening; approximately 200 finalists are then reviewed by up to 200 photography professionals worldwide — curators, gallerists, publishers, editors, educators, and media. The Top 50 are announced each year, alongside book awards and exhibition opportunities. Past finalists have gained acquisitions, exhibitions, and publication features. Open to photographers at any career stage. AI-generated imagery is not accepted for the 2026 cycle.
calls.summary: Photolucida's annual review by 200 photography pros. Top 50 designation, book awards, exhibition opportunities. AI not accepted.
prose: Critical Mass is Photolucida's flagship annual program, structured as a two-stage portfolio review by an unusually large jury. Photographers submit a 10-image portfolio; approximately 200 are advanced to a finalist round, where they are reviewed by up to 200 photography professionals from around the world — curators, gallerists, publishers, editors, educators, and journalists. The wide-jury format means each finalist's portfolio reaches roughly 200 industry-side viewers regardless of whether they place in the top 50.

From the finalist pool, the Top 50 designation is announced each year alongside book awards and exhibition opportunities. Past Critical Mass finalists have used the program to secure acquisitions, gallery representation, monograph publications, and editorial features — the value is partly the awards but more often the introduction itself.

Entry fees are tiered: $65 early-bird (June 1–9, 2026) or $75 regular (June 10 through July 1, 2026). Photographers who advance to the Top 200 finalist round pay an additional $200 to remain in the running.

Eligibility is open to photographers at any career stage. AI-generated imagery is explicitly excluded for the 2026 cycle. Photolucida itself is a Portland, Oregon-based non-profit. The 2026 deadline is July 1 at noon Eastern Time.

calls.title: Immagini e trame d'acqua — Le Stanze della Fotografia Open Call
calls.description: Inaugural open call from Fondazione Le Stanze della Fotografia (Venice) and the Association for the Heritage of the Prosecco Hills of Conegliano and Valdobbiadene, gathering testimonies, stories, and reflections on water as a force and necessity within cultural and landscape heritage. The project starts from the UNESCO World Heritage Prosecco Hills but invites participants to explore the theme in relation to other heritage sites in Italy and worldwide. Two participation formats: a photography-and-text project (3–10 images plus a narrative text up to three pages) or a video-story (max 2 minutes combining images, words, and sound). Submissions made by email; participants must also publish their work on their own social channels tagging the promoters. Three awards per category — Best Visual Narrative, Best Language/Experimentation, and Special Mention for Under-30/Students. Selected works exhibited at Le Stanze della Fotografia and gathered in a brochure distributed at the foundation's bookshop. Open to citizens, students, photographers, videomakers, and storytelling enthusiasts of any age and nationality.
jury: Denis Curti, Photography critic and curator
Marina Montedoro, President, Association for the Heritage of the Prosecco Hills
calls.summary: Free open call from Venice's Le Stanze della Fotografia on water in cultural & landscape heritage. Photography+text or video.
prose: Le Stanze della Fotografia is a Venice-based photography foundation, located on the Isola di San Giorgio Maggiore opposite St Mark's Square, run jointly with the Fondazione Giorgio Cini. Its inaugural open call "Immagini e trame d'acqua" — Italian for "images and weavings of water" — is organized in partnership with the Association for the Heritage of the Prosecco Hills of Conegliano and Valdobbiadene (the UNESCO World Heritage site north of Venice) and Marsilio Arte.

The brief is open in scope: water as a force and a necessity within cultural and landscape heritage, anchored by the Prosecco Hills but extending to any heritage site in Italy or abroad. Two submission formats: a photography-and-text project (3 to 10 images plus a narrative up to three pages) or a video-story (maximum two minutes combining images, words, and sound). There is no entry fee, and the call is open to citizens, students, photographers, videomakers, and storytelling enthusiasts of any age and nationality, individually or in collectives.

Three awards are given per category: Best Visual Narrative, Best Language and Experimentation, and a Special Mention for Under-30 entrants and students. Selected work is exhibited at Le Stanze della Fotografia and gathered in a brochure distributed through the foundation's bookshop and partner cultural venues. The jury includes photographer Maurizio Galimberti, photography critic and curator Denis Curti, writers Antonio G. Bortoluzzi and Sabrina Zuccato, and Marina Montedoro, president of the Heritage Association. Submissions close September 30, 2026; winners are announced within twenty days.

calls.title: EXPOSURE 2026 — 30th Annual Members' Juried Exhibition
calls.description: Photographic Resource Center's 30th annual members' juried exhibition. Twelve photographers selected to exhibit three works each. Juried by Audrey Lee Sands, Richard L. Menschel Associate Curator of Photography at Harvard Art Museums. Exhibition runs July 31 – September 6, 2026 at University Hall, Lesley University in Cambridge, MA. Applicants must be PRC members through September. Awards: Juror's Choice Award ($200) and two PRC Choice Awards ($100 each).
calls.summary: PRC Boston's 30th annual members' juried show. 12 photographers × 3 works. Juried by Audrey Lee Sands of Harvard Art Museums.
jury: Audrey Lee Sands, Richard L. Menschel Associate Curator of Photography, Harvard Art Museums
prose: The Photographic Resource Center (PRC) is a Boston-area photography organization that has run its annual members' juried exhibition for thirty years (the 2026 cycle marks the 30th edition). The show is hosted at University Hall, Lesley University in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Audrey Lee Sands, the Richard L. Menschel Associate Curator of Photography at the Harvard Art Museums. Twelve photographers are selected from the membership pool, with each chosen photographer exhibiting three works.

Cash awards: a Juror's Choice Award of $200 and two PRC Choice Awards of $100 each. Beyond cash, the exhibition runs July 31 through September 6, 2026 at the Lesley University venue, with selected work catalogued by PRC.
Eligibility is restricted to PRC members through September. The application fee is $35. Submissions go through a Google Form. The 2026 deadline is June 15.

calls.title: Vermont Center for Photography Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: Inaugural artist residency at Vermont Center for Photography (VCP) in Brattleboro, VT. Two-week residency from October 23 to November 6, 2026. Open to photographers and lens-based artists at any career stage, working in analog, digital, or hybrid formats. Priority for artists who would benefit from darkroom and digital lab access, have a focused project proposal, and face barriers to creating elsewhere. Includes 24/7 access to VCP's darkroom, digital lab, and lighting studio; a $500 creation stipend; 14-night stay at the historic Latchis Hotel (4-minute walk from VCP); and a one-month solo exhibition in the Picker Print Gallery.
calls.summary: Inaugural 2-week residency at VCP Brattleboro. Darkroom and digital lab access, $500 stipend, hotel stay, and solo exhibition.
prose: The Vermont Center for Photography (VCP) is launching an inaugural residency program in 2026, based at the center's facility in Brattleboro, Vermont (10 Green Street). The residency runs two weeks — October 23 through November 6, 2026 — with the resident receiving a $500 creation stipend, a 14-night stay at the nearby Latchis Hotel (a four-minute walk from VCP), and 24/7 access to the center's darkroom, digital lab, and lighting studio.

The residency culminates in a one-month solo exhibition at the Picker Print Gallery within VCP, with an opening reception on November 7, 2026. The combination of facilities access, accommodation, modest stipend, and built-in solo show distinguishes the program from purely studio-based residencies — the work made during the residency moves directly to gallery walls.

Eligibility is open to photographers and lens-based artists at any career stage working in analog, digital, or hybrid processes. The selection committee gives priority to applicants who would benefit from VCP's specialized equipment or who face barriers to similar facilities elsewhere — financial, spatial, or technical.

The application fee is $25 ($15 for VCP members). Applications require a CV/résumé, project proposal, and 10 to 15 work samples. The deadline is June 30, 2026 (11:59 PM EST), with notifications sent July 31, 2026.

calls.title: Wild & Free — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
calls.description: Public art exhibition on billboard ad space throughout New York City, curated by Gigi Chen, a contemporary wildlife-focused artist and nature photographer. Theme explores the close connection between nature, mythology, and civilization — how the natural world coexists with urban environments. Open to artists of all ages and backgrounds. Selected works displayed on NYC billboards for at least one month starting June 26, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has run public art billboard exhibitions since 2015.
calls.prize: Public billboard exhibition (1+ month) in NYC
calls.summary: NYC public art billboard exhibition curated by Gigi Chen. Theme: nature, mythology, and civilization. Opens June 26, 2026.

calls.title: The Printmaker and the Photographic Image: Dissolving Media Boundaries
calls.description: International juried exhibition for printmakers and photographers working in both traditions. Seeks hand-printed imagery that weds photographic elements with printmaking techniques — cyanotype, photogravure, photopolymer, photocollage, and other alternative processes especially welcome. Final image must be a hand-pulled print; no solely digital output. Successful images should display technical sophistication while conveying emotional valence. Exhibition June 19 – August 1, 2026 at Remarque Print Workshop & Gallery in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Maximum paper size 16×20". Accepted works must arrive by June 4, 2026. 50/50 commission on sales.
calls.summary: Hand-pulled prints combining photographic and printmaking techniques. Cyanotype, photogravure, photopolymer welcome. Albuquerque exhibition.

calls.title: Conversaciones — EMC Magazine Print Edition Open Call
calls.description: Open call for the printed edition of Conversaciones, EMC Magazine's photography open call returning in a new format after three virtual editions. The editorial team seeks images that speak to each other. Free theme. Up to 5 images per participant, analog or digital, submitted via WeTransfer at low resolution for selection and high-resolution TIFF (300 dpi, RGB) if accepted. Open worldwide to photographers of any nationality. Selected participants receive one printed copy of the magazine; international participants cover shipping. Authors retain intellectual property; EMC Magazine receives non-exclusive usage rights for this printed edition. Publication planned for July 2026.
calls.summary: Argentine indie photo magazine's printed edition open call. Free theme, $5 USD international fee, July 2026 publication.

calls.title: ESC 2036 — 0—1 Gallery Open Call
calls.description: 0—1 Gallery's annual open call inviting artists to imagine roughly ten years ahead, keeping in mind the pressure points of now — climate, extraction, technology, and what it means to remain human inside all that. Looking for works that speak of nature, technology, or human existence — from subtle gestures to monumental systems. All forms welcome including photography, new media, painting, sculpture, installation, performance, sound, graphics, video, mixed media, AR/VR, and writing. No entry fees; submit one link to portfolio, website, or project page. Open to everyone — artists at any stage from any place; age, gender, location, and background not used as filters. Selected artists included in a curated group exhibition in the Netherlands in 2026–2027 with additional visibility through 0—1's website and social media.
calls.summary: Free open call from The Hague gallery. Theme: nature, tech & humanity ten years ahead. Curated group exhibition 2026–2027.

calls.title: Being Human — Artdoc Magazine Open Call
calls.description: Documentary photography open call inviting photographers to examine how human presence manifests in diverse cultural contexts. Portraits, environmental images, and documentary work — all approaches welcome. Selected work may be featured in curated online exhibitions, the Featured Submissions page, or upcoming magazine issues. Submissions free for Artdoc Magazine members; non-members must subscribe to submit.
calls.summary: Documentary photography open call exploring human presence across cultural contexts. Magazine publication and online exhibitions.

calls.title: Flashes of Humanity — Pragovka Gallery 2027 Open Call
calls.description: Open call for the 2027 exhibition program and International Residency Program at Pragovka Gallery, a contemporary art space in Prague. Theme: Flashes of Humanity / Záblesky lidskosti — what it means to be human today, including subtle, almost imperceptible moments such as brief encounters and small acts of attention. Personal experiences, social questions, and experimental approaches all welcome; no medium restrictions, photography eligible. Two tracks: (1) exhibition projects (authorial or curatorial) at Pragovka Gallery in 2027 with the gallery covering transport, installation, accommodation, travel by agreement, PR, documentation, printed materials, and artist fees; (2) residency projects in the International Residency Program with an 80 m² studio, accommodation, travel by agreement, artist fees, and material cost contributions. Open to Czech and international artists and curators. Submission deadline 11:59 PM on May 17, 2026.
calls.prize: Exhibition or residency at Pragovka Gallery
calls.summary: Czech contemporary art gallery's 2027 open call for exhibition projects or international residencies. Photography eligible.

calls.title: Rencontres Marrakech + OFF Arles 2026 Open Call
calls.description: 6th edition open call for the Rencontres de la Photographie Marrakech and Festival OFF Arles 2026. Theme: 1826–2026: Two Centuries of Light, inviting work that explores light as origin, medium, language, and possibility — intimate or political, abstract or documentary, conceptual or experimental. 20 winners exhibit five photographs each at Galerie Triptyque in Arles during the opening week of Les Rencontres d'Arles (July 3–20, 2026), present a video at the Rencontres de la Photographie de Marrakech festival (October 7–10, 2026), and receive a dedicated online publication on the festival's official platform. 30 additional finalists also participate in the Marrakech video presentation and online publication.
calls.summary: 20 winners exhibit at Galerie Triptyque in Arles during Rencontres week + video presentation at Marrakech festival.

calls.title: Guest Room: Auronda Scalera & Alfredo Cramerotti
calls.description: Open call curated by Auronda Scalera (Artistic Director, curator, and lecturer; curator of "Ding Yi: Cosmotechnique" at Fondazione Querini Stampalia for Venice Art Biennale 2026) and Dr. Alfredo Cramerotti (Director, Media Majlis Museum at Northwestern University Qatar; President of IKT) exploring the theme "Shifting Thresholds." Invites photographic and image-based works engaging with displacement as a lived experience and aesthetic condition — migration, body transformation, exile, environmental change, and more subtle forms like digital mediation and algorithmic vision. Open to everyone. Selected work featured on Der Greif's platform with a face-to-face feedback session from the curators. Works must not have been previously selected by past Der Greif Guest Curators.
calls.summary: Theme: "Shifting Thresholds" — displacement, migration, body, exile, ecological change, digital mediation, algorithmic vision.
jury: Auronda Scalera, Artistic Director, curator, and lecturer
Alfredo Cramerotti, Director, Media Majlis Museum at Northwestern University Qatar

calls.title: Headlands Center for the Arts AIR 2027
calls.description: Fully sponsored 4–10 week Artist in Residence program at Headlands Center for the Arts in Sausalito, California. Approximately 60 artists selected each year, including local, national, and international applicants at all career stages. Photography is explicitly listed as an eligible discipline alongside drawing, painting, sculpture, film, video, new media, installation, writing, dance, music, interdisciplinary, social practice, arts professions, and architecture. Residency includes private studio space, chef-prepared meals, on-site housing, travel support, and a living expenses stipend. Application portal opens April 1, 2026; early bird fee ($35) closes May 4, 2026; regular fee ($45) thereafter. All applicants notified by December 11, 2026.
calls.summary: Fully sponsored 4–10 week residency in Sausalito, CA. Studio, meals, housing, travel covered. Photography eligible; ~60 artists/year.
prose: Headlands Center for the Arts is a multidisciplinary residency program housed at 944 Fort Barry, Sausalito, California — within the Marin Headlands, a National Park Service property a few miles north of the Golden Gate Bridge. The 2027 Artist in Residence program is fully sponsored: residents receive studio space, on-site housing, chef-prepared meals, travel support, and a living-expenses stipend.

Approximately 50 to 60 artists are selected each year. Residencies range from four to ten weeks. The program is unusually broad in its disciplinary scope, with photography explicitly named alongside drawing, painting, sculpture, film, video, new media, installation, fiction and nonfiction writing, poetry, dance, music, interdisciplinary practice, social practice, arts professions, and architecture.
Eligibility is open globally to artists at all career stages — emerging through established. Local Bay Area, U.S. national, and international applicants are all welcomed.

The application portal opens April 1, 2026 and closes June 1, 2026. Application fees are tiered: $35 early bird (through May 4), $45 regular thereafter. Submissions go through SlideRoom and require up to 12 images of work. All applicants are notified of selection decisions by December 11, 2026.

calls.title: Eliza Moore Fellowship for Artistic Excellence 2027
calls.description: Annual fellowship for one outstanding early-career artist developing new works that address plants, gardens, or landscapes in the broad sense. Open to visual artists (including photographers), literary artists, dancers, and musicians. Award includes a $10,000 individual grant and a required 2–5 week residency at the Oak Spring Garden Foundation's 700-acre estate in Upperville, Virginia, with access to staff, the rare book library (over 19,000 botanical art objects), and the working landscape. Eligible applicants must be early-career artists with some recognition through exhibitions, commissions, performances, grants, residencies, or publications, and not enrolled in an undergraduate program. Established artists with extensive solo exhibitions or published books are ineligible. 2027 residency start dates: March 1, April 25, May 24, July 12, August 29, or October 4. Application portal opens February 14, 2026.
calls.summary: $10,000 grant + 2–5 week residency at Oak Spring Garden Foundation in Virginia. For early-career artists working with plants or landscapes.

calls.title: Fondation Grantham Residency for Artists in Visual Arts 2027
calls.description: Four-week residency with grant for established visual artists at Fondation Grantham, in the wooded francophone municipality of Saint-Edmond-de-Grantham, approximately 100 km east of Montreal. The Foundation supports projects whose subject matter, materials, or approach engage the aesthetic, social, and global implications of current environmental issues. Photography is explicitly included as an eligible practice alongside installation, sculpture, painting, graphic art, performance, and sound, digital, and media arts. Phase 1 grant of CAD $5,000 (residency, materials, and production); Phase 2 of up to CAD $5,000 to support continued project development. Travel allowance up to CAD $1,000 for artists residing 500+ km away. Open to artists from Quebec, elsewhere in Canada, or abroad with at least five years of professional practice; duos welcome. 2027 residency takes place in January, February, July, or August. Winners announced September 12, 2026.
calls.summary: 4-week residency in Quebec for established artists at the intersection of visual arts and environmental issues. CAD $5,000–$10,000 grant.

calls.title: BLM Canyon Country District Artist in Residence 2026
calls.description: Two- to four-week residency hosted by the BLM Canyon Country District in the Moab Field Office, Utah. Open to visual artists working in any medium suitable for digital reproduction, including photography, painting, printmaking, sculpture, and video. Selected artist creates work that represents the Canyon Country District; the BLM may suggest specific areas or themes within field office boundaries. Includes a $125/week stipend funded by the Canyonlands Natural History Association, access to a BLM campsite for the duration of the residency, and use of the Moab Field Office for drinking water and showers. Residency takes place between September 11 and October 31, 2026 (artist chooses dates and length). Selection panel includes BLM and Canyonlands Natural History Association staff who evaluate portfolio, resume, community engagement proposal, and application responses. Notifications by July 15, 2026.
calls.summary: 2–4 week residency in Moab, UT, hosted by the BLM. Photography eligible. Free; $125/week stipend + campsite.
prose: The Bureau of Land Management's Canyon Country District Artist in Residence program is a public-lands residency hosted at the Moab Field Office in Utah — the gateway to public lands surrounding Arches National Park, Canyonlands, and the wider Colorado Plateau red rock country. The residency is funded in partnership with the Canyonlands Natural History Association.

Residencies run between September 11 and October 31, 2026, with the selected artist choosing a 2- to 4-week window within that range. The setup is unusually rugged: residents stay at a BLM campsite for the duration of the residency and use the Moab Field Office for drinking water and showers. There is no formal indoor housing or studio.

Stipend is $125 per week, paid by the Canyonlands Natural History Association. Eligibility is open to visual artists working in any medium suitable for digital reproduction — photography, painting, printmaking, sculpture, video. The selected artist makes work that represents the Canyon Country District; the BLM may suggest specific areas or themes within the field office boundaries.

The selection panel includes BLM and Canyonlands Natural History Association staff, who evaluate portfolio, résumé, community engagement proposal, and application responses. There is no application fee. The 2026 deadline is June 1; selections announced by July 15.

calls.title: Sonntag Grant 2026 Photobook Open Call
calls.description: Photobook open call from the Berlin-based Sonntag Grant for Photography in collaboration with Replika Publishing. Reserved for FLINTA artists (female, lesbian, inter, non-binary, trans, agender), 18+, of any nationality or location. Seeks projects that challenge the boundaries of the book as form, with emphasis on conceptual depth, material inquiry, and artistic dialogue. All forms of photographic work accepted; projects must be completed or at an advanced stage suitable for photobook production. AI-generated images are not accepted. One artist is selected to work directly with Replika Publishing to produce a new photobook with a print run of at least 350 copies (50 going to the artist). Submissions accepted globally from April 1 through midnight (Berlin/CET) on May 31, 2026.
calls.summary: Berlin photobook open call for FLINTA artists, in collaboration with Replika Publishing. Winner gets photobook with 350+ print run.

calls.title: Ucross Spring 2027 Residency
calls.description: Two- to six-week residency at the Ucross Foundation's 20,000-acre working ranch in northeastern Wyoming. Spring Session 2027 runs February through early June. Open to visual artists, writers, composers, choreographers, interdisciplinary artists, performance artists, and collaborative teams; both established and emerging artists encouraged, international applicants welcome. Approximately 115 residents per year; up to 10 in residence at any time. Includes living accommodations, all meals (chef-prepared lunch and dinner Monday–Friday, plus weekend provisions), dedicated work space, weekly housekeeping, linens and towels, and wireless internet. No stipend; residents provide their own materials and arrange travel to Sheridan, WY. Application opens May 1, 2026; no fee waivers available.
calls.summary: 2–6 week residency on a 20,000-acre Wyoming ranch. Photography eligible. Lodging + meals + work space; international applicants welcome.
prose: The Ucross Foundation runs an artist residency on a 20,000-acre working ranch in northeastern Wyoming. The program was founded in 1981 with the first residency in 1983, and now hosts approximately 115 residents annually across two sessions: Fall (August through early December) and Spring (February through early June). Residencies run between two and six weeks; up to ten artists are in residence at any time, typically split as four writers, four visual artists, and two composers.

There is no residency fee. Residents receive private living accommodations, dedicated work space, all weekday meals prepared by the in-house chef (with self-catering provisions for weekends and breakfasts), weekly housekeeping, linens, and wireless internet. There is no stipend — artists provide their own materials and arrange their own travel to Sheridan, Wyoming, the nearest airport.

Eligibility is open globally to visual artists, writers, composers, choreographers, interdisciplinary and performance artists, and collaborative teams, at both established and emerging career stages. Applicants must demonstrate professional standing, with both U.S. and international applicants welcome.

The application fee is $40, with no waivers available. Spring 2027 applications are accepted through Submittable from May 1 through July 15, 2026; Fall applications open later in the year (November 1 through January 15). Decisions are typically released within several months of each deadline.

calls.title: SCAN Full Contact 2026
calls.description: First edition of Full Contact, a professional photography meeting organised by SCAN, the international photography festival hosted by Tarragona City Council. Twelve photographers are selected for a portfolio-review and networking day at Teatret del Port in El Serrallo (Tarragona) on 17 October 2026, with accommodation, meals, and curatorial conversations covered. One project is selected as the Full Contact Award winner and receives a solo exhibition during SCAN's 2027 official programme along with a €900 fee (incl. tax) for exhibition and communication rights. Open to photographers of legal age residing in any country of the European Union or the United Kingdom.
calls.summary: Free SCAN Tarragona portfolio-review meeting for 12 EU/UK photographers. Winner gets a 2027 solo show + €900.
jury: Arola Valls Bofill, Independent Curator & Researcher

calls.title: Camera Work: Shadow and Light 2026
calls.description: Juried photography exhibition at Black Box Gallery in Portland, Oregon, exploring the dialogue between shadow and light. Both black-and-white and color work welcome — formal, conceptual, expressive, minimal, intricate, literal, or abstract approaches all considered. Juried by Todd Johnson, gallery founder/director, with an MFA in Photography from the San Francisco Art Institute and 25 years in arts education and administration. 26 photographs selected for the physical exhibition (June 1–25, 2026); 50 additional images included in the online gallery; all 76 published in a purchasable catalog. Black Box provides free archival printing, matting, and framing for accepted work. The gallery retains 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers; submission via PayPal payment + email with up to 5 JPEGs.
calls.summary: Portland gallery juried photography show exploring shadow and light. Free printing, matting, and framing for the 26 accepted works.
jury: Todd Johnson, Founder/Director, Black Box Gallery

calls.title: Rotlicht Festival 2026 — Anthropocene: Hybrid Realities
calls.description: International open call from the Rotlicht Festival for Analog Photography in Vienna. Theme: Anthropocene: Hybrid Realities — submissions engaging with the tensions of the human-shaped epoch through experimental, critical, and process-oriented approaches in analog and hybrid photography. Purely digital work is excluded; at least one analog process must be involved. Open to anyone aged 16+ not affiliated with the festival. Photos must be from the last 5 years (2021–2026). Submit a single series or project (max 15 images). 20 winners are exhibited at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, each receiving a €250 honorarium, €150 travel allowance, festival pass, and inclusion in the official catalogue. The Grand Prix winner receives an additional solo exhibition, €250, and festival cover feature. Winners announced beginning of September 2026.
calls.summary: Open call for analog photography festival in Vienna. Theme: Anthropocene. 20 winners exhibited; €250 honorarium + €150 travel.
jury: Hanin Hannouch, Curator for Analog and Digital Media, Weltmuseum Wien (Chief Juror)
Miriam Marzura, Curator, Leica Galerie Wien
Miha Colner, Curator, Galerija Božidar Jakac
Sabina Salamon, Curator, Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Rijeka
Florence Drouhet, Artistic Director, Photo Festival LaGacilly-Baden
prose: The Rotlicht Festival is an Austrian festival dedicated to analog photography, held in Vienna at the Atelierhaus der Akademie der bildenden Künste — an exhibition space of more than 1,300 square meters at the Academy of Fine Arts. The festival is organized by the Zigutamve Association.

The 2026 theme is "Anthropocene: Hybrid Realities," exploring tensions between human intervention and nature, control and vulnerability, construction and decay. Submitted work must be made within the previous five years (2021–2026) and must include at least one decisive analog process. Purely digital work is excluded; AI-generated and AI-enhanced images are not accepted.

Twenty winning projects are selected from the open call. Each winner receives an exhibition slot at the main venue, two copies of the official catalogue, €250 prize money, a €150 travel allowance, a festival pass, and free registration for Photodays Rovinj 2027. The Grand Prix winner additionally receives a solo exhibition at the Photo Cluster Gallery, an additional €250, the cover artwork credit on 2026 festival materials, and a free hotel stay at partner hotel Korotan.

The 2026 jury is led by Chief Juror Hanin Hannouch (Curator for Analog and Digital Media at Weltmuseum Wien) and includes Miriam Marzura (Leica Galerie Wien), Miha Colner (Galerija Božidar Jakac), Wiktoria Michałkiewicz (REZO agency), Sabina Salamon (Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Rijeka), artist Laura Ettel, and Florence Drouhet (Photo Festival LaGacilly-Baden). Entry fee is €20 per project. The deadline is June 30, 2026; winners announced early September.

calls.title: AAP Magazine #58 Black & White
calls.description: Black & white theme issue of AAP Magazine. Open to photographers 18+; submit a cohesive series of at least 3 images (up to 40). 25 winners published in AAP Magazine Volume 58 with online gallery placement and a free copy. Cash prizes: $500 (1st), $300 (2nd), $200 (3rd). Early-bird fee ($30 for first 3 images, $5 each additional) ends May 15, 2026; regular fee $35 thereafter. Winners announced approximately July 15, 2026.
calls.summary: B&W themed issue of AAP Magazine. $1,000 cash + publication. Up to 40 images, min 3 as a cohesive series.
jury: Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, Founder & Editor, All About Photo
prose: AAP Magazine is the print publication of All About Photo, the photography platform run by Sandrine Hermand-Grisel. Each issue is themed and curated from open-call submissions, with the magazine functioning as both contest and editorial outlet. Issue #58 is themed "Black & White" — open to all interpretations of monochrome photography across photojournalism, street, documentary, portrait, landscape, wildlife, architecture, fashion, and fine art.

Twenty-five winners are published in the printed AAP Magazine Vol. 58 alongside the online Winners Gallery on the All About Photo platform. Each published photographer receives one complimentary copy of the magazine and is featured across All About Photo's social channels.
Cash awards total $1,000: $500 first place, $300 second, $200 third. Twenty-two additional finalists (4th through 25th) are recognized but do not receive cash.

Submissions require a minimum of 3 images forming a cohesive body of work or unified series connected by subject, style, or concept; up to 40 images may be submitted per applicant. Entry fees follow a tiered structure: early bird (through May 15) is $30 for the first 3 images and $5 each additional; regular fee (after May 15) is $35 for the first 3 and $5 each additional. The 2026 deadline is June 2; winners announced approximately July 15. AI-generated images are not accepted; eligibility is open to professional and amateur photographers aged 18 or over.

calls.title: Prairie Ronde Artist Residency — Fall 2026
calls.description: Five- to six-week residency at The Mill in Vicksburg, Michigan — a 416,000-square-foot former paper mill on 80 acres of land. Fall session runs September 15 to December 20, 2026. Open to artists across all media including photography; the program does not limit residency to any specific medium and seeks artists who can engage directly with The Mill and its surrounding rural property. Two to four residents per session. Includes a $2,000 stipend on completion, $500 travel grant, private housing in a historic village home, gallery exhibition in downtown Vicksburg, video documentation, and brewery membership. Process-based residency for independently driven artists; one piece produced during the residency is donated to the permanent collection. International applicants are temporarily not being considered (as of April 2025). Selections announced July 30.
calls.summary: 5–6 week residency at a historic paper mill in Vicksburg, MI. All media incl. photography. $2,000 + travel + housing + gallery show.
prose: Prairie Ronde Artist Residency is hosted at The Mill at Vicksburg — a 416,000-square-foot former paper mill on 80 acres in Vicksburg, Michigan (101 S. Main, Suite 200). The Fall 2026 session runs five to six weeks between September 15 and December 20, with two to four residents in residence at any time.

Each resident receives a $2,000 stipend (paid on completion), a $500 travel grant, private housing in a historic village home, and a gallery exhibition in downtown Vicksburg at the end of the residency. The program also provides video documentation of the residency and a complimentary membership to the local brewery. One completed work made during the residency is donated to the residency's permanent collection.

The residency is process-based and accepts artists across all media, including photography. Writers are accepted only if they propose new work specifically related to The Mill and Vicksburg. Children of residents are welcome with an accompanying caregiver (additional costs are the artist's responsibility); pets are considered case-by-case.

Eligibility is currently restricted to U.S.-based artists — international applicants are temporarily not being considered as of April 2025. The application fee is $25. Selection is by a six-person panel comprising three former residents, one community member, and the Residency Director and Coordinator. The Fall 2026 deadline is June 15, with selections announced July 30.

calls.title: Source Graduate Photography Online 2026 — BA
calls.description: Annual graduate showcase from Source, Belfast-based quarterly photography magazine, running since 2007. Open to photographers graduating from a BA in 2026 in Ireland or the UK. Submit up to 8 images with an artist statement and website link. Selected work featured on the Graduate Photography Online platform and in a printed supplement; participants receive a 1-year digital subscription to Source (worth £26.99). MA/MFA submissions have a separate later deadline (August 7, 2026).
calls.summary: BA graduate showcase from Source magazine for UK/Ireland 2026 grads. 8 images. Featured online + in printed supplement.
jury: Peggy Sue Amison, Artistic Director, East Wing
Amara Eno, Photo Editor, Financial Times HTSI

calls.title: Source Graduate Photography Online 2026 — MA/MFA
calls.description: Annual graduate showcase from Source, Belfast-based quarterly photography magazine, running since 2007. Open to photographers graduating from an MA or MFA in 2026 in Ireland or the UK. Submit up to 8 images with an artist statement and website link. Selected work featured on the Graduate Photography Online platform and in a printed supplement; participants receive a 1-year digital subscription to Source (worth £26.99). BA submissions have an earlier deadline (May 11, 2026).
calls.summary: MA/MFA graduate showcase from Source magazine for UK/Ireland 2026 grads. 8 images. Featured online + in printed supplement.
jury: Pauline Vermare, Curator of Photography, Brooklyn Museum
Paul McAree, Curator/Director, Lismore Castle Arts
Kimberly Hoang, Picture Editor, British Red Cross
prose: Source Photographic Review is a Belfast-based quarterly photography magazine, with the Graduate Photography Online platform launched in 2007 as its annual showcase for new graduates. The MA/MFA edition is open to photographers who graduated from a Master's-level program in 2026 from a course based in the United Kingdom or the Republic of Ireland.

Each accepted submission gets an individual web page on the Source platform featuring up to eight images, an artist statement, and a website link — an editorial showcase rather than a one-off feature, with pages remaining online indefinitely as part of the magazine's archive. Selected work also appears in a printed supplement included with an issue of Source.

The entry fee is £33 for UK courses or €38 for Republic of Ireland courses, and includes a complimentary one-year digital subscription to Source magazine (worth £26.99). The submission deadline is August 7, 2026.

The 2026 MA/MFA jury comprises Pauline Vermare, Curator of Photography at the Brooklyn Museum; Paul McAree, Curator and Director of Lismore Castle Arts; and Kimberly Hoang, Picture Editor at the British Red Cross. (BA submissions follow a separate, earlier track with a May 11 deadline.)

calls.title: Encontros da Imagem Photobook Award 2026
calls.description: Photobook award from the 36th edition of Encontros da Imagem festival in Braga, Portugal. Two categories: Best Published Award and Best Dummy Award, each with €1,000 cash prize. Up to two honorable mentions per category. All submitted books shown in a group exhibition during the festival, September 18 – November 1, 2026. Theme: Territory and Identity. Open to artists, photographers and publishers worldwide aged 18+, individually or collectively. Maximum 3 photobooks per applicant per category (each counted as separate entry). Physical books must arrive in Braga by 15 July 2026.
calls.summary: Two photobook awards (Best Published and Best Dummy) at 36th Encontros da Imagem. €1,000 each + group exhibition. Theme: Territory and Identity.

calls.title: Open Panoràmic 2026 — Burning with Desire
calls.description: Open call from Festival Panoràmic (10th anniversary edition) in Granollers, Barcelona and Terrassa. Theme Burning with Desire takes the bicentennial of photography as its starting point, positioning photography and cinema as practices of desire — for memory, justice, beauty, permanence. Three categories: still image (series or single works), audiovisual essay (5-18 min .mov/.mp4), and installation/other formats. Selected projects included in the festival's exhibition programme, October 15 – December 27, 2026. Open to artists and collectives of any nationality, 18+, individually or collectively. Projects must be created between 2022 and 2026. One project per category maximum.
calls.summary: Free open call from Festival Panoràmic (10th anniv.). 3 categories: still image, audiovisual essay, installation. Theme: Burning with Desire.

calls.title: Alt+1000 9th Edition Open Call — Emerging Scene
calls.description: 9th edition open call from the Alt+1000 outdoor photography festival in La Vue-des-Alpes, canton de Neuchâtel. Theme explores the notion of jeu (play) in connection with landscape — including in-game photography, screen capture, photomontage, and the visual exploration of digital environments and playscapes. Festival runs September 18 to October 10, 2027. Four emerging photographers are selected, each receiving a CHF 800 honorarium with all production, installation, and promotion covered by Alt+1000. Open to photographers and artists using photography who are studying at a Swiss art school or in early career (maximum 5 years after graduating) in Switzerland. All photographic genres and techniques welcome — artistic, conceptual, or documentary. Capacity to adapt to outdoor exhibition is a primary evaluation criterion; proposals requiring electrical power are not accepted. Submission via email as a single .zip with the subject line APPEL À PROJET ALT+1000 2027. Working languages: French and English.
calls.summary: Outdoor photography festival in the Swiss Alps. 4 emerging Swiss photographers selected. CHF 800 + production. Theme: play and landscape.

calls.title: PhEST Pop-Up Open Call 2026 — What If?
calls.description: Sixth international contest from PhEST – See Beyond the Sea, the international photography and contemporary art festival in Monopoli, Italy. Theme: WHAT IF? — exploring our relationship with the present and imagining possible futures through visual art. Two categories: SERIES (10–20 fixed images, illustrations) and SINGLES (video, animation, and this year also short films). Six winning projects selected: an exhibition at PhEST 2026 for the best international project, an exhibition for the best Puglia-based artist, an exhibition of the best international short film (UniBa Award), a Fujifilm X-T5 mirrorless camera kit with 16-80mm lens (€2,550 value, offered by Fujifilm Italia), publication on the PhMuseum platform with a free Annual copy, publication on LensCulture, and projection of works during the opening nights of PhEST 2026. Festival runs August 7 – November 1, 2026 in Monopoli, Italy. Submissions via LensCulture (free account required); 200-word English description, short bio, 2000-pixel JPGs.
calls.summary: PhEST Monopoli's free international competition. Theme: What If? Prizes include exhibition, Fujifilm X-T5, PhMuseum and LensCulture publications.
jury: Arianna Rinaldo, Curator and Photo Editor

calls.title: Yaddo Residency — Summer 2026 Cycle
calls.description: Two-week to two-month residency at Yaddo's 400-acre estate in Saratoga Springs, NY, founded in 1900. Open to professional and emerging artists across literature, visual art (painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking, photography, mixed media, installation), music composition, performance, and film & video. Residents receive room, board, and a private studio; modest access grants available to offset travel. The Summer cycle covers residencies November 2026 through June 2027. Portal opens June 1; application fee waivable in cases of financial hardship. Yaddo encourages applications from artists from backgrounds underrepresented in arts and culture.
calls.summary: 2-week to 2-month residency in Saratoga Springs, NY. Photography eligible. Founded 1900. Encourages underrepresented backgrounds.
prose: Yaddo is an artist residency on a 400-acre estate in Saratoga Springs, New York, founded in 1900 — one of the oldest residency programs in the United States. The program runs continuously across the year, with residencies ranging from two weeks to two months. The Summer 2026 application cycle covers residency placements between November 2026 and June 2027.

Residents receive a private bedroom, individual studio or workspace, three meals daily (communal dinners, plus breakfast and a packed lunch), weekly housekeeping with linens and towels, and access to the estate's grounds. Modest access grants are available to offset travel costs. There are no publication, exhibition, or performance requirements imposed on residents.

Eligibility spans five disciplines: literature, visual art (painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking, photography, mixed media, installation), music composition, performance, and film & video. Applicants must be at the professional level or emerging artists demonstrating professional promise; degree-seeking students at the time of application are not eligible. Artists may apply once every other calendar year.

International applicants are welcome but must have working English; Yaddo provides no visa or interpreter assistance. The application fee is $35 (waivable for financial hardship). The Summer 2026 deadline is July 1, with results in early October. Applications go through SlideRoom; initial review is anonymous, and selection is by independent peer-review Admissions Committees judging solely on the quality of the work.

calls.title: CIAR Fall Artists' Residency 2026
calls.description: Eight-day residency on Cuttyhunk Island off the Massachusetts coast, September 9–16, 2026. Open to visual artists at all career stages working across drawing, painting, collage, small sculpture, photography, and video. Artists must have a portable studio practice suitable for the island setting. Programming includes communal meals prepared by resident chefs, complimentary golf carts to roam the island, and conversations with visiting artists Claudia Keep and Randall Exon. Housing at the historic Avalon Inn (linens and towels provided); base cost $1,950 (triple) to $3,600 (single) plus ferry travel. Multiple full and partial fellowships available — the new Environmental Artist Fellowship, the Open Merit Fellowship, the Paul Cuffe Fellowship for an artist of color, the Wellspring Fellowship for parent artists, and work-study options — covering up to the full residency cost.
calls.summary: 8-day visual arts residency on Cuttyhunk Island, MA. Photography accepted. Fellowships cover full cost for artists of color, parent artists, and others.

calls.title: Urban 2026
calls.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of urban environments. Open to street photography that captures the people inhabiting these spaces, cityscapes, architecture, and beyond. Selected work displayed in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow (4–30 September 2026), with work also appearing in an online gallery and exhibition catalogue. All participants put forward for Photographer of the Month consideration. Images printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames; photographers retain all copyright. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit 1–8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on shortest side) via free file-transfer to the gallery email.
calls.summary: Urban-themed photography exhibition — street, cityscape, architecture. Glasgow gallery exhibition Sep 2026, online gallery, catalogue.

calls.title: Pink 2026
calls.description: International photography exhibition exploring the colour pink across any genre — nature, urban settings, portraits, still life, or beyond. Selected work displayed in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow (4–30 September 2026), with work also appearing in an online gallery and exhibition catalogue. All participants put forward for Photographer of the Month consideration. Images printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames; photographers retain all copyright. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit 1–8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on shortest side) via free file-transfer to the gallery email.
calls.summary: Photography exhibition exploring the colour pink across any genre. Glasgow gallery exhibition Sep 2026, online gallery, catalogue.

calls.title: Cape Town Photo Festival 2026 Open Call — TRUTH
calls.description: Open call for the inaugural Cape Town Photo Festival, running 2–26 September 2026. Theme: TRUTH — exploring how truth is constructed, mediated, and challenged through photography, with focus on personal truth, social truth, and technical truth. Two categories: Solo Exhibition (6–8 images, with 300-word statement and 150-word bio) and Group Exhibition (up to 4 images, 150-word bio, optional 150-word statement). A curatorial panel selects work based on conceptual strength, relevance to the theme, and technical and visual quality. Selected artists exhibit at the festival in Cape Town and may be considered for the festival's photography auction, talks, and workshops. Open to local and international photographers of all career levels; students encouraged. Notification by 25 May 2026.
calls.summary: Cape Town Photo Festival 2026 open call. Theme: TRUTH. Solo or group exhibition at Sep 2026 festival. Students discounted.

calls.title: PhotoArtDoc 2026 Open Call — State of Transition
calls.description: Annual photography competition from PhotoArtDoc, a festival at the intersection of documentary and art organised by the Belarusian Independent Photographic Association (founded 2023). Theme: TRANSFORMATION — State of Transition, exploring how individuals navigate continuous change and uncertainty as a fundamental condition. Open to photographers and artists working with photography worldwide. Image transformation techniques such as montage, collage, and multiple exposure are permitted; methods must be described. 1st place wins exhibition in Vilnius, Lithuania, plus zine publication and online gallery feature. 2nd and 3rd places featured in the PhotoArtDoc 2026 zine and online gallery. Projects must have been created or completed between 2024 and 2026; maximum two projects per author.
calls.summary: Photography festival at the intersection of documentary and art. Theme: TRANSFORMATION. Free entry, Vilnius exhibition + zine.
jury: Michael Grieve, Photographer & Founder, Werkstatt: / ArtFotoMode
Kateryna Radchenko, Curator & Founder, Odesa Photo Days

calls.title: Photometria Awards 2026 — Coming of Age
calls.description: Open call for the 18th Photometria International Photography Festival in Ioannina, Greece. Theme: Coming of Age (18+) — exploring the layered and evolving condition of growing up, moments of rupture, and the tension between freedom and responsibility. Sole judge: Alec Soth (Magnum, Guggenheim Fellow). 1st prize: Nikon Z30 Kit with NIKKOR Z DX 12-28mm lens. 2nd and 3rd: signed photo album by Alec Soth. One top-three winner receives a solo exhibition at the next festival. Top 25 photos exhibited in Ioannina during the 18th edition (Sep–Nov 2026) and travel to other cities in Greece. AI-generated images not accepted. Entry: free for 1 photo, €5 for 3 photos.
calls.summary: 18th Photometria Festival open call. Theme: Coming of Age. Sole judge Alec Soth. Nikon Z30 + solo exhibition for top three.

calls.title: 10th Singapore International Photography Festival 2026 Open Call
calls.description: 10th biennial SIPF Open Call for image-makers and photographers worldwide, with no theme. Two categories: Portfolio (cohesive body of work in images and/or video) and Photobook (both published and dummy books, which must be production-ready in physical form). Shortlisted submissions presented in the SIPF Open Call Showcase at the 10th biennale edition of SIPF in Singapore, mid-October to end-November 2026. Three SGD $2,000 cash prizes awarded: Best Portfolio, Best Published Photobook, Best Dummy Photobook. Shortlisted artists receive exposure to SIPF's network, discounted portfolio reviews and masterclasses, complimentary festival admission, and opportunities to participate in artist tours, talks, and workshops. Organised by DECK Photography Art Centre, a registered Charity in Singapore supported by the National Arts Council. Submission fee: USD $30 for Photobook, USD $45 for Portfolio.
calls.summary: 10th biennial SIPF Open Call. Portfolio + photobook categories. 3× SGD $2,000 prizes. Showcase in Singapore Oct–Nov 2026.

calls.title: Filter Space 2026/27 Call for Exhibition Proposals
calls.description: Annual open call for exhibition proposals at Filter Space, Filter Photo's Chicago gallery. Selected artists, curators, and collectives receive a 4–6 week exhibition in 2027–2028, at least one reception, an event hosting opportunity (artist talk, panel, or workshop), printed marketing materials and press releases, and a W.A.G.E. Standards-based stipend ($1,250 for solo shows; $625/artist for two-person; $315/artist for groups of 3–5). Proposals should relate to photography, photographic materials, or lens-based artwork, including moving-image pieces, installations, and performances connected to photography. Submit an artist or curatorial statement (500 words max), bio and CV for all participants, 10–12 sample images (JPEG, 1000 px longest side), and links to video/multimedia (max 5 minutes). Review in July 2026; announcement in August 2026.
calls.summary: Filter Space Chicago 4–6 week exhibition for artists, curators, and collectives. W.A.G.E. stipend. Lens-based work.
jury: Emilia Mickevicius, Assistant Curator of Photography, Center for Creative Photography and Phoenix Art Museum
Kristin Taylor, Curator of Academic Programs and Collections, Museum of Contemporary Photography
Yechen Zhao, Assistant Curator of Photography and Media, Art Institute of Chicago
prose: Filter Photo runs Filter Space, a photography-focused exhibition space at 1821 W Hubbard Street, Suite 207 in Chicago. The 2026/27 Call for Exhibition Proposals seeks photography, photographic materials, and lens-based artwork — including moving-image work, installations, and performances related to photography — from individual artists, curators, and collectives, for solo or group projects.

Selected proposals receive a four- to six-week exhibition slot in 2027–2028 with at least one opening reception, plus the opportunity to host an artist talk, panel, or workshop during the run. Filter Photo provides marketing materials and press support.

Stipends are paid based on W.A.G.E. (Working Artists and the Greater Economy) standards, which sets a baseline minimum-fee schedule for exhibiting artists — for example, $1,250 for a solo exhibition at this venue size. The W.A.G.E. baseline distinguishes Filter Photo from venues that exhibit work without paying artists.

Selection is by Filter Photo staff plus an external Exhibition Advisory Committee. The 2026 advisory panel comprises Luciano Medrano (Director, PATRON Gallery), Emilia Mickevicius (Center for Creative Photography / Phoenix Art Museum), Kristin Taylor (Museum of Contemporary Photography), and Yechen Zhao (Art Institute of Chicago). Submissions go through Submittable; the deadline is June 17, 2026, with results announced August 2026.

calls.title: Studio Museum in Harlem Artist-in-Residence 2026–2027
calls.description: Eleven-month residency (November 2, 2026 – October 3, 2027) for three artists of African and Afro-Latinx descent working in any media, including photography. Residents receive a $50,000 stipend paid biweekly, 24-hour access to a private studio and shared spaces within the museum, institutional guidance, professional development, research support, and regular studio visits with the curatorial team. Culminating exhibition and publication at Studio Museum June–September 2027. Open to artists 18+ at all career stages (geared toward emerging practitioners). Local, national, and international artists eligible. Submit CV, 5–10 images or videos of work, and artist statement. Letters of recommendation encouraged but not required.
calls.summary: 11-month Harlem residency for artists of African and Afro-Latinx descent. $50K stipend, private studio, culminating exhibition.

calls.title: Baxter St 2026–2027 Guest Curatorial Open Call
calls.description: Annual open call for emerging independent curators and artist-curators to propose exhibitions at Baxter St at the Camera Club of New York. Three guest-curated shows selected per year for 2026–2027 season. Projects should contribute to contemporary lens-based arts dialogue and demonstrate innovative curatorial approaches, with preference for artists not yet represented by New York galleries. Maximum two artists per proposal; curator cannot be an exhibiting artist. Curator fee plus artist fees and full production budget provided. Curators must be located in the tri-state area (NY, NJ, CT) at the time of exhibition. Cannot have exhibited at Baxter St in the previous two years. Submit overview, 300-word concept statement, up to 8 images and up to 2 videos (max 3 min each).
calls.prize: Curator and artist fees + production budget
calls.summary: Three guest-curated shows at Baxter St NYC. Emerging curators, tri-state area. Curator and artist fees plus production budget.

calls.title: Fresh Eyes x Hungry Eye vol. 2
calls.description: Second Fresh Eyes x Hungry Eye collaboration, an international open call for emerging photographers powered by Amsterdam-based GUP Magazine. Selected artists receive minimum 4 pages in a softcover publication with international distribution to galleries, curators, agencies, and media, plus promotion through GUP and Fresh Eyes channels. One image from each selected artist is displayed in a group exhibition at Hungry Eye Fair, Amsterdam (September 2026), with two free entry tickets. Selected photographers also receive three copies of the publication and portfolio review opportunities. Three 'Exceptional Talent Award' winners receive free publication inclusion. Jury of GUP editors, gallerists and photographers. Free to apply; selected participants pay €350 (excluding VAT and shipping). Open worldwide to emerging photographers.
calls.prize: Publication + exhibition at Hungry Eye Fair
calls.summary: Softcover publication + group exhibition at Hungry Eye Fair Amsterdam. Emerging photographers worldwide. Jury by GUP editors.

calls.title: Copenhagen Photo Festival 2026 Open Exhibition
calls.description: Annual open exhibition at Copenhagen Photo Festival 2026 on the theme 'Forestil dig...?' (Imagine if...?). 50 selected works printed, framed, and exhibited at the Royal Theatre (Det Kongelige Teater) from 11–17 June 2026. Non-selected submissions shown digitally during the festival (11–21 June 2026). Submit one square (1:1) JPG at 300 dpi, printable at 30×30 cm. Prizes: 4,000 DKK / 2,000 DKK / 1,000 DKK CEWE printing vouchers. Selected photographers get free festival access and reception invitation. Open internationally to photographers 18+.
calls.summary: Open exhibition at Copenhagen Photo Festival — 50 works printed and shown at the Royal Theatre. Theme: Imagine if...?

calls.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Local Landscapes
calls.description: Submit up to 5 local landscape images with captions for publication in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK), issue OP 329. Winner receives Sunski Ferrata sunglasses (RRP £149.95). JPG at 300ppi.
calls.summary: Submit local landscape images for Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). Winner receives Sunski sunglasses.

calls.title: Print Swap Inaugural Exhibition
calls.description: Inaugural open call from Print Swap, a new iOS app founded by London photographer Sam Faulkner for direct print-for-print exchanges between photographers. 50 selected images are printed and exhibited at The Print Space in London, opening May 7, 2026. Selected photographers receive permanent Founding Artists status in the app. All printing and exhibition costs are covered. Submissions made via the Print Swap iOS app. Open to photographers worldwide.
calls.summary: Inaugural exhibition at The Print Space London via new print-exchange iOS app. 50 artists selected, prints fully produced and shown.

calls.title: From Your Archive
calls.description: Open call juried by Laurie Freitag, founder of L.A. Photo Curator, inviting photographers to submit work from their existing archives — images that feel clear, resolved, and hold over time, across all photographic styles. First place receives a solo online exhibition, a featured Q&A article, and homepage feature for one month. All selected photographers appear in a group online exhibition with artist statement and bio, with consideration for Top 40 Images of the Year and Photographer of the Year. 5% of entry fees donated to No Kid Hungry; additional 5% to the winner's chosen charity. AI-generated work not accepted. Submit 3 or 6 images (not 4 or 5). Limited fee waivers available on request. Open worldwide.
jury: Laurie Freitag, Founder of L.A. Photo Curator
calls.summary: Juried by Laurie Freitag. Submit 3 or 6 images from your archive. Solo online exhibition for winner, group show for all selected.

calls.title: The City Series: Cambridge — Shutter Hub Editions Publication
calls.description: Open call for The City Series: Cambridge, the inaugural edition of Shutter Hub's ongoing series of photobooks exploring the people, places, and cultures that shape cities worldwide. Photographers are invited to approach Cambridge openly — through people, atmosphere, details, routines, abstractions, or unexpected moments that feel personal — showing what the city feels like rather than what it looks like. Selected images featured in a printed publication available at shutterhub.org.uk and selected stockists. Published in collaboration with Velvet Magazine. Pay-what-you-can entry with £10 minimum; free submissions available on request for photographers with limited income. Open worldwide.
calls.summary: Inaugural photobook in Shutter Hub's City Series, exploring Cambridge through atmosphere, routines, and personal moments. Pay-what-you-can.

calls.title: The Colour Library: Yellow — Shutter Hub Editions Publication
calls.description: Open call for The Colour Library: Yellow, part of Shutter Hub's curated series exploring the emotional, symbolic, and visual power of individual colours. This edition is dedicated to yellow — bold and joyful, energetic and optimistic, but also capable of signalling caution, unease, or something hauntingly strange. Welcomes all approaches from bold monochromes to subtle glows, conceptual or documentary. Selected photographers featured in a professionally produced photobook held in international collections including the British Library and V&A. 100 images will be selected. Featured photographers receive promotion and a dedicated page on the Shutter Hub website. Pay-what-you-can entry with £15 minimum. Free submissions on request for photographers with limited income. Open worldwide.
calls.summary: Photobook dedicated to the colour yellow, from bold monochromes to subtle glows. Held in British Library and V&A collections.
prose: Shutter Hub is a UK-based photography organization that runs an artist network, exhibition program, and publishing imprint. Their publications are held in the collections of the British Library, the V&A, and the Portuguese Center of Photography, which gives Shutter Hub-published work an unusual archival afterlife — books stay on shelves long past the moment they're released.

The Colour Library is a curated photobook series published by Shutter Hub Editions, with each volume dedicated to a single color and the emotional, symbolic, and visual associations it carries. The Yellow edition welcomes any approach to the color — bold monochromes to subtle glows, conceptual to documentary, the joyful and the cautionary — provided the work is family-appropriate.

Selection is for 100 images. The published book is perfect-bound A5 portrait (148×210mm) on 140gsm matte paper with a 350gsm cover. Featured photographers receive a credit listing with a link to their website on a dedicated promotional page on the Shutter Hub site, and the book is distributed worldwide through Shutter Hub's bookstore network and into national collections.

Submissions are pay-what-you-can with a £15 minimum donation; free submissions are available on request for photographers with limited income. Each photographer can submit up to 10 images as JPEGs (300dpi, CMYK, max 5MB, sized for A5 portrait), with filenames structured as lastname_firstname_imagetitle.jpg. The deadline is 5pm UK time on July 16, 2026; selection is announced within 12 weeks.

calls.title: Lucie Foundation Scholarship Program 2026
calls.description: Annual program offering four cash grants across two categories (Fine Art and Photojournalism/Documentary), each split between Professional and Emerging photographers. Prizes: Fine Art Professional $3,000 + Fine Art Emerging $1,000 + Photojournalism/Documentary Professional $3,000 + Photojournalism/Documentary Emerging $1,000 plus a Sony camera and lens. Winners featured in a group exhibition that travels to House of Lucie Galleries worldwide (Los Angeles, Athens, Budapest, Ostuni, Samui). 'Professional' means earning majority of income from photography; 'Emerging' means enrolled students, photographers in their first five years, or those who don't earn majority from photography. Early bird discounts: 20% off until April 23, 10% off until April 30. Applicants submit a project proposal (1,500 characters max), one-page bio/CV, and 20 digital images. Open to photographers worldwide aged 18+.
jury: Antares Wells, Assistant Curator, Museum of Contemporary Art Australia
calls.summary: Four cash grants for Fine Art and Documentary photographers (pro and emerging). Winners tour House of Lucie galleries worldwide.
prose: The Lucie Foundation is a 501(c)(3) non-profit best known for the annual Lucie Awards and the International Photography Awards (IPA). Its Scholarship Program runs alongside those, awarding four cash grants per year split across two categories: Fine Art and Photojournalism/Documentary. Each category is divided between Professional and Emerging applicants, where "Professional" means earning the majority of one's income from photography and "Emerging" covers students, photographers in their first five career years, or those who do not earn the majority of their income from the medium.

Prize structure: Fine Art Professional $3,000; Fine Art Emerging $1,000; Photojournalism/Documentary Professional $3,000; Photojournalism/Documentary Emerging $1,000 plus a Sony camera and lens. Winners are featured in a group exhibition that travels to the House of Lucie galleries in Los Angeles, Athens, Budapest, Ostuni, and Samui — five physical venues across three continents.

Submissions are open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and older. Applicants submit a 1,500-character project proposal, a one-page biography or CV, and twenty digital images (JPG, 72 DPI, max 4MB each). Entry fees are $25 (Professional) and $15 (Emerging), with early-bird discounts of 20% (through April 23) and 10% (through April 30). The 2026 final deadline is September 30; winners are announced in October.

The 2026 jury comprises Antares Wells (Assistant Curator, Museum of Contemporary Art Australia), Kateryna Radchenko (Ukraine-based curator and photography researcher), and Elizabeth Ferrer (curator and writer specializing in Latinx photography).

calls.title: PLACE/MEMORY — CONTACT Photography Festival
calls.description: Open call photography exhibition at Northern Contemporary Gallery in Toronto, presented as part of the 2026 CONTACT Photography Festival — Canada's largest photography festival. Photographers are invited to submit work that represents their current practice through the medium of photography, responding to the theme PLACE/MEMORY. Physical group exhibition runs May 21 – June 2, 2026, with an opening reception on May 21, 6–9pm. One submission per artist via the official Google form. Work drop-off May 19; pick-up June 3. Part of the CONSTELLATION program curated by Su-Ying Lee and Emilie Croning.
calls.summary: Toronto gallery exhibition during CONTACT Photography Festival on the theme of place and memory. Physical show May 21 – June 2, 2026.

calls.title: Women's Studio Workshop — Art-in-Ed Workspace Residency 2026
calls.description: 6–7 week workspace residency combining teaching with personal studio practice at Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, NY. Artists teach intaglio, silkscreen, or hand papermaking to local public school students — fourth and/or eighth graders three days/week for three weeks in Spring (elementary) or high school students one day/week for 4 weeks in Fall (plus school visits). Outside of teaching, artists work independently in any WSW studio including darkroom photography. Residency includes $175/day per teaching day plus $525 for lesson planning, free housing, and 24/7 studio access. Artist covers travel and materials. Fall 2026 cohort teaches high school; Spring 2027 cohort teaches elementary. Applications open February 15; notification in July.
calls.summary: Teaching-artist residency combining printmaking/photo instruction with personal studio work. Daily teaching stipend plus free housing.

calls.title: BEERS London Group Exhibition 2026
calls.description: Open call for a group exhibition of approximately 12 artists at BEERS London, a contemporary gallery in the heart of the City. All artistic media welcome including photography. Selected artists consigned for exhibition period plus up to three months, with 50/50 commission split on sales. Gallery actively promotes selected work to collectors. No guaranteed representation or sales. Open worldwide. Exhibition runs August–September 2026. Selected artists notified approximately four months before opening.
calls.summary: Group exhibition of ~12 artists at contemporary London gallery. All media including photography. Aug–Sep 2026 show.
prose: BEERS London is a contemporary commercial gallery in the City of London that runs an annual open call for a curated group exhibition. The 2026 cycle selects approximately 12 artists working across all media — painting, sculpture, photography, video, mixed media — for a show in August through September 2026.

Selected artists consign their work for the duration of the exhibition plus up to three months afterward, during which the gallery actively promotes the work to its collector base. Sales split commission 50/50. Insurance is provided by the gallery during the exhibition window.

The application is structured to allow combining tracks: the group exhibition application alone is £10, and the combined residency-plus-exhibition application is £25 (£5 less than applying separately). Selection is by the BEERS London team alongside guest curators. Eligibility is open globally to artists at any career stage.

Inclusion in the group exhibition does not guarantee gallery representation or sales — the format is closer to a curated open submission than to a representation pitch. Selected artists are notified approximately four months before the exhibition opening. The 2026 deadline is June 1.

calls.title: L'OLTRE 2026
calls.description: Open call from Naples-based photography association The Docks (founded 2020) inviting photographers and visual artists to explore visions that lie at the edges of conventional reality — beyond appearance, logic, and the visible. Winning project published as the first volume of L'OLTRE 2026 in a limited edition by The Docks Publishing. Honorable mentions featured on The Docks' channels as emerging artists. Fee is €15 total (€5 membership + €10 minimum donation). Open to all nationalities, genders, and ages. AI-generated works explicitly accepted.
calls.summary: Photobook call exploring visions beyond conventional reality. Winner published in limited edition by The Docks Publishing.

calls.title: Joan Wakelin Bursary 2026
calls.description: Annual £2,000 bursary for the production of a photographic essay on an overseas social documentary issue. Administered by the Royal Photographic Society in partnership with The Guardian. Winner also receives portfolio printing by Metro Imaging (up to 12 C-types at 16×12") and a portfolio review with Creative Director Prof Steve Macleod. Established in 2005 in memory of documentary photographer Joan Wakelin (d. 2003). Funds new original projects only; does not support ongoing projects or travel to/within war zones. Awarded to individuals, not groups. Open to all photographers worldwide.
calls.summary: £2,000 bursary for overseas documentary photo essays. RPS x The Guardian. Free entry, open worldwide. Named after Joan Wakelin.
prose: The Joan Wakelin Bursary is a £2,000 grant for the production of a photographic essay on an overseas social documentary subject, administered by the Royal Photographic Society (RPS) in partnership with The Guardian. The bursary was established in 2005 in memory of documentary photographer Joan Wakelin, who died in 2003.

Beyond the cash, the winner receives portfolio printing by Metro Imaging — up to 12 C-type prints at 16×12 inches — and a portfolio review with Creative Director Professor Steve Macleod. The combination is designed to fund production of the work and prepare it for editorial placement.
The bursary funds only new original projects; ongoing work is not eligible. Travel to or within war zones is excluded. The award is given to individuals rather than groups or collectives.

There is no application fee, and the bursary is open to photographers worldwide. The 2026 deadline is July 6. Applications go through RPS's awards platform; applicants submit a project proposal rather than completed images.

calls.title: Women's Studio Workshop — Studio Residency Grant 2026
calls.description: 4–6 week fully funded residency for artists at any career stage at Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, NY. Work independently in one of five studios: intaglio, letterpress, papermaking, screenprinting, or darkroom photography. Grant includes $350/week stipend, up to $500 for materials, up to $250 toward travel within the Continental US, free onsite housing, and 24/7 studio access. Applications open February 15; residencies take place September through June, 1–2 years after application.
