calls.summary: Fully funded darkroom residency with weekly stipend, materials budget, travel assistance, and onsite housing in Rosendale, NY.

calls.title: Women's Studio Workshop — Anita Wetzel Residency Grant 2026
calls.description: 4–6 week fully funded residency for mature artists aged 45 and older at Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, NY. Honors the legacy of Anita Lynn Wetzel. Work in any of five studios: intaglio, letterpress, papermaking, screenprinting, or darkroom photography. Grant includes $350/week stipend, up to $500 for materials, up to $250 toward travel within the Continental US, free onsite housing, and 24/7 studio access. Residencies take place September through June, 1–2 years after application.
calls.summary: Fully funded darkroom residency with stipend and housing, dedicated to mature artists aged 45+. Rosendale, NY.

calls.title: Stories: Narrative Photography
calls.description: Curated international group photography exhibition exploring narrative and storytelling. Seeking photographs that tell stories — personal or social, literal or symbolic, about persons, communities, objects, or places. All creative photographic interpretations welcome. Curated by Zsolt Bátori (PhD, Rutgers; founder/director PH21 Gallery; Photolucida board member) and Borbála Jász (art historian; Photolucida juror). Curator's choice receives three free entries for future PH21 exhibitions. Up to three honorable mentions. Special rate for students, unwaged, and low-income economies (€15–20). Images submitted by email as JPEG, longest side max 1280px. Early bird deadline May 18 at reduced rates; final deadline May 25. Exhibition at PH21 Gallery in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter, July 25 – August 18, 2026.
jury: Zsolt Bátori, Photographer & Philosophy of Art
Borbála Jász, Art Historian & Philosophy of Art
calls.summary: Curated group show on narrative and storytelling. Physical exhibition in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter, July–August. Student rates available.

calls.title: PORTAL
calls.description: Juried photography exhibition exploring the theme 'at the edge of becoming.' Seeking photographs depicting transition as a condition — figures between visibility and disappearance, spaces suggesting restricted entry, suspended moments, or structurally unstable compositions. The strongest images will resist resolution, embodying transition rather than describing it. Juried by Douglas Stockdale (visual artist, editor, educator; founder of PhotoBook Journal; work in collections at Museo d'Arte Contemporanea di Roma, Beinecke Library at Yale, Reminders Photography Stronghold). All photographic styles and processes accepted. Exhibition June 20 – August 20, 2026.
jury: Douglas Stockdale, Visual Artist & Founder of PhotoBook Journal
calls.summary: Transition & becoming — figures, spaces, suspended moments. Juried by Douglas Stockdale (PhotoBook Journal founder).
prose: Decagon Gallery is an online curatorial platform that runs themed photography exhibitions with published catalogs and social distribution. "PORTAL" is the gallery's open call for photography exploring tension at the edge of transition — images that hold a viewer at the moment a shift is imminent but not yet complete. Literal interpretations (doors, windows, thresholds) are accepted only when the photograph carries inherent tension; the brief favors work that embodies transition rather than describing it.

Cash awards total $1,000 across three placements: $500 first place plus a solo website exhibition, $300 second, $200 third. All selected photographers receive a permanent exhibition page on the Decagon site and inclusion in the published catalog. The 2026 exhibition runs June 20 through August 20.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Douglas Stockdale, founder of PhotoBook Journal and author of the Singular Images blog. His work is held in collections at Museo d'Arte Contemporanea di Roma and the Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library at Yale.

All photographic processes are welcome. Entry fee is $25 for up to 8 images. Eligibility is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over. Submissions are JPG at 2100 pixels on the long side, no watermarks or borders. The 2026 deadline is June 3 at 11:59 PM Eastern; results announced June 15.

calls.title: The Emergence Project 2026
calls.description: Annual graduate showcase for recently graduated UK-based photographers (graduated 2023–2026). Free to submit. Gallery covers all printing and installation costs, with work printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames. Submit up to 8 images along with a brief statement about your work, graduation details, and why you'd like to participate. Exhibition July 3–31, 2026 at Glasgow Gallery of Photography.
calls.summary: Free graduate showcase for UK photography grads (2023–2026). Gallery covers printing and framing. Glasgow exhibition, July.

calls.title: Across America 2026
calls.description: Photography exhibition celebrating America's diverse and dynamic essence — landscapes, people, culture, or any aspect that embodies the nation's spirit. Up to 3 images forming a cohesive series. Juried by Brian Crowley (landscape/street photographer) and Ron St. Jean (portrait/fine art photographer, 40+ years experience). Exhibition at The Art Center gallery in historic downtown Dover. Artists receive 70% of sale price. All work must be for sale and cannot be removed during the exhibition. Members enter free. Open to US photographers of all levels, 18+. Exhibition July 13 – August 31, 2026.
jury: Ron St. Jean, Portrait & Fine Art Photographer
calls.summary: Photography celebrating America's diverse essence — landscapes, people, culture. Juried exhibition in Dover, NH, July–August.

calls.title: Fine Art Photography Awards 2026/2027
calls.description: 13th edition of the international fine art photography contest. 20 categories: Abstract, Architecture, Conceptual, Experimental, Fashion, Fine Art, Landscape, Nature, Night Photography, Nudes, Open Theme, Panoramic, People, Photojournalism, Photomanipulation, Portrait, Seascape, Street Photography, Travel, Wildlife/Animals. Professional and Amateur divisions. Early bird deadline October 11, 2026; final deadline February 14, 2027. Winners announced April 11, 2027. Panel of 15 international jurors. Professional Grand Prize: $3,000 + Fine Art Photographer of the Year title. Amateur Grand Prize: $2,000. Category winners receive gold/silver/bronze awards. Open worldwide.
calls.summary: 13th edition — 20 categories from landscape to street. $3K professional / $2K amateur grand prizes. 15 international jurors.
prose: Fine Art Photography Awards is an international competition founded in 2014 and now running its 13th edition. Submissions are open to amateurs and professionals worldwide across 20 categories: Abstract, Architecture, Conceptual, Experimental, Fashion, Fine Art, Landscape, Nature, Night Photography, Nudes, Open Theme, Panoramic, People, Photojournalism, Photomanipulation, Portrait, Seascape, Street Photography, Travel, and Wildlife/Animals.

The Professional Grand Prize is $3,000 plus the Professional Fine Art Photographer of the Year title. The Amateur Grand Prize is $2,000 plus the Amateur title. Category winners receive Gold, Silver, Bronze, or White badges and certificates; all winners receive gallery showcase and international press coverage.

Entry fees use a tiered structure with separate amateur and professional rates. At early deadline (October 11, 2026): Amateur $19 single / $24 series; Professional $24 single / $29 series. At final deadline (February 14, 2027): Amateur $24 single / $29 series; Professional $29 single / $34 series. Additional categories cost $10 each.

The jury comprises 15 international photographers, including Jaco Marx, Michele Palazzo, Karolina Wojtasik, Tugo Cheng, Jan Møller Hansen, Juan Pablo de Miguel, Anna Tihanyi, and others, with names rotating between editions. Winners are announced April 11, 2027.

calls.title: Black and White
calls.description: Celebrating the power and timelessness of black and white photography — the deep, unending shades of grey. All photographic genres welcome. At least 26 images selected for exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 22×22 white framing and custom matting. 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to all skill levels. Exhibition July 4 – July 25, 2026.
jury: Holly Hart, Conceptual Fine Art Photographer & Decode Gallery Founder
calls.summary: B&W photography — all genres. Pro printing on Ilford Pearl paper and museum framing included. Exhibition in Tucson, AZ.

calls.title: Global Ability Photography Challenge 2026
calls.description: 5th edition of the world's largest inclusive photography competition, exclusively for persons with disabilities. Open to all styles — documentary, portrait, street, conceptual, abstract, or experimental. No theme restriction, no age limit. Top 20 photographs exhibited in Ahmedabad, India, with works featured across media and global campaigns. Custom trophies by designer Michael Foley. Award ceremony June 24, 2026. Travel and accommodation support provided for winners. Over 4 editions, GAPC has reached 8 million people and 50,000+ participants from 30+ countries. Organized by Not Just Art (Youth4Jobs) with Adani GreenXTalks.
calls.summary: Free photography competition exclusively for persons with disabilities — ~$20K in prizes, top 20 exhibited in Ahmedabad.

calls.title: #HopperHappens Juried Photography Exhibition
calls.description: Photography-only juried exhibition inspired by the #HopperHappens Instagram series — real-world moments evoking Edward Hopper's style, light, and mood. 55 photographs selected and displayed across 55 businesses and nonprofits in Nyack, NY, birthplace of Edward Hopper. $1,000 in cash prizes: First $500, Second $300, Third $200, plus Juror's and Visitor's Choice awards. Juror: Richard Tuschman, celebrated for his 'Hopper Meditations' series. Exhibition June 1 – July 5, 2026. Open internationally, ages 18+. Work must be completed after January 1, 2020 and never previously exhibited at EHHM. MFA student discounts available.
calls.summary: Photography inspired by Hopper's light and mood — 55 works displayed across 55 Nyack venues. Juror: Richard Tuschman.

calls.title: Narrative
calls.description: Photography exhibition exploring visual storytelling through single images or cohesive series. Documentary, street, conceptual, staged, and experimental approaches welcome. Exhibition at Chico Art Center gallery, August 15 – September 18, 2026, with opening reception September 4. Member fee $25. Free exhibition catalog via Blurb. Opportunity to sell work (30% commission to center). Previously exhibited work at CAC ineligible.
calls.summary: Photography exhibition on visual storytelling — documentary, street, conceptual, staged, or experimental approaches.
prose: Chico Art Center is a community arts gallery at 450 Orange Street, Suite 6 in Chico, California. "Narrative" is the gallery's open call for photography that explores visual storytelling — work that communicates a narrative through a single image or cohesive series, whether personal journey, cultural or historical commentary, political statement, or fiction.

All photographic mediums and styles are welcome — documentary, street, conceptual, staged, experimental — with no thematic constraint beyond the storytelling brief. AI-generated images are not currently accepted. Work previously exhibited at CAC is ineligible.

Selected work is exhibited at Chico Art Center August 15 through September 18, 2026, with an opening reception on September 4. The gallery handles installation. Each artist receives a free copy of a printed exhibition catalog produced via Blurb, and selected work is promoted through the gallery's website and social channels.
Sales are facilitated by the gallery, which requests a 30% donation but pays the artist the full listed price. Artists are responsible for shipping and insurance.

Entry fee is $35 (general) or $25 for CAC members. Submissions take up to 7 images via JotForm. The 2026 deadline is June 14 at 11:59 PM. Selection is by Gallery Director Cameron Kelly with a CAC board member.

calls.title: Flatland Feature — Issue 2
calls.description: Online photography feature showcasing photographers' work in a series format as a virtual gallery experience. Selected photographers' work featured for six months on the MWCP website (July–December 2026). Each feature consists of 10–20 images with an accompanying artist statement and biography. Visitors can view and purchase photographs online (50% commission). Open internationally, all subject matter and genres accepted.
calls.summary: Online portfolio feature — 10–20 images showcased for 6 months on MWCP website. All genres, open internationally.

calls.title: The Art of Abandonment
calls.description: International open call exploring abandoned and rediscovered objects, locations, and structures. Photographers examine what these forgotten spaces reveal about humanity, memory, and the passage of time. Online exhibition June 1 – July 1, 2026. Curator's Choice, Director's Choice, and Honorable Mentions awarded. Blind jury process — juror sees only the image and title.
calls.summary: Themed exhibition exploring forgotten structures, objects, and places — what they reveal about humanity and time.

calls.title: Encontros Da Imagem Award 2026
calls.description: Open call for the 36th edition of Encontros da Imagem, one of Europe's oldest photography festivals, founded in 1991 in Braga, Portugal. Three projects selected for solo exhibitions during the festival across multiple northern Portuguese cities, September 18 – November 1, 2026. One overall winner receives €2,000. Seventeen further projects included in a collective video screening. Theme: Territory And Identity. Projects must use photography or video with coherent narrative structure, produced within the last five years. Maximum three projects per applicant.
calls.summary: Major European photo festival (36th edition). €2,000 prize + solo exhibition. Theme: Territory And Identity. Open worldwide.
jury: Arianna Catania, Independent Curator & Photo Editor
Arianna Rinaldo, Independent Curator & Photography Consultant

calls.title: 31st National Competition 2026
calls.description: Soho Photo Gallery's 31st annual National Competition. Approximately 60 photographs selected for exhibition at the gallery's spacious W23rd Street location in Chelsea, New York. Cash prizes for first ($400) and second ($200) place. Third place and up to four honorable mentions receive prizes from sponsor Archival Methods. Juror: Joanna Lehan, Manager of Curatorial Projects at Museum of the City of New York. Open to photographers who are residents of the United States. Exhibition July 2026.
calls.summary: Annual photo competition at Soho Photo Gallery NYC. ~60 works exhibited. $400 first, $200 second. US residents only.
jury: Joanna Lehan, Manager of Curatorial Projects, Museum of the City of New York

calls.title: BLACK & WHITE
calls.description: International juried photography exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis celebrating monochrome photography as a deliberate creative choice. Up to 74 images selected for exhibition June 20 – July 11, 2026. Awards include Juror's Choice (free entry to three future calls) and Directors' Choice (free entry to two future calls), plus eight honorable mentions. Members receive 10 images for the price of 5. Free submissions available for artists experiencing financial hardship. Juror: Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, fine art photographer, printmaker, and founder of All About Photo.
calls.summary: Monochrome juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery Minneapolis. Up to 74 works selected. Open internationally.

calls.title: Thresholds 2026: Up, Close and Personal
calls.description: Annual street photography exhibition at the Los Angeles Center of Photography, one of LA's leading photography institutions. 2026 theme: Up, Close and Personal — intimate street photography. Digital projection exhibition and in-person opening event at LACP Helms Design District, May 7–31, 2026. Open to international photographers of all skill levels. Prizes: 1st place $500 plus one-year LACP membership, 2nd place $500 LACP gift card, 3rd place $250 LACP gift card. Juror: Michaela Norah Mohrmann, assistant curator at UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art. Members receive 25% discount on fees.
calls.summary: Street photography exhibition at LACP LA. $500 first place. Digital projection show + opening event. Open worldwide.

calls.title: Light Dreams
calls.description: Juried exhibition of alternative and historical process photography at Light Art Space gallery in Silver City, New Mexico. Theme explores light as an internal, psychological, and symbolic presence — where light and dreams intersect through hand-made photographic processes. Accepted media: cyanotype, platinum/palladium, silver gelatin, wet-plate collodion, gum bichromate, and other alternative processes. Digital negatives acceptable but straight digital and AI-derived work ineligible. 3D and experimental work encouraged. Open internationally, ages 18+. Gallery actively invites LGBTQ+, Black, Latinx, Indigenous, and artists of color. Exhibition July 4 – September 6, 2026, with reception July 5. Student rate $20.
calls.summary: Alt-process juried show in New Mexico. Cyanotype, platinum, wet-plate & more. Open worldwide, student rate $20.

calls.title: COAL Prize 2026 — The Night
calls.description: Annual art and ecology prize from French foundation COAL. 2026 theme: The Night — defending darkness as a common good, a major ecological issue for regeneration of life, a refuge, and a right to rest. Main prize: €12,000 grant plus creative residency at Domaine de Belval (François Sommer Foundation). Special Jury Prize: €3,000. Centre Wallonie-Bruxelles mention: €2,000 plus exhibition. Ateliers Médicis mention: residency near Paris. Ten artists nominated by committee, winners chosen by jury. Submit single PDF (max 30MB) with project description, technical note, budget, 2+ HD visuals, CV, and portfolio. Open worldwide, all disciplines including photography and lens-based media.
calls.summary: €12,000 art & ecology prize with residency. Theme: defending darkness. Jury Prize €3,000. Free, open worldwide.

calls.title: 1st Photobook Grants 2026
calls.description: Fourth edition of the 1st Photobook Grants supporting photographers who have never published a monograph. Three grants of €5,000 each in three categories: photographers from the Global South (Africa, Caribbean, Southeast Asia, Latin America, Middle East), French photographers or those residing in France (SAIF grant), and female photographers of any nationality. Must partner with an independent French publisher and provide a letter of commitment. Supported by the French Ministry of Culture and SAIF. Winners announced June 2026; books must be published by November 30, 2027.
calls.summary: Three €5,000 grants for debut photobook projects. Categories: Global South, French, and female photographers. Free, needs French publisher.

calls.title: Ten x Ten – 18th Annual Small Works
calls.description: Annual small works exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (November 14 – December 31, 2026). Celebrates creative expression within the square photographic format. All works are 10"×10" and priced at $200 each. MWCP provides printing at no cost to selected artists. Open to all photographers internationally.
calls.summary: Annual 10"×10" square-format exhibition at MWCP, Wichita. Affordable collectible works, MWCP prints at no cost.
prose: Ten x Ten is the Midwest Center for Photography's annual square-format exhibition, now in its 18th year. The brief is unusually concrete: every accepted print is exactly 10 inches by 10 inches, and every print is sold at the same price — $200 each — for the duration of the show. The format levels the field across genres and career stages and produces a uniform grid hang that has become the show's signature.

MWCP is a small photography-focused space in Wichita, Kansas. Selected work is exhibited both physically and online; MWCP covers all printing costs for accepted entries, which is unusual for a juried show at this scale. A $30 frame rental is the only out-of-pocket expense for selected artists who want their work framed for the wall.

Submissions are open internationally to photographers working in any process — film, digital, iPhone, or alternative. The 2026 exhibition runs November 14 through December 31, with the submission deadline September 1.

calls.title: FOTOHOF>CALLING
calls.description: Biennial open call for contemporary photographic projects. Around 25 artists are selected for online publication on the FOTOHOF>CALLING platform and in the FOTOHOF>CALLING Magazine. 10 finalists are invited to present their projects in Salzburg on October 3, 2026, with an open-air projection on Inge-Morath-Platz. Projects must be no older than three years and never exhibited in institutional settings (museums, galleries, festivals). Student/university work and residency programs are exempt from this rule. Open to artists who reside, work, or stay in Europe.
calls.summary: Biennial call for contemporary photo projects. 25 selected for publication, 10 finalists present in Salzburg. Open to European artists.

calls.title: Martin House Creative Residency 2026
calls.description: 2–4 week project-based residency at Frank Lloyd Wright's Darwin D. Martin House in Buffalo, New York. Residents live in the Gardener's Cottage on campus and create new work inspired by the architecture, design, landscape, and social history of Martin House. Open to artists working in any discipline including photography, writing, and research. Residents receive $5,000 stipend paid in two installments and up to $1,000 travel allowance for non-local applicants. Residency term runs June–October 2026. Must deliver a free public program, performance, or exhibition sharing work with the community. Requires US social security number. Application window March 30 – May 13, 2026.
calls.summary: 2–4 week residency at Frank Lloyd Wright's Martin House. $5,000 stipend + $1,000 travel. Work inspired by architecture and design.

calls.title: Loghaven Artist Residency 2027
calls.description: Residency on 90 acres of forested land in Knoxville, Tennessee for practicing artists at any career stage. Sessions range from 2–6 weeks between February and October 2027. All fellows receive an $850/week living stipend, travel subsidy ($400–$800 on a sliding scale), and up to $200 in materials shipping reimbursement. Disciplines include visual arts, writing, dance, music composition, theater, and interdisciplinary work. Applicants must be 21+, live 120+ miles from Knoxville, and have legal US work authorization. International artists are not eligible. Applications open June 1, 2026. Submit 8 JPEG images for visual art via SlideRoom.
calls.summary: 2–6 week residency on 90 forested acres. $850/week stipend plus travel subsidy. Visual arts, writing, and more.
prose: Loghaven is an artist residency on 90 acres of woodland at 1001 Loghaven Drive in Knoxville, Tennessee. Artists are housed in five historic log cabins that have been rehabilitated and modernized, with access to purpose-built studio space on the grounds.

The 2027 program runs across six sessions of varying lengths: a four-week February cycle, a six-week April–May cycle, a two-week June cycle for fellows only, a two-week July cycle for teaching/faculty artists, a two-week September cycle, and a four-week October–November cycle. Applicants choose their preferred session at submission.

Financial support is unusually substantive for a residency: an $850 per week living stipend for the duration of the stay, a sliding-scale travel subsidy of $400–$800, and up to $200 reimbursement for materials shipping. Disciplines accepted include visual arts, writing, dance, music composition, theater, and interdisciplinary work.

Eligibility is restricted: artists must be at least 21 years old, hold U.S. work authorization, live at least 120 miles from Knoxville, and not be enrolled in a degree-seeking program. International artists are not eligible. Two professional references are required.

The application fee is $25, with waivers available June 1–July 15. Applications open June 1 and close July 15, 2026 at midnight Eastern Time. The selection panel — a national committee of artist peers and arts professionals — meets August through September, with applicants notified by November 1.

calls.title: FMoPA 2026 International Photography Competition
calls.description: International photography competition open to photographers worldwide. Submit up to 15 images across 7 categories: People/Portraits, Places/Landscape, Nature/Science/Animals, Documentation/Photojournalism, Still Life, Abstract, and Conceptual. Best in Competition receives $1,000 cash prize. Category winners receive goods and services. Winning works exhibited June 16 – August 2, 2026 at FMoPA in Tampa's Ybor City District.
calls.summary: International photography competition. $1,000 grand prize and exhibition at FMoPA Tampa. 7 categories.
jury: Jessica Jarl, Global Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska
Hiromi Nakamura, Curator, Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Photography
Elena Paraskeva, Photographer and Art Director
Bärbel Reinhard, Photographer, Curator and Educator
Kristen Roles, Photographic Artist and Educator

calls.title: Fotograf Magazine 2026 Open Call
calls.description: Open call for publication in Fotograf Magazine, a leading international photography publication based in Prague. Two selected projects published in the next printed issue. Open to professionals, amateurs, and students submitting independent fine-art photography or moving-image projects. Submit CV, portfolio PDF, and project description with images via email.
jury: Felix Hoffmann, Curator and Director, FOTO ARSENAL WIEN
Peter Watkins, Visual Artist and Lecturer, FAMU
calls.summary: Publication opportunity in leading international photography magazine based in Prague. Two projects selected for print.

calls.title: Grenze Arsenali Fotografici 2026 Open Call
calls.description: Open call for the ninth edition of Grenze - Arsenali Fotografici international photography festival in Verona. Theme: Nachleben. Three artists selected for exhibition during the festival opening September 2026.
jury: Aida Redžepagić & Jelena Janković, Sarajevo Photography Festival
David Pujado, Belgrade Photo Month Founder
Simone Azzoni, Co-Founder & Artistic Director, Grenze
calls.summary: International photography festival in Verona. Theme: Nachleben. Three artists exhibited. Strong international jury.

calls.title: Photography 4 Humanity / Fotografiska Global Prize 2026
calls.description: Global photography prize exploring the theme HOME — safety, belonging, identity, memory, loss, and place. Open to photographers worldwide. Selected photographs exhibited at United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day (December 10, 2026), guest-curated by James Nachtwey.
calls.summary: Theme: HOME. Selected work exhibited at UN Headquarters NYC, curated by James Nachtwey. Free entry.
jury: Pauline Benthede, Global VP Artistic Direction & Exhibitions, Fotografiska
Sophia Emmerich, Lead Editor, Fotografiska Emerging Platform
prose: The HOME open call is a joint initiative by Photography 4 Humanity, Fotografiska, and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. The brief is the single word "home" — interpreted across safety, belonging, dignity, identity, memory, loss, and place — and the call is positioned as a human rights project rather than a conventional photography prize.

Selected work is exhibited at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day, December 10, 2026. The exhibition is guest-curated by James Nachtwey, with Pauline Benthede (Fotografiska's Global VP of Artistic Direction & Exhibitions) and Sophia Emmerich (Lead Editor of the Fotografiska Emerging Platform) joining selection.

The selection structure has three tiers: one Main Image, ten Runners-up, and twenty Honorable Mentions — 31 photographers in total. Submissions are limited to three images per applicant. Only lens-based photography is accepted (analog or digital); AI-generated or prompt-based images are explicitly excluded.
There is no entry fee. The call is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over, with explicit emphasis on emerging artists. The deadline is July 12, 2026; results are announced October 5, 2026.

calls.title: Minimalist Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: Seventh edition of the international award celebrating minimalist photography as a visual language. Open to photographers worldwide. Submit single images or series (2–7 images) across 12 categories including Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscape, Long Exposure, Portrait, and Street. Grand prize: €2,000 cash, hand-crafted trophy, title of Minimalist Photographer of the Year, and inclusion in the official annual book. Earlybird deadline May 1; final deadline June 2, 2026.
calls.summary: International award for minimalist photography. €2,000 grand prize, book publication, and exhibition. 12 categories.
calls.ai: Only accepted if incorporating a real photograph
jury: Milad Safabakhsh, Founder, Minimalist Photography Awards
prose: The Minimalist Photography Awards is an international competition focused exclusively on minimalist photography as a visual language. The 2026 cycle is the 7th edition; the awards have been running annually since the first edition in 2019. The program is based in Bregenz, Austria, and was founded by photographer Milad Safabakhsh.

Submissions are accepted across 12 categories: Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscape, Long Exposure, Portrait, Street, and others. Photographers may submit single images or series of 2 to 7 images per category.

The Grand Prize Winner receives €2,000 in cash, a hand-crafted trophy, and the title "Minimalist Photographer of the Year," along with inclusion in the official annual book and gallery exhibition opportunities. Category winners are featured in the annual book and online showcase.

The 2026 jury comprises Sylvia Janschek (photographer), Matthias Weissengruber (photographer), Leon Boch (photographer), and founder Milad Safabakhsh, with the international panel rounding out across editions.

Entry fees are tiered with an early bird deadline May 1 and final deadline June 2, 2026 (23:59 UTC). Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18 and over. AI-generated work is accepted only if it incorporates a real photograph; fully AI-generated work is excluded.

calls.title: Villa Lena Foundation — Artist Residency 2027
calls.description: Residency program for artists of all disciplines in a 19th-century villa in Tuscany, Italy. Residencies run 4–5 weeks between April and October 2027. Includes studio space, accommodation, and half-board meals five days a week. Residency fee of €150/week covers room, studio, and meals. Artists must donate a completed work to the foundation's collection. Access to ceramic and wood workshops, screening room, and weekly excursions.
calls.summary: 4–5 week residency in a Tuscan villa with studio, accommodation, and meals. €150/week residency fee. All disciplines.

calls.title: Taylor Wessing Photo Portrait Prize 2026
calls.description: One of the world's most prestigious portrait photography competitions. Open to photographers worldwide, aged 18+. Submit up to 6 portraits taken after 1 January 2025. First prize £15,000, second £3,000, third £2,000. Selected works exhibited at the National Portrait Gallery in London from November 2026 to January 2027. The prize celebrates contemporary portraiture, interpreting 'portrait' in its widest sense — photography concerned with portraying people with an emphasis on their identity as individuals.
calls.summary: Premier international portrait prize. £15,000 first prize. Exhibition at National Portrait Gallery, London, Nov 2026–Jan 2027.

calls.title: EMERGE 2026
calls.description: Annual fellowship for emerging photographers. Open to all emerging photographers worldwide working in any photographic medium. Twenty photographers selected for group exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (September 4–21, 2026). One photographer receives the $200 EMERGE Fellowship Award plus one year of online representation by MWCP.
calls.summary: Fellowship for emerging photographers. 20 selected for exhibition, one awarded $200 + year-long online representation.
prose: EMERGE is the Midwest Center for Photography's annual fellowship for emerging photographers — a more concentrated track than the gallery's larger Ten x Ten exhibition. The program aims to give early-career photographers their first formal exhibition placement, with selection emphasizing work that demonstrates a distinct voice rather than technical polish alone.

Twenty photographers are selected for the group exhibition at MWCP's gallery in Wichita, Kansas, running September 4 through 21, 2026. One photographer additionally receives the $200 EMERGE Fellowship Award plus one year of online representation by MWCP, which functions as ongoing visibility for the work beyond the exhibition window.
Eligibility is open to emerging photographers worldwide working in any photographic medium — the program does not specify a fixed years-since-graduation cutoff but emphasizes early-career work.
Submissions require 5 to 14 images plus a brief artist statement. Entry fee is $50 for up to 5 images. Submissions are made by email through the MWCP entry page. The 2026 deadline is June 1.

calls.title: Human Depiction
calls.description: International portrait photography exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (May 1–25, 2026). Seeks photographs capturing the essence of human subjects — emotional gestures, visual expressions, and the full range of personality. Individual images evaluated on merit. Selected artists' work printed and framed by MWCP for gallery display.
calls.summary: International portrait exhibition at MWCP, Wichita. Capturing the essence of human subjects through emotional and expressive photography.

calls.title: Blossom
calls.description: International floral photography exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (June 5–22, 2026). Celebrates photographs of flowers and plants in all forms — from nature photography to still-life approaches. Open to all photographic media and styles. Selected artists' work printed and framed by MWCP for gallery display.
calls.summary: International floral photography exhibition at MWCP, Wichita. All styles welcome — nature, still life, macro, and more.

calls.title: Traversing Terrain
calls.description: International landscape and cityscape photography exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (July 11–27, 2026). Features photographs describing and documenting natural and man-made landscapes — urban, suburban, and rural environments. All photographic media welcome. Selected artists' work printed and framed by MWCP for gallery display.
calls.summary: International landscape and cityscape exhibition at MWCP, Wichita. Urban, suburban, and rural environments welcome.

calls.title: White: Absence of Color
calls.description: International achromatic photography exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (August 7–24, 2026). Explores photography emphasizing the lightest end of the color spectrum — minimal color saturation conveying striking imagery and psychological impact. All photographic media welcome. Selected artists' work printed and framed by MWCP for gallery display.
calls.summary: International achromatic photography exhibition at MWCP, Wichita. Explores the lightest end of the spectrum with minimal color.

calls.title: Developed Work 2026
calls.description: National photography fellowship competition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (October 2–26, 2026). Open to all US-based photographers. Seeks thematically developed bodies of work with cohesive conceptual frameworks demonstrating the pulse of contemporary American photography. Winner receives the $200 Developed Work Fellowship Award and one year of online representation by MWCP.
calls.summary: National fellowship for developed bodies of work. $200 award + one year online representation at MWCP, Wichita.
prose: Developed Work is the Midwest Center for Photography's annual national fellowship competition, focused on thematically developed bodies of work rather than individual standout images. The brief is explicit: selection emphasizes a cohesive conceptual framework — submissions are evaluated on the body of work as a whole rather than its strongest image.

The Wichita, Kansas gallery exhibits selected work in person, with the 2026 exhibition running October 2 through 26. The winner receives the $200 Developed Work Fellowship Award and one year of online representation by MWCP, which functions as ongoing visibility for the work beyond the exhibition window.

Submissions are limited to U.S.-based photographers and require 5 to 14 images plus a brief artist statement explaining the work's intent. Entry fee is $50 for up to 5 images. The 2026 deadline is July 1.

The competition runs alongside MWCP's other open calls, including the international Ten x Ten Small Works exhibition. Where Ten x Ten samples individual 10×10 inch prints across many photographers, Developed Work selects a single fellow per cycle whose practice exemplifies sustained thematic exploration.

calls.title: Lisbon Street Photo Fest: Open Call 2026
calls.description: 2nd edition. Street photography open call in two categories: Singles (individual photos) and Series (10–15 images). Finalists exhibited at Faculdade de Belas-Artes da Universidade de Lisboa during festival weekend, 25–27 September 2026. €4,000 in cash prizes plus VSCO Pro memberships. Photos must be captured after 1 January 2024. No AI-generated content or watermarks.
calls.summary: 2nd edition. Street photography Singles & Series. €4,000 in prizes. Exhibition in Lisbon, Sept 25–27.

calls.title: The Photo Review 41st Annual International Photography Competition
calls.description: 41st edition of one of photography's most respected annual competitions. Juried by Dr. Sarah Kennel, Aaron Siskind Curator of Photography at the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts. Selected work exhibited at the Woodmere Art Museum in Philadelphia and published in The Photo Review journal. $1,000 purchase prize from Haverford College plus equipment and printing prizes. All entrants receive a full-color catalogue.
jury: Dr. Sarah Kennel, Aaron Siskind Curator of Photography, Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
calls.summary: 41st edition. Juried by Dr. Sarah Kennel (VMFA). Exhibition at Woodmere Art Museum, Philadelphia. $1,000 purchase prize.

calls.title: Athens Street Photography Festival 2026
calls.description: First edition of the Athens Street Photography Festival. Submit up to three street photographs taken in 2025 or 2026. Finalists' work exhibited at TAF (The Art Foundation) in Athens during the festival (May 14–17, 2026). Winner selected by Magnum photographer Nikos Economopoulos. Free to submit; selected finalists pay €50 per exhibited image to cover production costs.
calls.prize: Exhibition at TAF + winner selected by jury
calls.summary: 1st edition. Free street photo submissions, finalists exhibited at TAF Athens. Winner chosen by Magnum's Nikos Economopoulos.

calls.title: Abstract 2026
calls.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of abstract. Submit images exploring abstract concepts in any photographic style. Selected work displayed in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow, with work also appearing in an online gallery on the gallery's website. Images printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames. Photographers retain all copyright.
calls.summary: Abstract photography in any style. Month-long Glasgow gallery exhibition plus online gallery. Fujifilm printing, copyright retained.

calls.title: Portrait 2026
calls.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of portrait. Open to everyone. Selected work displayed in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow, with work also appearing in an online gallery on the gallery's website. Images printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames. Photographers retain all copyright.
calls.summary: Portrait photography, open to all. Month-long Glasgow gallery exhibition plus online gallery. Fujifilm printing, copyright retained.

calls.title: Rancho Linda Vista — Summer Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: One-month summer residency for visual artists at Rancho Linda Vista, a historic arts community on 100+ acres in Oracle, Arizona. Resident receives a furnished one-bedroom house, separate studio space, and $1,000 stipend. Access to swimming pool, library, and wilderness trails. Open studio exhibit at conclusion of stay. Available for July or August 2026. Must provide own transportation and materials. MFA preferred but not required.
calls.summary: One-month summer residency with $1,000 stipend, house, and studio on 100+ acres of Arizona wilderness.

calls.title: La Embajada 2026
calls.description: Third edition of La Embajada, a programme promoting contemporary Spanish photography within the European circuit through an exhibition during the opening week of Rencontres d'Arles. Six projects selected, each artist receiving €1,400 fee. Selected photographers exhibit during the festival's opening week (July 6–13, 2026) and participate in active mediation with audiences. La Embajada creates a temporary 'embassy' to showcase photographic projects and foster professional connections at the epicentre of world photography. Organised by El Local (independent space for contemporary photography in Madrid) in partnership with Plataforma Fotografía e Imagen, with support from Spain's Ministry of Culture. Submit one project per applicant via digital form. Work must be produced and exhibition-ready. Physical presence in Arles during opening week is mandatory.
calls.summary: Six Spanish photographers exhibit at Rencontres d'Arles opening week. €1,400 each. Free, supported by Ministry of Culture.
jury: Christoph Wiesner, Director, Les Rencontres d'Arles
Elisa Medde, Director, Foto Colectania Foundation

calls.title: APhF Pick:26 Book Award
calls.description: Annual juried photobook award from the Hellenic Centre of Photography as part of Athens Photo Festival. Open to all photobooks worldwide produced or published between January 2025 and March 2026 with a minimum edition of 100 copies. Winner receives €2,000 cash prize and inclusion in the main festival exhibition programme at Benaki Museum. Ten photobooks featured in the APhF:26 print catalogue, twenty shortlisted and exhibited at Benaki Museum / Pireos 138. All submitted works added to the APhF Library and Athens Photo Research Center. Submit online entry form, cover image, project description, artist biography, and mail two physical copies to the Hellenic Center of Photography in Athens. €15 for each additional project by the same applicant.
jury: Marta Weiss, Curator of Photography, Victoria and Albert Museum
Cécile Sayuri Poimboeuf-Koizumi, Publisher, Chose Commune
Sylvia Sachini, Curator, APhF Book Program
calls.summary: Photobook award from Athens Photo Festival. €2,000 prize. 20 shortlisted exhibited at Benaki Museum. Min 100-copy edition.

calls.title: ABSURIA — International Abstract & Surrealist Photography Contest 2026
calls.description: First edition of a new international festival dedicated exclusively to abstract and surrealist photography. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide. 100 photographs selected for physical exhibition across multiple venues in Tours, Loire Valley, France from May to September 2026. Fourteen winners honoured at an awards ceremony in Tours in early May. Categories: Abstract Photography and Surrealist Photography, each with Professional and Amateur divisions plus a Young Hopefuls award. Winners receive the ABSURIA Trophy — a physical gold statuette created specifically for the contest. All nominees exhibited in 3D online galleries on the festival website. Printing costs covered by organisers. AI-generated images not accepted. Fee varies by number of works submitted: amateur €20–€40, professional €25–€50, up to 6 images per registration.
calls.summary: First international festival for abstract & surrealist photography. Physical exhibition in Tours, France. Trophy + online 3D gallery.

calls.title: Athens Photo Festival Dummy Award 2026
calls.description: International photobook dummy competition run by the Hellenic Centre of Photography as part of Athens Photo Festival. Open to all photographers and artists who use photography, regardless of age or nationality. Winner receives a publishing contract with Chose Commune for the production of a photobook with a production budget of up to €15,000 and a minimum print run of 400 copies. Winning project included in the festival's main exhibition programme at Benaki Museum in Athens. Twenty shortlisted dummies exhibited at the festival, ten included in the printed catalogue. Submit digitally via online form (PDF, max 10 MB) and mail one physical dummy copy postmarked by the deadline. Projects should be finalized upon submission. If already printed, editions must be under 100 copies. Fee €25 per project, €15 for additional projects by the same applicant.
jury: Katerina Gregos, Artistic Director, EMΣT (National Museum of Contemporary Art, Athens)
Cécile Sayuri Poimboeuf-Koizumi, Publisher, Chose Commune
Marta Weiss, Curator of Photography, Victoria and Albert Museum
Sylvia Sachini, Curator, APhF Book Program
calls.summary: Dummy award with Chose Commune publishing contract (up to €15K). 20 shortlisted exhibited at Athens Photo Festival, Benaki Museum.

calls.title: Motion
calls.description: Curated international group photography exhibition exploring motion in still images. Photography cannot create the illusion of motion the way moving images can, yet photographers have developed powerful techniques for capturing and evoking it — from long exposures and motion blur to freezing split-second moments of action. PH21 Gallery invites submissions for a themed group show at their venue in Barcelona's historic Gothic Quarter. One curator's choice and up to three honourable mentions will be announced. Curator's choice receives free entry (up to 15 images) for the next PH21 exhibition. Early bird deadline April 20 at reduced rates; final deadline April 27. Special rate for students and unwaged (€15–€20). All photographers 18+ worldwide may enter with original work. Images submitted by email as JPEG, longest side max 1200px. Exhibition June 27 – July 21, 2026.
jury: Zsolt Bátori, Photographer & Philosophy of Art
Borbála Jász, Art Historian & Philosophy of Art
calls.summary: Curated group show on motion in photography. Physical exhibition in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter. Student rates available.

calls.title: Manipulation & Illusion
calls.description: Open call exploring the terrain between what is seen and what is constructed. Seeking work that engages with manipulation and illusion as they relate to perception, belief, identity, and power. Themes include optical, sensory, and spatial illusion; distortion, misdirection, and scale; unreliable memory; propaganda and political persuasion; digital manipulation and curated environments; institutional narratives and manufactured truth; manipulation as artistic method; and altered materials, images, and data. All disciplines welcome — photography, visual art, design, and fine craft. Submissions accepted exclusively through the Co-Ex Collaborative website portal. Selected work featured in a curated online collection. Open worldwide.
calls.summary: Explore perception, belief, identity, and power through illusion and manipulation. All disciplines. Free, open worldwide.
prose: Manipulation & Illusion is an open call from Co-Ex Collaborative for work that engages with the terrain between what is seen and what is constructed. The brief is unusually expansive: applicants can address optical, sensory, and spatial illusion; distortion, misdirection, and scale; unreliable memory; propaganda and political persuasion; digital manipulation and curated environments; institutional narratives and manufactured truth; manipulation as artistic method; or altered materials, images, and data.

The call is interdisciplinary — photography, visual art, design, and fine craft are all eligible. Submissions go through the Co-Ex Collaborative website portal, with one image per applicant. There is no entry fee.

Selected work is featured in a curated online collection on Co-Ex's site. Specific prize structure, jury composition, and historical context aren't published on the call page; the platform appears to operate as a curated online publication rather than a competition with cash awards. The deadline is July 19, 2026.

calls.title: Epson International Pano Awards 2026
calls.description: 17th edition of the world's largest international competition for panoramic photography. Three main categories: Open (professional and amateur, $22/image), Amateur (non-professional photographers earning less than $20,000 from photography, $20/image), and VR/360 ($20/image) — plus a new Aerial category for drone and aircraft images. Total prize pool over US$50,000 including $15,000 in cash prizes. Open category winner receives a package exceeding $11,000. Early-bird entries close June 22 at standard rates; late entries accepted through July 13 at higher rates. Photographers who enter during the early-bird period are eligible for the $1,000 Curator's Award. Images must be panoramic format with aspect ratio greater than 2:1 (or less than 1:2 for verticals). All photographic capture methods welcome including digital, film, and stitched panoramas. Open worldwide.
calls.summary: World's largest panoramic photography competition. $50K+ prizes incl. $15K cash. New Aerial category. Open, Amateur, VR/360.
prose: The Epson International Pano Awards is the world's largest competition exclusively for panoramic photography, now in its 17th edition. The prize is sponsored by Epson with major presence in Australia and Southeast Asia.

Three competition divisions run in parallel: Open (professional and amateur photographers, $22 per image), Amateur (restricted to non-professionals earning less than $20,000 annually from photography, $20 per image), and VR/360 ($20 per image). The 2026 cycle introduces a new Aerial category for drone and aircraft images, alongside the existing Nature/Landscapes and Built Environment subcategories.

The total prize pool exceeds US$50,000, with US$15,000 in direct cash. The Open category first prize is a package valued over $11,000. Early-bird entries (closing June 22) are eligible for the additional $1,000 Curator's Award; final-deadline entries (closing July 13) cost slightly more per image.

Submissions must meet the panoramic format requirement: an aspect ratio greater than 2:1 horizontally, or less than 1:2 vertically. All photographic capture methods are welcome — digital, film, and stitched panoramas. AI-generated work is not accepted.

The 2026 jury comprises Bill Bailey, Aaron Spence, Dan Zafra, Jacky Lee, Daniel Kordan, Abe Blair, Anette Mossbacher, and Jennifer Renwick. Eligibility is open worldwide. Results announced October 2026.

calls.title: REMEDY Photo Festival — Open Call 2026
calls.description: Photography festival focused on health, care, lived experience, and representation. Seeking photographic work exploring health in its broadest sense — physical, mental, chronic, invisible, communal, or systemic. Welcomes personal stories, portraiture, documentary, photojournalism, and fine art photography. Particularly interested in work by photographers with lived experience of long-term health conditions. Selected artists included in curated group exhibition at a photography gallery in Lincoln, with additional venues across Lincolnshire. No entry fee and no cost to exhibit — printing and display costs covered by the festival. Exhibition June 1–30, 2026. Past featured photographers include Anthony Luvera and JA Mortram.
calls.summary: Free festival exploring health — physical, mental, chronic, invisible. Lincoln, UK. Print and display costs covered.

calls.title: SQUARE Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Challenging photographers to compose within the square format — the most iconic and persistent format in photography. All photographic genres welcome including portraiture, landscape, documentary, architecture, and conceptual work. Twelve images selected for three-month exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 14×14 framing, and custom matting. Open worldwide to all skill levels. Exhibition August 1 – October 31, 2026.
jury: Holly Hart, Conceptual Fine Art Photographer & Decode Gallery Founder
calls.summary: Square format photography — all genres. Pro printing and museum framing included. Three-month exhibition in Tucson, AZ.
prose: SQUARE is Decode Gallery's themed exhibition for photography composed within the square format — Decode treats square as both a constraint and a tradition (Hasselblad, Rolleiflex, Polaroid SX-70, Instagram), inviting photographers to engage with the format across genres rather than treat it as a separate style.

All photographic genres are welcome: portraiture, landscape, documentary, architecture, conceptual, abstract. Twelve photographs are selected for the three-month physical exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson, Arizona, running August 1 through October 31, 2026.

What's unusual: the gallery covers all professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 14×14 inch framing, and custom 7×7 inch mats. The artist provides only the high-resolution JPEG. Prints are retained in the gallery's flat files for six months after the exhibition for further promotion.

Sales terms split commission 50/50. Selection is by Decode founder Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer with a BA from the Art Institute of Seattle. Entry fee is $40 for up to 10 images. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. The 2026 deadline is June 13; selected artists are notified within two weeks.

calls.title: HOME
calls.description: Exploring the multifaceted nature of home — as feeling, memory, sanctuary, physical space, heritage, or identity. Photographers invited to capture domestic spaces, loved ones, landscapes, or personal belonging. At least 26 images selected for exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 22×22 white framing and custom matting. Open worldwide to all skill levels. Exhibition June 6 – 27, 2026.
jury: Holly Hart, Conceptual Fine Art Photographer & Decode Gallery Founder
calls.summary: Exploring the multifaceted nature of home — feeling, memory, sanctuary, heritage. Pro printing and museum framing in Tucson, AZ.

calls.title: Cumberland Valley Photographers 2026
calls.org: Washington County Museum of Fine Arts
calls.description: Annual juried photography exhibition at the Washington County Museum of Fine Arts, this year celebrating contemporary perspectives as the nation approaches its 250th anniversary. Photographers explore history, identity, place, and civic life through four themes: Unfinished Revolutions, Power of Place, Tell Everyone's Story, and American Experiment. Respond literally or metaphorically through documentary, conceptual, figurative, or abstract approaches. All photographic processes accepted. Submissions open April 1–30, 2026. Selected work exhibited June 20 – October 11, 2026. Open to photographers from Maryland, Virginia, West Virginia, Pennsylvania, and Washington, DC.
calls.summary: Juried museum exhibition on America's 250th anniversary themes. Open to MD, VA, WV, PA, DC photographers. $3K+ in cash prizes.

calls.title: UNSTAGED Journal — Issue 02: Eerie
calls.description: Second issue of UNSTAGED, an independent photography journal dedicated to lens-based inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity. Issue 02, guest curated by Karla Guerrero (Mexico City-based photographer, curator, and editor active in the contemporary photography scene), explores the theme Eerie — quiet disturbance, a poetics of phantasmagoria where images silently evoke meaning. The eerie as the fleeting suggestion that something unnameable lingers just beneath what we think we see. Something quietly disturbing. Submit 5–10 photographs as JPG files (long edge 2000px) with artist statement and bio. Upload work to Google Drive and send the link to reach@arek-ratai.com. Name files: Name_Series_Title_01. Free entry, free print publication for selected photographers.
calls.summary: Free indie photography journal on authenticity. Theme: Eerie. Guest curated by Karla Guerrero. Print publication.

calls.title: Canon Female Photojournalist Grant 2026
calls.description: 26th edition of the grant awarded in partnership with Canon, supporting female photojournalists pursuing long-term documentary projects. Winner receives €8,000 to support completion of an existing project or facilitate the making of a new one. Winning project exhibited at the Visa pour l'Image festival in Perpignan, France, September 2026. Open to professional female photojournalists worldwide, no age or nationality restrictions. Free entry. Winner selected in June by a jury of industry experts. Application window: March 18 – May 19, 2026.
calls.summary: €8,000 grant for female photojournalists. 26th edition with Canon. Long-term documentary projects. Exhibited at Perpignan.

calls.title: A Black Perspective: Celebrating the Voice & Vision
calls.description: Exhibition celebrating diverse narratives by Black photographers exploring resilience, heritage, joy, identity, and extraordinary aspects of Black life. Various photographic styles welcome including alternative practices and collage work. Juried by Arnika Dawkins, fine art photographer and founder of the Arnika Dawkins Gallery in Atlanta, specializing in imagery by and of African Americans. Selected work exhibited May 21 – June 19, 2026 at PhotoSC gallery, 918 Lady Street, Columbia, SC. Work must be printed 8x10" to 16x20", framed, and ready to hang.
jury: Arnika Dawkins, Fine Art Photographer & Gallery Founder
calls.summary: For Black photographers exploring resilience, heritage, joy, and identity. Exhibition in Columbia, SC. Juried by Arnika Dawkins.

calls.title: ANIMAL LIFE
calls.description: International juried photography exhibition celebrating the complexity and individuality of animals. Photographers invited to explore animal subjects with curiosity, empathy, and imagination — companion animals, wildlife, insects, and sea life through observation, environmental portraiture, documentary, or experimental approaches. Welcomes diverse perspectives on human-animal relationships. All lens-based photographic and lens-based art practices welcome, including black and white, color, traditional and non-traditional processes. Images showcasing violence or inhumane treatment will not be considered.
calls.summary: Exploring animal subjects with curiosity, empathy, and imagination. All lens-based work welcome. Minneapolis.

calls.title: FFSP 2026 — Italian Photographers Open Call
calls.org: Italian Cultural Institute of São Paulo
calls.description: Open call for Italian photographers as part of the São Paulo Photography Festival 2026, organized by the Italian Cultural Institute of São Paulo. Fifteen photographers will be selected for a free exhibition in May 2026 as part of the festival's official programme. One finalist will receive a round-trip flight between Brazil and Italy and official participation in FFSP 2026, fostering cultural and professional exchange between the two countries. Open to Italian citizens of legal age residing in Brazil or Italy. Submit 1 to 5 photographs on any theme of your choice.
jury: Margherita Marziali, Vice-Director, Italian Cultural Institute of São Paulo
Lillo Teodoro Guarneri, Director & Cultural Attaché, Italian Cultural Institute of São Paulo
João Kulcsár, Director, São Paulo Photography Festival
calls.summary: Free exhibition in São Paulo for Italian photographers in Brazil/Italy. Winner receives round-trip airfare.

calls.title: Delfina Foundation — Latin America & Caribbean Residency 2026
calls.description: Twelve-week fully funded residency at the Delfina Foundation in London, supported by Jorge M. Pérez and El Espacio 23. Open to visual artists based in Latin America, the Caribbean, and related diasporic communities in the United States. Artists from Chile, Peru, Ecuador, Brazil, and Argentina are not eligible for this cycle (these countries received dedicated residencies in prior years). Two artists will be selected from this call: one for the autumn 2026 residency (September 21 – December 13) and one for the winter 2027 residency (January 5 – March 25). Apply via Cognito Forms with completed application form — read the Guidance Notes document before applying.
calls.summary: Fully funded 12-week residency in London for Latin American/Caribbean artists. Excludes Chile, Peru, Ecuador, Brazil, Argentina.

calls.title: MACK — Debut Photography Book Submissions
calls.description: MACK's annual submission window for first-time photobook authors. Founded by Michael Mack (former Managing Director of Steidl) in 2010, MACK is one of the most prestigious art and photography publishers in the world, releasing approximately 40 books per year with artists including Robert Adams, Alec Soth, and Wolfgang Tillmans. This window is specifically for artists who have not previously had a book published — seeking emerging voices and experimental approaches to the book form. Submit a PDF draft sequence and completed submissions form via email during the May 1–31 window only. No WeTransfer, Dropbox, or download links accepted. Email subject line: 'Submission: Debut Photography Book'. Response within one month after the window closes.
calls.summary: MACK's window for first-time photobook authors. One of the world's most prestigious photography publishers.

calls.title: MACK — Photography Submissions
calls.description: MACK's annual photography submission window. One of the world's most prestigious art and photography publishers, founded by Michael Mack in 2010 and based in London. This window seeks photobook projects that expand visual vocabulary and challenge expectations of photography's potential, with a special interest in voices and perspectives that are often underrepresented in the photobook landscape. Submit a PDF draft sequence and completed submissions form via email during the June 1–30 window only. No WeTransfer, Dropbox, or download links accepted. Email subject line: 'Submission: Photography'. Response within one month after the window closes.
calls.summary: MACK's annual photography window. Prioritizes underrepresented voices in the photobook landscape.
prose: MACK is a London-based independent photobook publisher founded by Michael Mack in 2010. The publisher operates several imprints — MACK, SPBH Editions, A24, the Judd Foundation imprint, and Important Flowers — and has become one of the more closely-watched contemporary photobook publishers internationally.

MACK accepts submissions in dedicated thematic windows rather than rolling submissions, with each window edited by a different team member. Two photography-specific windows run in 2026: the Debut Photography Book window (May 1–31, 2026), edited by Michael Mack and Iman Hakimi, restricted to artists with no previously published books — they look for experimental approaches to the book form. The Photography window (June 1–30, 2026), edited by Morgan Crowcroft-Brown, is open to both established and emerging photographers, with stated focus on underrepresented voices and expanded visual vocabulary.

Each submission consists of a single PDF (a draft sequence of the project) plus a completed submissions form, sent to submissions@mackbooks.co.uk with the subject line "Submission: Photography." WeTransfer, Dropbox, and other download links are not accepted. The publisher commits to responding within one month of each window's deadline.

MACK does not provide feedback on rejected submissions. From acceptance to publication, the publisher notes "it typically takes between one and two years to develop and prepare a book for publication" — submission is the beginning of a long collaborative process rather than an immediate decision.

calls.title: Graz Residency for International Photographers (GRIP) 2026
calls.description: One-month residency for early-career photographers and lens-based artists in Graz, Austria. Fifth edition of GRIP, a joint initiative by Camera Austria and Kulturvermittlung Steiermark. Resident works on an ongoing project or develops new work, with access to Camera Austria's 11,000+ volume study library. Residency concludes with a presentation in Camera Austria's exhibition and library space. Open to international early-career artists working with photography and/or lens-based arts. Apply by email with informal statement of purpose and PDF portfolio.
calls.summary: One-month residency in Graz for early-career photographers. €1,000 stipend.

calls.title: Hidden Narratives Residency 2026
calls.description: Year-long residency engaging with the Royal Geographical Society's historic photographic collection of over one million pieces spanning 1845–1945. Artists explore materials relating to environment and humanitarian themes, developing work examining hidden narratives, loss, and human impact. Includes three research and presentation visits to the UK, a talk at Summit Photo 2026 (July 17–19), and an exhibition at Summit Photo 2027. In partnership with the Royal Geographical Society and the Italian Cultural Institute in London. Open to Italian visual artists, photographers, or practitioners with archive research experience, aged 18+, proficient in English.
jury: Danit Ariel, Artist, Writer & Photoworks Curator
Maria Teresa De Palma, Cultural Attaché, Italian Cultural Institute London
Jamie Owen, Curator, Royal Geographical Society
Rocco Venezia, Artist, Curator and Educator
calls.summary: Year-long residency with Royal Geographical Society's 1M+ photo archive (1845–1945). Three UK visits, Summit Photo exhibition. Italian artists only.

calls.title: Marilyn Stafford FotoReportage Award 2026
calls.description: Annual £4,000 grant for professional female photographers working on documentary photo essays that address social, environmental, economic, or cultural issues. Landmark 10th edition, supported by Nikon. Selected work must showcase positive solutions and demonstrate practical engagement with the subject matter. Named after Marilyn Stafford, pioneering documentary photographer. Winner's work exhibited at POST, Brighton & Hove's centre for photography, September 17–20, 2026, and featured on Lenscratch and FotoDocument. Open to female photographers (or those identifying as female) aged 18+ at any career stage, any nationality worldwide. Must have completed at least one prior documentary photo essay and already started the proposed project.
jury: Andrea Bruce, Photojournalist, NOOR Photo Agency co-owner, Nikon Ambassador
Donna De Cesare, Photojournalist, Associate Professor, University of Texas at Austin
Nina Emett, Director of FotoDocument, Documentary Photographer, Curator
Neo Ntsoma, Photojournalist, Founder of Neo Ntsoma Productions
Isabella Franceschini, 2024 Marilyn Stafford FotoReportage Award winner
calls.summary: £4,000 grant for female documentary photographers. 10th edition, supported by Nikon. Free entry. Exhibition at POST Brighton.

calls.title: Inge Morath Award 2026
calls.description: Annual award supporting women and nonbinary photographers under 30 working on long-term documentary projects. Administered by the Magnum Foundation in cooperation with Magnum Photos and the Inge Morath Estate. The recipient receives $7,500 and one finalist receives $1,000 to support completion of their project. Selected by the full membership of Magnum Photos during their Annual General Meeting, alongside the Inge Morath Estate and the Executive Director of the Magnum Foundation. Named after Austrian-born Magnum photographer Inge Morath (1923–2002). Now in its 25th year.
calls.summary: $7,500 grant for women/nonbinary photographers under 30. Long-term documentary project. 25th year. Selected by Magnum Photos membership.

calls.title: Women in Nature — Artist's Commission
calls.description: Photographic commission by Tóchar Midlands Wetland Restoration and Photo Museum Ireland highlighting the work of women in nature restoration in Ireland. €15,000 commission (including €3,000 travel bursary) for a single artist to create a series of 12 portraits of women in nature, together with photographs of the habitat they are working to restore. Outputs include exhibitions, community conversations, and a publication. Open to artists resident on the island of Ireland working in photography or lens-based media. Judged on creativity and originality (25%), technical skill and execution (20%), impact and storytelling (15%), and track record (10%). Co-financed by the EU Just Transition Fund and the Government of Ireland.
calls.summary: €15,000 commission for 12 portraits of women in nature restoration across Ireland. Exhibition + publication.

calls.title: Home
calls.description: Global open call exploring the theme of home — safety, belonging, dignity, identity, and place. In partnership with Fotografiska Emerging and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. Selected works will be exhibited at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day, December 10, 2026. Curated by James Nachtwey and Pauline Benthede (Fotografiska Global VP Artistic Direction). Open to emerging photographers worldwide. 31 artists selected: 1 main image, 10 runner-ups, 20 honorable mentions. All forms of lens-based photography welcome, analog or digital. AI-generated or prompt-based images not accepted.
jury: Pauline Benthede, Global VP Artistic Direction, Fotografiska
Sophia Emmerich, Lead Editor, Fotografiska Emerging Platform
calls.summary: Exploring home — safety, belonging, dignity. Selected works exhibited at the United Nations HQ in New York.
prose: The HOME open call is a joint initiative by Photography 4 Humanity, Fotografiska, and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. The brief is the single word "home" — interpreted across safety, belonging, dignity, identity, memory, loss, and place — and the call is positioned as a human rights project rather than a conventional photography prize.

Selected work is exhibited at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day, December 10, 2026. The exhibition is guest-curated by James Nachtwey, with Pauline Benthede (Fotografiska's Global VP of Artistic Direction) and Sophia Emmerich (Lead Editor of the Fotografiska Emerging Platform) joining selection.

The selection structure has three tiers: one Main Image, ten Runners-up, and twenty Honorable Mentions — 31 photographers in total. Submissions are limited to three images per applicant. Only lens-based photography is accepted (analog or digital); AI-generated or prompt-based images are explicitly excluded.
There is no entry fee. The call is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over, with explicit emphasis on emerging artists. The deadline is July 12, 2026.

calls.title: Exibart Street Photography Contest — 5th Edition
calls.description: Fifth edition of the international street photography contest by Exibart Street, Italy's leading contemporary art magazine. Two categories: Best Single Photo (€10) and Best Series of 3–9 images (€49). Winners receive a Leica Q3 or Xiaomi 17 Ultra with Leica lenses, plus interviews and editorial coverage across the Exibart network. Sponsored by Leica Camera. Open to photographers worldwide.
jury: Alan Schaller, Photographer, Co-founder Street Photography International (President)
Biba Giacchetti, Curator & Communication Strategist, Founder Sudest57 & Orion57
Andrea Pacella, Director Global Marketing & Communication, Leica Camera AG
Eolo Perfido, Creative Director & Leica Akademie Instructor, Editorial Director Exibart Street
Barbara Di Maio, Photographer & Researcher, Co-founder Women in Street Italy
Francesca Tiboni, Photographer, Co-founder Women in Street Italy
calls.summary: International street contest by Italy's leading art magazine. Leica Q3 grand prize. Five categories.
prose: The Exibart Street Photography Contest is run by Exibart Street, the photography arm of Italy's contemporary art magazine Exibart, with Leica Camera as main sponsor. The 2026 cycle is the contest's 5th edition. Submissions are split into two categories — Best Single Photo and Best Series — with separate fee structures: €10 for a single image, €49 for a series of 3 to 9 images.

Top prizes are camera hardware: a Leica Q3 (full-frame compact, fixed 28mm Summilux lens) and a Xiaomi 17 Ultra equipped with Leica-branded lenses. Selected photographers also receive editorial coverage across the Exibart network — interviews, features in the magazine, and inclusion in the contest's online gallery. Submissions are open worldwide to photographers aged 18 or over.

The jury is led by president Alan Schaller, the British photographer and co-founder of Street Photography International, alongside Biba Giacchetti (curator, founder of Sudest57 and Orion57), Andrea Pacella (Leica Camera AG, Global Marketing & Communication), Eolo Perfido (Editorial Director of Exibart Street and Leica Akademie instructor), Barbara Di Maio and Francesca Tiboni (co-founders of Women in Street Italy), and Uros Gorgone (Exibart General Manager). Submissions close October 15, 2026.

calls.title: RESTART2026
calls.description: International photography competition and exhibition for photographers starting their careers or reconsidering their creative direction with new work. Submit a series of 10–20 photographs created after 2021 that has not been fully exhibited or published. 10 finalists exhibit at Prospekto gallery in Vilnius. Top 3 winners receive individual exhibitions at Vilnius Photography Gallery the following year with partial production support. Printed catalogue for finalists. Featured on photography.lt and screened at NIDA Meeting Photography symposium in September.
jury: Gytis Skudžinskas, Artist, Book Artist & Curator
calls.summary: For photographers starting careers or reconsidering direction. 10-20 new photographs. Top 3 win solo exhibition in Vilnius.

calls.title: DPPF 2026 Sports Photography Grants
calls.description: Grants supporting emerging and early-career sports photographers with fewer than 3 years cumulative paid professional sports photography experience. Seven photographers receive $5,000 each for career development plus expenses-paid trip to the Sports Photography Gathering (September 16–18, 2026). Up to 3 winners eligible for year-long mentorship with Advisory Board members. Up to 3 additional applicants receive $2,500 Development Grants. Open worldwide except countries under active US sanctions.
calls.summary: Seven $5,000 grants for emerging sports photographers plus mentorship. Up to 3 additional $2,500 grants.

calls.title: Bowness Photography Prize 2026
calls.description: Australia's richest photography prize, now in its 21st year. Open to Australian citizens or permanent residents (12+ months). Winner receives $50,000 AUD and acquisition into MAPh's permanent collection. Two Honourable Mentions receive $2,500 each. Wai Tang Commissioning Award of $10,000 for a future exhibition. People's Choice Award of $5,000. Finalists exhibited at MAPh gallery. Accepts still photo-based media including analogue and digital photography produced within the past year. Up to 3 works per $55 entry. AI permitted only if not the substantial or overriding input. Entries open April 16, 2026.
calls.summary: Australia's richest photography prize. $50,000 AUD winner. 21st year. Australian citizens/residents only.
prose: The Bowness Photography Prize is Australia's richest photography prize, awarded annually by the Museum of Australian Photography (MAPh) at Wheelers Hill, Victoria. The 2026 cycle is the 21st edition. The prize is named for William and Sandra Bowness, longtime supporters of the museum.

Cash prizes are substantial: a $50,000 AUD main prize plus acquisition of the winning work into MAPh's permanent collection. Two Honourable Mentions receive $2,500 each. The Wai Tang Commissioning Award provides $10,000 toward a future MAPh exhibition. The People's Choice Award is $5,000.

Eligibility is restricted to Australian citizens and permanent residents of at least 12 months' standing. Submissions are limited to still photo-based media, including analogue and digital photography, produced within the past year. AI is permitted only if it is not the substantial or overriding input — fully AI-generated work is excluded.
Each $55 AUD entry covers up to 3 works. Finalists are exhibited at MAPh gallery. The 2026 application window opens April 16; the deadline is June 14, with the winner announced September 17, 2026.

calls.title: Flanelle Print No. 47 — July 2026
calls.description: Montreal-based fashion and arts magazine (est. 2012) accepting submissions for Print No. 47, publishing July 2026. Open to artists, photographers, and designers worldwide. Selected work featured in quarterly print and digital magazine with international distribution. Two-phase review process. Work must be unpublished and exclusive to Flanelle. Paid upgrade options available for cover placement and priority publishing.
calls.summary: Montreal fashion and arts magazine. Quarterly print and digital with international distribution. Est. 2012.
prose: Flanelle Magazine is a Montreal-based fashion photography, arts, and culture publication, founded in 2012. The magazine publishes quarterly in January, April, July, and October, with each issue produced in both print and digital formats and distributed internationally.

Print No. 47 publishes July 2026. Submissions are accepted from artists, photographers, and designers worldwide. Each photo set must include a minimum of 10 photographs following the issue theme and mood board. Editorials must be unpublished and exclusive to Flanelle.

Standard print submissions are free. Optional paid upgrades are available for cover contests, advertorial placement, or priority publishing. The magazine uses a two-phase review process, with selected artists notified individually after editorial review.

Selected work appears in the quarterly print issue and digital edition with international distribution, plus possible social media exposure across the magazine's channels. Selected artists receive digital versions of their published spreads on request. Submissions go through Kavyar (kavyar.com/flanellemag); the Print No. 47 deadline is June 1, 2026.

calls.title: Embracing Our Differences 2027 Outdoor Exhibition
