calls.description: International outdoor juried exhibition in its 23rd year. 50 selected artworks are displayed as billboard-sized panels (16 ft × 12.5 ft) in public parks in Sarasota and St. Petersburg, Florida, from January to April 2027. Three awards: $2,000 Best-in-Show Adult, $2,000 Best-in-Show Student, $2,000 People's Choice. Work must reflect themes of diversity, inclusion, kindness, and respect. Accepts photography, painting, drawing, mixed media, digital art. Horizontal orientation only. No limit on entries per artist. 150-word artist statement required. Over 5.2 million visitors since 2004. AI-generated work not accepted.
calls.summary: 50 artworks displayed as billboard-sized panels in Florida parks. Themes: diversity, inclusion, kindness.
prose: Embracing Our Differences is an international juried public-art exhibition that has run annually since 2004, now in its 23rd year. Selected artworks are displayed as billboard-sized panels — 16 feet by 12.5 feet — in public parks in Sarasota and St. Petersburg, Florida, from January through April. Since the program's founding the exhibitions have drawn over 5.2 million visitors collectively, making it one of the most heavily-visited outdoor art shows in the United States.

Fifty artworks are selected per cycle. Three cash awards of $2,000 each are given: Best-in-Show Adult, Best-in-Show Student, and People's Choice. The brief asks for work that reflects diversity, inclusion, kindness, and respect, with the panel format favoring strong horizontal compositions readable at billboard scale.

Eligible media span photography, painting, drawing, mixed media, and digital art — work must be horizontal in orientation, and AI-generated submissions are not accepted. There is no fee, no limit on entries per artist, and a 150-word artist statement is required.
Submissions go through Zealous. The 2027 cycle deadline is July 1, 2026, with results announced in early fall.

calls.title: Night Aesthetics
calls.description: Open call exploring the visual world of the night. Looking for works that engage with light, movement, atmosphere, intimacy, and the energy that appears when the day lets go. Whether captured on a crowded dance floor, in a quiet street, or somewhere in between. Welcomes lens-based photography in all forms including analog and digital. Three winners each receive €2,500 and feature on the Fotografiska Emerging platform. In partnership with Jägermeister.
jury: Atiba Jefferson, Staff Photographer Thrasher Magazine & Canon Explorer of Light
Julia Schoierer, Portrait & Street Photographer, Berlin
calls.summary: Exploring the visual world of the night — light, movement, atmosphere. Three winners receive €2,500 each.

calls.title: The 2026 Lumen Prize
calls.description: Leading international award for art created with technology, now in its 15th year. Three categories: Legacy Futures, Systems & Structures, and Experiential Innovation, each with a $5,000 prize. The Jury also selects one Gold Award Winner receiving $15,000. Works may include film, photography, AI-generated art, interactive installations, VR experiences, and more. Finalists announced August, winners announced November. Awards ceremony at Kunstsilo Museum in Norway.
jury: Melanie Lenz, Digital Curator, V&A Museum
Rachel Falconer, Senior Lecturer & Head of Digital Arts Computing, Goldsmiths University London
Myriam Achard, Chief New Media Partnerships & PR, PHI
Christiane Paul, Adjunct Curator Digital Art, Whitney Museum
Ulrich Schrauth, Artistic Director, UBS Digital Art Museum
Annie Bicknell, Curator Public Programmes, Tate
calls.summary: Leading award for art created with technology. 15th year. $15,000 Gold Award. Categories include AI, VR, and more.

calls.title: Nest — Group Exhibition
calls.description: Group exhibition exploring how creative practice nurtures wellbeing, inspires reflection, or aids recovery. Open call for art created in response to lived experience of mental health, disability, or health journey. All mediums welcome including photography, painting, film, sculpture, ceramics, poetry, and installation. Curated by photographic artist Livvy Eden. Exhibition runs 22 May – 6 June 2026 at 103 Walcot Street, Bath. Selected artists asked for £25 participation donation.
calls.summary: Exploring how creative practice nurtures wellbeing, aids recovery. Open to lived experience of mental health. Bath, UK.

calls.title: Michael P. Smith Fund for Documentary Photography 2025
calls.description: Annual grant honoring legendary New Orleans documentary photographer Michael P. Smith. Awards cash prizes and exhibition opportunities to Gulf Coast photographers whose work combines artistic excellence and a sustained commitment to a cultural documentary project. Open to photographers residing in Gulf Coast states: Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, and Florida. Subject matter not limited to Gulf Coast region. Grant winner receives $3,000, PhotoNOLA Portfolio Review access, NOPA Palladium membership, and exhibition. Two honorable mentions receive Portfolio reviews and membership. Top 10 finalists listed on NOPA website. Winner donates two prints to NOPA permanent collection.
jury: Alyssa Ortega Coppelman, Photography Consultant & Photo Editor
calls.summary: Annual grant for Gulf Coast photographers. $3,000 winner prize, PhotoNOLA Portfolio Review, and exhibition.

calls.title: Camille Lepage Award 2026
calls.org: Association Camille Lepage – On est ensemble
calls.description: Annual €8,000 award supporting a photojournalist committed to a long-term reporting project. Established by the family of Camille Lepage, the photojournalist killed while reporting in the Central African Republic in 2014. Funded for the tenth year by the SAIF (Société des Auteurs des Arts Visuels et de l'Image Fixe). The award helps a photographer carry out and complete a reporting project already under way. Open to professional photojournalists with no restriction on age, gender, or nationality. Award presented in September 2026 at the International Festival of Photojournalism Visa pour l'Image-Perpignan. The winning report must be completed within one year so that it can be presented at the 2027 festival as an exhibition or evening show.
calls.summary: €8,000 prize for a photojournalist on a long-term reporting project. Free entry, worldwide. Presented at Visa pour l'Image-Perpignan.

calls.title: Love & Romance Show
calls.description: Online exhibition exploring how love has transformed alongside cultural and societal changes, and how those shifts shape personal experience today. Submit up to 3 images connecting the theme of love and romance. Virtual exhibition launches May 7, 2026.
calls.summary: Online exhibition exploring how love has transformed alongside cultural and societal changes.

calls.title: EDITION 502 — Open Call for Photo Edition
calls.description: Open call for an independent 6×9 photo edition of 12 small photographs. EDITION 502 covers all design, production, and distribution costs. Author receives a percentage of sales. Looking for authors with a clear visual language and comprehensible concept, regardless of education or professional background. Submit 12 photographs with serial character, a cover sheet, and a text (max 2,400 characters).
calls.summary: Independent 6x9 photo edition of 12 small photographs. All production and distribution costs covered.

calls.title: Texture of Light
calls.description: Photography exhibition exploring light as a tactile, physical medium. Submit images where light feels like a material — surface tension on objects, atmospheric mass in fog or dust, architecture of shadow, or abstract luminescence through long exposures and macro work. Selected images will be printed and displayed matted and framed at Western Market in Washington, DC. Exhibition opens May 2, 2026.
calls.summary: Exploring light as a tactile, physical medium — surface tension, atmospheric mass, architecture of shadow. Washington, DC.

calls.title: Anja Niedringhaus Courage in Photojournalism Award 2026
calls.description: Award honoring courageous, high-impact photojournalism by women, nonbinary, and gender-diverse creatives. Submit 12 photographs (6 from 2024–2026, 6 from broader career) plus a 500-word statement. Open to women, nonbinary, and gender non-conforming photojournalists working full-time in journalism. Self-nomination or third-party nomination accepted. Named after Pulitzer Prize-winning photographer Anja Niedringhaus (1965–2014).

calls.summary: Honoring courageous photojournalism by women, nonbinary, and gender-diverse creatives. Named after Pulitzer winner.

calls.title: LT5 Alternative Photography Show
calls.description: Open call for photographers working in alternative photography — including toy and plastic cameras, Polaroid, pinhole, photograms, and other alternative processes. Submit up to 2 works for exhibition at KALEID Gallery in San Jose, CA. Opening reception May 1 during South First Fridays Art Walk. Exhibition runs May 1–29, 2026. Contact curator via DM or email for submission details.
calls.summary: Toy cameras, Polaroid, pinhole, photograms, and alternative processes. Exhibition at KALEID Gallery, San Jose, CA.

calls.title: Artphilein Open Call 2026
calls.description: Open call for photographers exploring adolescence from an internal perspective — digital culture, identity negotiation, and contemporary pressures experienced by young people. Submit a single PDF with 10–20 images. Winner receives a solo exhibition at Artphilein Library in Autumn 2026, publication in Artphilein Dossier, and CHF 1,000 cash award.
jury: Caterina De Pietri, Curator, Artphilein Foundation
calls.summary: Exploring adolescence — digital culture, identity, contemporary pressures. Solo exhibition and CHF 1,000 award.

calls.title: L'Image Satellite 2026
calls.description: Open call for photographers and visual artists working with contemporary still image practices including documentary, experimental, vernacular, and hybrid image forms. Selected artists exhibit at L'Image Satellite festival in Nice, September–October 2026. Artists receive €500 presentation fee, round-trip artwork transport, accommodation, and travel. Submit up to 20 JPEG images via online form and email.
calls.summary: Selected artists exhibit in Nice, Sep-Oct 2026. €500 honorarium, transport, accommodation, and travel covered.

calls.title: Fabula Works — Duo/Solo Show in Rome
calls.description: Inaugural open call for two photographers to exhibit in a five-week show at Millepiani Gallery in Rome. No thematic restrictions — submit 10–25 photographs as a cohesive series or curated selection. All printing and promotional costs fully covered. Opening reception June 26, 2026. Exhibition runs June 26–July 31, 2026.
calls.summary: Two photographers exhibit at Millepiani Gallery in Rome. No thematic restrictions. All costs covered.

calls.title: Rarefied Light 2026
calls.description: Annual statewide juried exhibition with juror Nevada Wier (National Geographic, Smithsonian). Submit 1–20 images of any photographic form except AI-generated work. Selected work travels to galleries in Anchorage, Fairbanks, Juneau, and Cordova from October 2026. Includes three-day workshop (August 14–16) on color, light, action, and pattern in image-making.
calls.summary: Statewide juried exhibition with Nevada Wier (Nat Geo). Travels to four Alaska galleries from October 2026.
prose: Rarefied Light is the Alaska Photographic Center's annual statewide juried exhibition. The 2026 cycle is juried by Nevada Wier, a photographer whose work has appeared in National Geographic, Smithsonian, and Getty Images. The exhibition is restricted to Alaska-based photographers — Rarefied Light is one of the few photography prizes structured specifically around the state.

Selected work tours four Alaska galleries from October 2026 onward, traveling between Anchorage, Fairbanks, Juneau, and Cordova. The traveling format means accepted work reaches audiences across Alaska's geographically dispersed cities — a different kind of exhibition reach than a single venue stop.

The 2026 cycle includes a three-day workshop with the juror on August 14–16, 2026: "Seeing Photographically — Color, Light, Action, Pattern," instruction on converting visual observation into compelling photographs. Workshop fees are $250 (APC member), $300 (non-member), or $275 (member renewal plus workshop). A jury lecture takes place August 13.

Submissions accept up to 20 images of any photographic form except AI-generated work. Entry fees are $15 to $30. Eligibility is restricted to Alaska residents. Submissions go through CaFÉ; the 2026 deadline is June 10 at 10 PM AST, with results in July.

calls.title: Prix Mustaqbal 2026 — Momentum
calls.description: Annual competition promoting emerging contemporary creation. Open to artists aged 18–35, Moroccan or foreign residents in Morocco, working in drawing, painting, installation, photography, or sound art. No thematic constraints. Approximately 15 finalists exhibited at Artorium in Casablanca. Winner receives artist residency at Jardin Rouge and duo-shows in Paris and Casablanca.
calls.summary: Emerging artists 18-35, Moroccan or foreign residents in Morocco. Winner receives Jardin Rouge residency.

calls.title: No Place Art — Edition Two: MATERIALITY
calls.description: International open call for artists working in printmaking, painting and mixed media. 80 artists selected for 10-day exhibition at The Handbag Factory in London. 30+ awards from 19 awarding bodies including purchase awards up to £1,000, artist residencies, solo and group exhibitions, mentoring, editorial features, materials vouchers, and workshops.

calls.title: 59 Rivoli — Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: 6-month artist residency at the iconic 59 Rivoli in the heart of Paris, a former squat turned official artist residence hosting 30 artists with free open studios visited by the public. Open to visual artists and sculptors of all ages, internationally. Residencies begin May 2026.
calls.summary: 6-month residency at iconic 59 Rivoli in Paris — former squat turned official artist residence. Free open studios.

calls.title: LensCulture Critics' Choice 2026
calls.description: Global competition where 20 leading photography critics and curators each select 3 photographers. Up to 60 winners featured in LensCulture online gallery. calls.title: Analog Sparks — International Film Photography Awards 2026

prose: Analog Sparks is an international competition specifically for film and analog photography, founded by Hossein Farmani (founder of the Lucie Foundation and IPA) and Reka Koti. Submissions are accepted in eight categories: Architecture, Fine Art, Human, Lifestyle, Nature, Photojournalism, Technique, and Zines & Photo Books.

The competition accepts color and black-and-white film, instant film, collodion, alternative techniques, and hybrid analog-digital workflows where the original capture was on film. Purely digital work is not accepted. The main prize is €1,000, and category winners are exhibited at House of Lucie galleries in Athens and Ostuni.

The 2026 jury comprises Barna Erdesz (art director and gallerist), Danial Shah (documentary photographer), Eva Szombat (visual artist), Hossein Farmani (founder), Ibrahim Mursal (visual artist and writer), Kenro Izu (photographer), Kira Krasz (visual artist), Mikkel Horlyck (photojournalist), Mo Laudi (curator), and Wanda Martin (Canon Ambassador).

Entry fees follow a tiered deadline structure with progressively lower discounts: 10% off through January 23, 5% off through March 15, then standard rates through May 15, June 19 (extended), and the final deadline July 31. Eligibility is open to photographers 18 and over worldwide, including students and emerging artists.

prose: The Photography Network is a membership-based academic and curatorial organization for photography scholars, historians, curators, and artists. The PN Awards run two parallel programs: the Book Prize and the Project Grant.

The Book Prize honors innovation in photography scholarship, expression, and distribution. Eligible work includes edited volumes, exhibition catalogs, photobooks, and scholarly monographs — the prize is open to authored or edited work by current Photography Network members. The structure is unusual in that it treats the photobook as scholarship rather than purely as artistic output.

The Project Grant supports emerging scholars, curators, and artists with funds to complete works in progress — publications, articles, exhibitions, or research projects. Both programs require English-language submissions.

The 2026 jury comprises Lucy Gallun (Curator of Photography at MoMA), Ileana L. Selejan (Lecturer at the University of Edinburgh), and Giulia Paoletti (Associate Professor at the University of Virginia). The deadline is June 15, 2026, with results announced December 2026. Specific prize amounts are not published on the awards landing page; applicants should contact the awards coordinator (photographynetworkawards@gmail.com) for current details.

prose: Fotografiska's emerging program is structured around continuous open calls plus rotating themed cycles. The "Foto of the Day" track runs weekly: seven images selected from open submissions, featured on Fotografiska's website and social channels. Themed calls run alongside it, with regional eligibility for some — Sweden-only for the Stockholm shows, Baltics-and-Finland for Tallinn — and global eligibility for others.

Selected work has been shown at Fotografiska's museum locations in Berlin, Stockholm, and Tallinn. The platform doesn't publish guaranteed compensation; outcomes vary by call. Submissions are free, limited to three images per cycle, and AI-generated work is excluded.

The platform's permanent jury includes James Nachtwey and Pauline Benthede, Fotografiska's VP of Artistic Direction. Themed calls bring in additional jurors specific to each theme. The "Home" call is currently open with a July 12, 2026 deadline; "Foto of the Day" remains continuous.

prose: The Deloitte Photo Grant was established in 2023 by Deloitte Italy under the patronage of Fondazione Deloitte ETS, in association with Still Love srl. The grant runs in two parallel tracks: an Open Call for emerging photographers and a Nominations category that brings in invited photographers separately.

The 2026 theme is "Proximities" — investigating new forms of distance in contemporary life (physical, economic, technological, social) and how communities endure despite contemporary pressures. The Open Call is restricted to photographers under 35 years of age.

The Open Call winner receives €25,000 in project funding plus a solo exhibition at Triennale Milano, the major Milan design and contemporary art museum. The parallel Nominations category carries a €50,000 prize. Submission to the Open Call is free.

The 2026 jury, chaired by artistic director Denis Curti, includes Magnum photographers Alec Soth and Bruce Gilden, Suzanne Cotter (Director, Museum of Contemporary Art Australia), Sunyoung Kim (Senior Curator, Hanmi Museum), Bernardino Castro (Director, Portuguese Photography Center), Barbara Ceferin (Owner, Galerija Fotografija), Katarzyna Sagatowska (Curator, Jednostka Gallery), Guido Borsani (Chairman, Italian Deloitte Foundation), and Carlos Idun-Tawiah (the 2025 winner).
Submissions require 10 images. AI-generated work is accepted with mandatory disclosure. Submissions are open March 10 through June 14, 2026; jury voting closes September 6, with results in September.

calls.title: Denis Roussel Award 2026
calls.description: For photographers working with historical and alternative photographic processes including silver gelatin. Submit 7 images and statement. $2,000 main award plus merit awards. Portfolio review prize included.
jury: Christopher James, Professor, Lesley University College of Art and Design
calls.summary: For historical and alternative photographic processes including silver gelatin. $2,000 main award.
prose: The Denis Roussel Award is administered by Rfotofolio, an organization dedicated to showcasing photographers and supporting work in historical photographic processes. The award honors photographer and educator Denis Roussel, who died of cancer in 2017 — Roussel worked across landscapes, portraits, and still life, and the award reflects his belief that "there is beauty everywhere." The prize was established in 2018.

The focus is exclusively historical and alternative photographic processes — silver gelatin, platinum, palladium, gum bichromate, cyanotype, anthotype, salt prints, wet plate collodion, and similar. Inkjet prints are not eligible, and AI-generated work is excluded.

The prize structure is layered: a $2,000 main award; two $500 Merit Awards; a $500 Rfotofolio Merit Award; the Christopher James Award (a one-on-one portfolio review with the longtime juror); and additional sponsor awards from Bostick & Sullivan and Mark Nelson covering chemistry and equipment.

Past winners include Luther Gerlach (2018), Tina Rowe (2019), Lesha Rodriguez (2020), Diana Bloomfield (2021), Henri Blommers (2022), and Lisa Nebenzahl (2023). Christopher James (Lesley University College of Art and Design) has served as juror from 2020–2024.

There is no entry fee (donations optional). Applications require seven edited images and a written statement of up to two paragraphs. The 2026 cycle runs March 5 through June 27; results announced July 19.

jury: Monica Aguilar Villamarin, Visual Artist & Photo Educator
calls.summary: Celebrating innovative photographic books. Three categories. $3,000 Book of the Year. Open worldwide.
prose: The Lucie Foundation Photo Book Prize is the foundation's annual award for photography in book form. Three categories carry cash prizes: Book of the Year ($3,000, awarded to the publisher), First Book ($2,000, awarded to the photographer), and Self-Published ($2,000, awarded to the photographer). The prize structure reflects how photo books actually get made — recognizing publishers for their craft, debut authors for theirs, and independents for going it alone.

Eligible work spans the full range of contemporary photo publishing: traditionally published books and zines, hand-made and limited editions, exhibition catalogues, photography combined with other media, multi-artist anthologies, and single-artist publications. Books must be published between September 2024 and September 2026 to qualify for the 2026 cycle. There is no submission limit per applicant.

Entry fees are $75 for publishers and $50 for photographers on the first submission, with 20% off subsequent category entries of the same book. Submissions require a completed form and a PDF of the book up to 60MB; individual JPG files used for evaluation must be 72 DPI and under 4MB each. Final deadline is September 15, 2026 (midnight ET); winners are announced in fall 2026.

The eleven-juror panel for 2026 includes photographers Martin Schoeller, Jamel Shabazz, Lele Saveri, and Paul Baldonado; editors Merve Arkunlar (212 Magazine) and Elizabeth Krist; and curators Eleni Mouzakiti, Yumi Goto, Emmanuel Iduma (Tender Photos), and Monica Aguilar Villamarin.

prose: Nes is a 1- to 6-month residency in Skagaströnd, a small fishing town on Iceland's north coast. The program is deliberately interdisciplinary: the same campus hosts visual artists, writers, musicians, dancers, and researchers, with discipline-specific spaces — a research library for writers, the BioPol dance studio, a ceramics workshop, and access to the local music school. Visual artists receive an individual workspace inside a shared open-plan studio.

The fall 2026 cycle covers September, October, and November; private bedrooms and shared common areas are included. Monthly cost is €850. The application fee is $15 and submissions go through SlideRoom; selection prioritizes "curiosity and experimentation" over conventional credentials. Nes does not currently offer scholarships or stipends — artists fund their own stay.

The location is remote: Skagaströnd has a population of about 500, and the residency draws on that isolation as part of its program. Past residents have used the time for self-directed projects, with optional artistic and cultural exchange built into the schedule.

prose: The Hopper Prize runs twice a year, awarding six grants per cycle: two at $4,500 and four at $1,000. Founded in 2018, it awards $26,000 annually across both cycles. There's no medium restriction — recent recipients have worked in photography, painting, sculpture, video, performance, and installation. The prize is open to all career stages and accepts direct applications only; nominations aren't part of the process.

Beyond the cash awards, 30 artists per cycle are archived at hopperprize.org with biographies and links to their websites. That's 60 artists per year placed on the prize's site alongside winners — being shortlisted is roughly five times more likely than winning, and the archive itself functions as a form of recognition.

The current juror is Misa Jeffereis, an assistant curator at the Contemporary Art Museum St. Louis, a non-collecting institution with a contemporary program. The juror rotates each cycle. Application fee is $40. Deadline May 12, 2026; results announced August 28, 2026.

prose: JUST ADD WATER is a themed open call from Art Fluent, the Boston-based curatorial platform. The brief is the element itself: oceans, rain, rivers, puddles, or even just a hint of blue — work that engages with water as subject matter or as metaphor.

Cash prizes total $1,250: a Best of Show award of $750 and two Director's Choice awards of $250 each. All accepted work is displayed in the online gallery on art-fluent.com. Selection is curated by Creative Director Amy Matteson Neill and an anonymous committee.

Entry fee is $25 for the first work and $10 each additional, up to a maximum of 20 entries per artist. All fine art mediums are accepted: painting, sculpture, photography, video, digital art. AI-generated work is not accepted, and previously exhibited work at Art Fluent is ineligible.

Submissions go through CaFÉ (callforentry.org), which requires a free artist account. Open globally to amateur and professional artists. The 2026 deadline is June 5 (midnight MST), with notifications by July 2.

calls.title: BOTANICALS
calls.org: New York Center for Photographic Arts
calls.description: All photographic processes accepted. Winners receive $4,000 cash, online gallery feature, catalog publication. New York, NY.
calls.summary: All photographic processes accepted. $4,000 cash prize, online gallery, and catalogue. New York.
prose: BOTANICALS is the New York Center for Photographic Arts (NYC4PA) themed call for photography of plant life — flowers, trees, leaves, vines, fruit, gardens, beaches, windowsills, parks, rainforests. The brief is loose: any photographic process and any setting where vegetation is the subject.

Cash prizes total $4,000 across 10 awards: a Grand Prize of $1,100, three First Prizes of $400, three Second Prizes of $325, and three Third Prizes of $250. Beyond the cash awards, 20 Juror Selections and 20 Honorable Mentions are also recognized — featured in the online gallery and catalog with certificates. The winning image is also featured on the NYC4PA website homepage.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Dan Burkholder, photographer known for pioneering work in HDR and mobile photography techniques. All 2D photographic mediums are accepted: print, transfers, encaustic, black-and-white, color, and experimental techniques.

Entry fee is $40 for the first three images, with $10 each additional and unlimited submissions allowed. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Images that have won NYC4PA prizes in the prior two years are not eligible. Submissions go through SmarterEntry; the 2026 deadline is June 7 at midnight Pacific Time.

calls.title: Snider Prize
calls.org: Museum of Contemporary Photography at Columbia
calls.description: For emerging artists in final year of graduate study. Winner: $3,000; two honorable mentions: $500 each. Acquisitions into MoCP permanent collection.
calls.summary: For emerging artists in final year of graduate study. $3,000 winner. Acquisitions into MoCP permanent collection.
prose: The Snider Prize is administered by the Museum of Contemporary Photography (MoCP) at Columbia College Chicago. The prize was established by Lawrence K. and Maxine Snider to support emerging photographers transitioning from graduate study into professional practice.

Eligibility is restricted to artists in their final year of graduate study in photography or photo-related disciplines. The award structure is one main winner and two honorable mentions: the winner receives $3,000 plus acquisition of the winning work into the MoCP permanent collection; honorable mentions receive $500 each. Acquisition into MoCP's collection is the more durable element of the prize — the museum holds significant photography holdings used in exhibitions and academic research.

Recent winners include Ching-Wei Wang (MFA, Parsons, 2025), Claire Warden (MFA, School of the Art Institute of Chicago, 2024), and Sidian Liu (MFA, Parsons, 2023). The pattern across recent cycles favors candidates from major MFA programs, though the prize is not formally restricted to specific institutions.

Submissions go through JotForm and require 10 images plus supporting materials. Entry fee details and jury composition are not published on the prize landing page. The 2026 deadline is June 12 at 11:59 PM; results announced fall 2026.

calls.title: Evolution Grant
calls.description: Unrestricted $1,000 grant per cycle to individual artist with recognized artistic excellence and demonstrated commitment.
calls.summary: Unrestricted $1,000 grant per cycle for individual artists with recognized artistic excellence.
prose: The Evolution Grant is a recurring unrestricted grant from Art Fluent, the same Boston-based curatorial platform that runs themed open calls like HER.SELF and Manipulation & Illusion. Each grant cycle awards $1,000 to one visual artist with the funds explicitly unrestricted — applicants do not need to propose a specific project, and the grant can support any expense that enhances the artist's ability to make work (materials, studio rent, equipment, time off).

Selection is on the body-of-work submitted rather than a single project pitch. Applications require 5 to 20 pieces, an artist statement, and a bio. The 2025 recipient was Mark Guglielmo. Once awarded, artists cannot reapply.
Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional artists. All fine art mediums are accepted except AI-generated work; copies and instructor-guided pieces are excluded.

The application fee is $35 (non-refundable). Submissions go through CaFÉ (callforentry.org), which requires a free artist account. The June 2026 cycle deadline is June 19, 2026 at midnight MST; results announced by July 31.

calls.description: One-month artist residency in Syracuse, New York, for photographers and image-based media artists worldwide. Light Work has supported over 400 artists through this program since 1975, many achieving international recognition. Twelve to fifteen artists selected annually. Residents receive a $7,500 stipend, a furnished apartment, 24-hour access to state-of-the-art digital and darkroom facilities, and generous staff support. calls.summary: One-month residency in Syracuse for photographers. $7,500 stipend, apartment, 24-hour darkroom/digital access. Published in Contact Sheet.
prose: Light Work is a non-profit photography center in Syracuse, New York, founded in 1973. Its Artist-in-Residence program — running for over five decades and counting more than 400 alumni — is one of the longest-running photography residencies in the United States. Past residents have included photographers who went on to MacArthur Fellowships, museum acquisitions, and major editorial careers; the alumni list is treated as part of the program's identity.

Each cycle, twelve to fifteen artists are selected for a one-month residency at Light Work's facility (316 Waverly Avenue, Syracuse). Residents receive a $7,500 stipend, a furnished apartment near campus, 24-hour access to Light Work's digital lab and darkroom, and on-staff support. Each resident's work is published in Contact Sheet, Light Work's annual publication, with a commissioned essay.

Eligibility is open globally to artists working in photography or image-based media. There is no application fee. The program is in partnership with Autograph ABP and the Darryl Chappell Foundation, which jointly support specific residency lines for British photographers and Black photographers respectively.

Applications are submitted through SlideRoom (with a physical mail option for those who require it). The 2027 cycle deadline is July 1, 2026. The selection committee reviews applications in late fall, with notifications sent in December.

prose: The Arte Laguna Prize was founded in 2006 by Cultural Association MoCA and is now in its 21st edition. The prize is one of Europe's largest cross-disciplinary art competitions, with categories spanning painting, sculpture, installation, photography, video art, performance, virtual and digital art, digital graphics, environmental and land art, urban and street art, and art design.

The main cash prize is €10,000 (subject to 25% withholding tax under Italian law). Beyond cash, 120 finalists exhibit at Arsenale Nord in Venice from November 6 through 29, 2026 — the same Venetian Arsenale site that historically hosts portions of the Venice Biennale. Special prizes additionally include residencies at venues in Venice, Australia, China, Croatia, and Peru, plus gallery exhibitions and corporate commissions.

The 2026 jury comprises seven international curators including Yuko Hasegawa (Curator & Director, 21st Century Museum Kanazawa), Wang Chunchen (Chief Curator, CAFA Art Museum Beijing), Linzi Stauvers (Artistic Director, Ikon Gallery), Hèlio Menezes (curator), Gianluigi Ricuperati (curator and art director), Jemima Kulumba (Co-Founder, WIA), and additional industry-side voices.

Entry fees are tiered by age: artists under 35 pay €97.60, artists 35 and over pay €122. Additional works beyond 5 cost €24.40 each. There is no age limit for entry, and the prize is open to all nationalities and qualifications. The 2026 deadline is June 30; the finalist exhibition opens November 6.

The format is in the name: each work is a "mini print" no larger than 20×20 cm in image and paper dimensions, with the small format chosen to make printmaking accessible across techniques and to scale a large international group exhibition into a manageable space.

The 2026 theme is "Open Sea — Reality, imagination and poetics." All printmaking disciplines are accepted, including traditional techniques (etching, lithography, woodblock, linocut), monotype, and digital prints. Each artist may submit up to three prints.

The main prize pool is €4,000. Selected work is exhibited at the Exhibition Space of the Archive of the Port Authority of Santander from September 11 through December 8, 2026. Entry fees range from €35 to €65 depending on the submission tier.

calls.title: World Cyanotype Day
calls.description: Annual international celebration of the cyanotype process. Submit your cyanotype work to be featured.
calls.summary: Annual international celebration of the cyanotype process. Submit your cyanotype work to be featured.
prose: World Cyanotype Day is an annual celebration of the cyanotype process — a 19th-century alternative photographic technique that uses iron-based salts and UV light to produce prints in distinctive shades of blue. The event was founded in 2015 by AlternativePhotography.com (itself established in 1999) and runs each year on the last Saturday of September. The 2026 cycle covers September 26 through October 2.

Submissions are free and open to anyone working with the process. Each year carries a theme — 2025's was "Cultivating Community," with the 2026 theme to be announced in spring. The format is single-image submissions: 1080px on the longest side, under 2MB, JPEG only (no PNG, TIFF, or HEIC), with filenames structured as "Name Surname, Title, Country.jpg." No nudes; submissions must follow the year's theme.
Selected work is shown across AlternativePhotography.com's gallery, Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, BlueSky, and YouTube channels. There is no cash prize.

The event references Anna Atkins — the first woman to illustrate a photography book, using cyanotypes — as part of its lineage. AlternativePhotography.com is a non-profit, runs the event without sponsor backing, and maintains a substantial educational resource library on cyanotype chemistry, paper preparation, and exposure techniques.

calls.title: World Anthotype Day
calls.description: Annual celebration of plant-based photographic printing processes. Entries open August 1; submission deadline October 31 (last Saturday in October).
calls.summary: Annual celebration of plant-based photographic printing processes. Entries open August through October.
prose: World Anthotype Day is an annual celebration of the anthotype process — a 19th-century photographic technique that uses plant-based emulsions and sunlight to make images. The event runs from August 1 through the last Saturday in October each year, with submissions free and open to anyone working with the process. The 2026 cycle closes October 31.

Entries require three components: a written description of the process used (including the plant material, exposure time, and any layering), the final anthotype image at 2,500 pixels minimum, and a photograph of the source plant taken before processing. Each non-member submits a single print, made within the prior twelve months. Files go via WeTransfer, Dropbox, or Google Drive to anthotype@alternativephotography.com.

Selected work is featured across AlternativePhotography.com (~85,000 monthly visitors), the site's Facebook (12,000+ followers), Instagram (14,000), and YouTube channels. Exceptional images are considered for inclusion in the Anthotype Emulsions book series. There is no cash prize — recognition is editorial.

The event was originally held in August but moved to October after a participant survey: 99% of respondents preferred the later window for longer exposure times and access to ripe plant material. AlternativePhotography.com is a non-profit and runs the event without sponsor backing. The site's resource library lists 25+ commonly-used plants — beetroot, blackberry, butterfly pea, turmeric, walnut — and explicitly encourages experimentation with unusual emulsions.

prose: The International Photography Awards (IPA) was founded in 2003 and is now in its 23rd edition — one of the longer-running international photography competitions. The IPA is the sister organization of the Lucie Foundation, which administers the Lucie Awards.

Submissions are split between Professional and Non-Professional tracks across 11 categories: Advertising, Analog/Film, Architectural, Editorial, Event, Fine Art, Nature, People, Sports, Photography Book, and Special Category. Total prize pool is $60,000 across the program.

Top awards: International Photographer of the Year (Professional, $10,000) and Discovery of the Year (Non-Professional, $5,000). Each Professional Category winner receives $1,000 cash plus a $500 travel allowance; each Non-Professional Category winner receives $500 plus $500 travel. Beyond cash, IPA category winners receive an IPA Trophy, two tickets to the IPA Awards Gala, inclusion in the Best of Show exhibition, screening at House of Lucie Galleries worldwide, publication in the IPA Annual Book, and press coverage to the program's 130,000+ member network.

The 2026 jury includes Anne Morin (curator at diChroma Photography), Caroline Metcalfe (Photography Director), Giovanna Calvenzi (photo editor and curator), Kirk McKoy (photojournalist), Michael Pritchard (Director-General of the Royal Photographic Society), Paris Chong (Leica Gallery LA), and others. prose: Nature Photographer of the Year (NPOTY) is an international nature photography competition organized by the Nature Talks Foundation (Stichting Nature Talks) in the Netherlands. The 2026 cycle is the contest's 11th consecutive year. Winners are announced at the Nature Talks Photo Festival on November 14, 2026.

The C11 category winner receives a photography weekend in Drenthe (Netherlands), and the C13 Youth winner (under 18) receives €250 in products.

Submissions are accepted across 13 categories total, including a free Youth category for photographers under 18 and a separate portfolio award. Photos can be from the current year or previous years — there is no recency restriction on submissions.
The 2025 contest received 24,781 entries from 96 countries, giving a sense of scale.

Eligibility is open to professional and non-professional photographers of all ages worldwide. AI-generated work is not accepted. Registration is free, but most categories carry a paid entry fee (€34 for the main contest, €17.50 for the Fred Hazelhoff portfolio award; the Youth category is free). prose: Exposure Photo Gallery is a photography gallery operating across two continents — its primary venue at Urquiza 739 in Río Tercero, Córdoba, Argentina, with a secondary venue in Buena Park, California (Exposure Los Angeles). "The Shape of a Moment" is the gallery's open call exploring photography's capacity to capture instants that reveal something essential through light, emotion, and time.

The Gold Award winner receives $500 cash and a solo exhibition at the Argentina gallery. Silver and Bronze awards recognize artistic quality without cash; ten Honorable Mentions appear as printed works in the physical exhibition; further selections are shown digitally. Special recognitions are reserved for photographers based in Córdoba Province. All recognized artists receive digital diplomas, and selected works are reproduced in an official exhibition book (print-on-demand).
The 2026 cycle is juried by Gary Hershorn, a 29-year Reuters editor and Getty Images contributor who has covered 17 Olympic Games and is the author of New York Celestial.

Entry fees are tiered by image count: $5 for 1 photo, $10 for 3, $15 for 6, $20 for 12. Unlimited submissions are permitted per applicant. AI-edited work is accepted; fully AI-generated work is not. Submissions are JPEG, max 2,000 pixels on the longest side. The 2026 deadline is June 30 at 11:59 PM PST; results announced August 3.

calls.title: Chromatic Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: International color photography competition across 20 categories including Aerial, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscape, Nature, Portrait, and Street. Separate Professional and Amateur divisions.
calls.summary: International color competition across 20 categories. Separate Professional and Amateur divisions.
prose: Chromatic Photography Awards is the color counterpart to several long-running monochrome competitions — entries must be in color, and black-and-white work is explicitly excluded. The 2026 cycle is the awards' 8th edition. Submissions are open to professionals and amateurs worldwide, with no age restriction stated on the official information page.

Entries can be made in 20 categories: Abstract, Architecture, Cityscapes, Conceptual, Culture, Environmental, Fashion and Beauty, Fine Art, Landscapes, Nature, Nudes, People, Photojournalism, Photomanipulation, Portrait, Sports, Still Life, Street, Travel, and Wildlife and Animal. Category winners receive Gold, Silver, or Bronze medals. The Professional and Amateur top winners receive $2,000 and $1,000 respectively, plus inclusion in the awards' Official Book. Honorable mentions receive certificates and badges.

Entry fees follow a tiered structure: $17 amateur / $22 professional per entry at the early deadline (July 19, 2026), rising to $22 amateur / $27 professional at final deadline (October 25, 2026). Winners are announced December 20, 2026.

The jury is composed of magazine editors, gallery curators, professional agents, and other industry-side professionals — names rotate per edition and are listed on the awards site. The competition does not state an AI policy on its information page, so applicants making AI-assisted work should email organizers before entering.

calls.title: PX3 Prix de la Photographie Paris 2026
calls.description: One of Europe's most prestigious photography awards. Categories include Analog, Architecture, Book, Fine Art, Nature, Portraiture, Press, and Advertising. Winners exhibited in Paris and internationally.
calls.summary: One of Europe's most prestigious awards. Categories from Analog to Advertising. Exhibited in Paris.
prose: PX3 (Prix de la Photographie Paris) is an international photography competition based in Paris, awarding work across eight categories: Analog, Architecture, Book, Fine Art, Nature, Portraiture, Press, and Advertising. The structure separates traditional editorial categories (Press, Portraiture) from medium-specific tracks (Analog, Book), giving applicants flexibility in how they position a series.
The main prize is €5,000, with category and subcategory recognitions stacking on top. Winners are exhibited at PX3's annual Paris showcase and featured in the prize's annual book and online archive.

The 2026 jury includes James Wellford (National Geographic), Steve McCurry (photographer), and Samuel Nja Kwa (Forbes Afrique), with the full jury list published on px3.fr. Entry fees range from €20 to €50 depending on category and submission tier. Eligibility is open to photographers 18 and over worldwide. The deadline is July 22, 2026; AI policy is not stated on the public submission page, so applicants making AI-assisted work should email organizers before entering.

calls.title: Camera Clara Photo Award 2026
calls.description: Award dedicated exclusively to photographers using large-format cameras. Rewards unpublished work presented as a coherent series of 5–10 images. Winner receives prize money plus exhibition production.

calls.summary: Exclusively for large-format camera photographers. Unpublished series of 5-10 images. Prize money + exhibition.
prose: Camera Clara is a French photography prize dedicated specifically to large-format photography. Founded in 2012 by Joséphine de Bodinat Moreno, it rewards an unpublished body of work made with a large-format camera, presented as a coherent series of 5 to 10 images. The €8,000 prize is paid by Joséphine de Bodinat Moreno and includes exhibition production support for the winner.

Submissions are free of charge. The award accepts only large-format work and excludes AI-generated images. Selection criteria emphasize coherence both in form and content, treating the series as the unit of evaluation rather than individual images — applicants are reviewed on whether the body of work holds together, not on whether any single image stands out.

The 2026 jury is unusually senior for a niche prize: Dominique de Font-Reaulx (Jury President), Aurélie Chauffert-Yvart (Artistic Director), Héloïse Conésa (Curator at the National Library of France), Marc Donnadieu (art critic and independent curator), Anne Lacoste (Director of the Institute for Photography of Hauts-de-France), Chantal Nedjib (communications consultant), Guillaume Piens (art historian and founder of Culture Squad Communication), Michel Poivert (Professor of Art History at Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne), and Fabien Simode (art critic and director of Maisons-Alfort Media Libraries), alongside founder Joséphine de Bodinat Moreno.
The 2026 deadline is midnight July 31; results are announced November 3. Applications are made through prixcameraclara.plateformecandidature.com.

calls.title: Tokyo International Foto Award 2026
calls.description: International photography competition introducing photographers to the creative community in Tokyo. Categories include Advertising, Architecture, Editorial, Fine Art, Nature, People, and Portfolio. Winners exhibited in Tokyo.
jury: Prof. William Snyder, Rochester Institute of Technology
calls.summary: International competition introducing photographers to Tokyo's creative community. Winners exhibited in Tokyo.
prose: Tokyo International Foto Awards (TIFA) is an annual photography competition that culminates in a winners' exhibition in Tokyo. The 2026 cycle is open to photographers aged 18 and over worldwide, with seven submission categories: Advertising, Architecture, Editorial, Fine Art, Nature, People, and Portfolio. The Portfolio category accepts series of 1 to 9 images.

The main prize is €3,000 in cash, with category winners and honorable mentions receiving recognition badges and inclusion in TIFA's annual archive. Selected work is exhibited in Tokyo as part of a winners' showcase; specific gala details are published after results.

Submissions are reviewed by a six-member jury that includes Hideko Kataoka (photo editor and curator), Mariama Attah (curator), Kenro Izu (photographer), Susan Baraz (Lucie Foundation Co-Chair), Professor William Snyder (Rochester Institute of Technology), and Alfie Goodrich (Japanorama).

Entry fees are tiered between €15 and €50 depending on category and submission type. AI-generated work is accepted, with no separate AI category. The 2026 deadline is August 1, with results announced in September.

calls.title: Milano Photo Awards 2026
calls.description: International photography exhibition and contest in Milan with a tribute to Sebastiao Salgado. Categories include street, portraits, reportage, and nature. Event September 25–27, 2026. Official sponsor: Nikon Italia.
calls.summary: Exhibition and contest in Milan with Sebastiao Salgado tribute. Street, portraits, reportage, nature. Nikon Italia.
prose: Milano Photo Awards is an Italian photography contest and exhibition run by TheStreetSoup, with Nikon Italia as official sponsor. The 2026 edition runs September 25–27 at Via Maurizio Gonzaga 7 in Milan, scheduled to coincide with Milano Fashion Week. The exhibition format is a 4×3 meter Samsung LED wall for digital display of selected work, with the top three winners in each category also receiving printed and framed prints. The 2026 edition includes a tribute to Sebastião Salgado.

The total prize pool is €30,000 in cash plus Nikon hardware. There are eight competition categories: Street Photography, Portrait & Identity, Wildlife & Nature, Movement & Sport, Human Landscape, Documentary & Social Vision, Conceptual & Fine Art, and Fashion & Style. AI-generated work is not accepted.

Entry follows a tiered structure with separate access levels: Exhibition Open (€20, 2 photos, €500 first prize plus a Nikon backpack and printing), Exhibition Room 1 (€50, 5 photos, €1,000 first prize plus printing and gala access), Exhibition Room 2 (€80, 8–10 photos, €1,500 first prize plus printing and gala access), and the Oriol Vision Award (€50, 5 photos), curated separately by guest judge Estevan Oriol. The submission deadline is August 15, 2026.

calls.title: Aesthetica Art Prize 2026
calls.description: Contemporary art prize celebrating photography, sculpture, installation, digital media, video, and painting. Winners receive exhibition at a major public gallery and publication in Aesthetica Magazine.
jury: Charlotte Hale, Head of Exhibitions, V&A Dundee
Taous Dahmani, Curator, The Photographers' Gallery

calls.summary: Contemporary art prize. Winners exhibited at major public gallery and published in Aesthetica Magazine.
prose: The Aesthetica Art Prize is run by Aesthetica Magazine, the UK contemporary art publication based in York. Founded in 2007, the prize has run annually for nearly two decades and is open across all media — Painting and Drawing; Video, Installation, and Performance; Photography, Digital Art and Installation; and Artists' Film. Photography submissions are evaluated alongside other categories rather than in a separate track.

The main prize is £10,000, with additional support including exhibition at a major UK public gallery, publication in Aesthetica Magazine, and inclusion in the prize's annual anthology. The prize runs an associated Future Now Symposium and publishes Future Now: 125 Contemporary Artists, a book featuring shortlisted and exhibited work from past cycles.

The 2026 jury draws from senior curators across major UK institutions: Carrie Chan (V&A), Charlotte Hale (V&A Dundee), Taous Dahmani (The Photographers' Gallery), Sarah Coulson (Yorkshire Sculpture Park), Poppy Bowers (The Whitworth), Dr James Finch (Royal Academy of Arts), Farah Dailami (The Hepworth Wakefield), artist Jason Bruges (Jason Bruges Studio), and producer Nephertiti Oboshie Schandorf.
Entry fee is £25. The 2026 deadline is August 31, with results announced early 2027. The prize accepts work from artists at any career stage, with no nationality restriction.

calls.summary: 19th annual international color photography competition. 235+ title awards across 35 categories.

calls.summary: Dedicated to color and its absence. Any approach to constructing the color space of the image welcome.

calls.title: Fotografiska HOME — Global Open Call
calls.description: Global open call exploring home — safety, belonging, dignity, identity, and place. Selected works exhibited at United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day, December 10, 2026. Guest curator: James Nachtwey. Submit up to 3 images. Lens-based photography only, no AI.
jury: Pauline Benthede, Global VP Artistic Direction & Exhibitions, Fotografiska
Sophia Emmerich, Lead Editor, Fotografiska Emerging Platform
calls.summary: Global open call exploring home. Exhibition at UN Headquarters. Guest curator: James Nachtwey. No AI.
prose: The HOME open call is a joint initiative by Photography 4 Humanity, Fotografiska, and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. The brief is the single word "home" — interpreted across safety, belonging, dignity, identity, memory, loss, and place — and the call is positioned as a human rights project rather than a conventional photography prize.

Selected work is exhibited at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day, December 10, 2026. The exhibition is guest-curated by James Nachtwey, with Pauline Benthede (Fotografiska's Global VP of Artistic Direction & Exhibitions) and Sophia Emmerich (Lead Editor of the Fotografiska Emerging Platform) joining selection.

The selection structure has three tiers: one Main Image, ten Runners-up, and twenty Honorable Mentions — 31 photographers in total. Submissions are limited to three images per applicant. Only lens-based photography is accepted (analog or digital); AI-generated or prompt-based images are explicitly excluded.
There is no entry fee. The call is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over, with explicit emphasis on emerging artists. The deadline is July 12, 2026.

calls.title: The Idle Class — Photography Issue
calls.description: Open call for photographers of all genres to submit work for the upcoming Photography Issue of The Idle Class Magazine. Submit via email with name, description, and files.
calls.summary: Open call for photographers of all genres for the upcoming Photography Issue of The Idle Class Magazine.

calls.title: Berlin Photo Awards 2026

jury: Alina Rudya, Photographer & Founder, Bell Collective
calls.summary: International competition with 24 categories. Winners exhibited at ERSTERERSTER Gallery Berlin.
prose: Berlin Photo Awards is an international photography competition based in Berlin, with the winners' exhibition held at ERSTERERSTER Gallery in the city. The 2026 cycle accepts submissions across 24 categories spanning the breadth of contemporary photography: Portrait, Landscape, Street, Fine Art, Wildlife, Drone, Smartphone, and others.

The total prize pool is €4,000. Beyond cash, winners are exhibited at ERSTERERSTER Gallery and published in the official Berlin Photo Awards Winners Photobook — the print archive functions as the long-term record of each year's selection.

The 2026 jury includes Thomas Kakareko (photographer and creative consultant), Jorg Nicht (travel and street photographer), Ezgi Polat (creative director), Yuto Yamada (photographer and videographer), Marcello Zerletti (photographer and coach), Alina Rudya (photographer and founder of Bell Collective), Patrick Noack, and Tejasvi Gala.
Entry fee is €25 per image. AI-edited work is permitted; fully AI-generated work is not. Eligibility is open to photographers worldwide. The 2026 deadline is June 27, with results announced July 25.

calls.title: Galleri Format — Window Exhibition 2026
calls.description: Open call for the sixth edition of Galleri Format’s Window Exhibition in Malmö. The exhibition takes place in the gallery’s large street-facing windows on Stora Nygatan beside Gustav Adolfs Torg, 12 June – 9 August 2026. Proposals should be adapted for the window space and target passing foot traffic. Gallery covers production costs and pays an exhibition fee per the MU agreement. Focuses on contemporary photography, video, and film.
calls.summary: Street-facing window exhibition in Malmö. Contemporary photography, video, and film. Production costs covered.

calls.title: Griffin Museum — Handmade Photobook Exhibition 2026
calls.description: 2nd annual exhibition for handcrafted photobooks where the artist's hand shapes the object itself. Submit handmade photobooks via CaFE. Juror: Caleb Cain Marcus of Luminosity Lab.

calls.title: Provoke USA — Open Call
calls.description: Open call for a photography zine inspired by the Japanese Provoke movement — destabilizing certainty and revealing a world beyond conventional language. calls.summary: Photography zine inspired by the Japanese Provoke movement — destabilizing certainty, revealing a world beyond language.

calls.title: Hariban Award 2026
calls.description: International collotype competition combining 170-year-old analogue printing with contemporary photography. Submit 12 black-and-white photographs. Grand Prize: funded two-week residency in Kyoto collaborating with master collotype printers, solo exhibition, and publication in official catalogue. Juror's Choice and Benrido Award winners receive catalogue publication and free Collotype Academy course.
jury: Diane Dufour, Founder & Artistic Director, LE BAL Paris
Erin O'Toole, Curator & Head of Photography, SFMOMA
KIM Jeong Eun, Founder, THE REFERENCE Seoul
calls.summary: International collotype competition. Grand Prize: two-week residency in Kyoto with master collotype printers.
prose: The Hariban Award is run by Benrido, a Kyoto-based collotype atelier founded in 1887 — over 130 years of continuous practice. Collotype is a 19th-century printing technique that achieves an unusually rich tonal range without screens or halftones; it was widely used through the mid-1900s before color printing replaced it commercially. Benrido has preserved the process since around 2000, making it one of the few remaining collotype workshops in the world.
The 2026 cycle is the 13th edition of the award. Approximately 3,700 entries have been submitted across all editions to date.

The Grand Prize is a fully funded two-week artist residency in Kyoto collaborating directly with Benrido's master collotype printers, plus a solo exhibition the following year and publication in the official catalogue. The Juror's Choice and Benrido Award winners receive catalogue publication and a free Collotype Academy course at Benrido.

Submissions are 8 to 12 black-and-white photographs at a $40 to $50 entry fee. AI-generated work is accepted. The 2026 jury comprises Diane Dufour (Founder & Artistic Director, LE BAL Paris), Erin O'Toole (Curator & Head of Photography, SFMOMA), KIM Jeong Eun (Founder, THE REFERENCE Seoul), and Leo Rongone (photographer and CEO of Moncler). The 2026 cycle is open April 1 through June 15; results announced September 15.

calls.title: Dark Frames III — Carlotta Gallery
calls.description: Black and white photography virtual exhibition. A continuation of the inquiry into monochrome photography — absence of colour as a space for deeper perception. Submit up to 3 images via email. Selected work shown in virtual exhibition with catalogue and certificate.
calls.summary: Black and white photography virtual exhibition. Absence of colour as a space for deeper perception.

calls.description: Nature photography virtual exhibition exploring the quiet intensity of plant life. From delicate details to expansive landscapes of growth. Submit up to 3 images via email. Selected work shown in virtual exhibition with catalogue and certificate.

calls.description: Photography virtual exhibition exploring Europe as a continuous negotiation between tradition and innovation, memory and experimentation. Submit up to 3 images via email. Selected work shown in virtual exhibition with catalogue and certificate.
calls.summary: Exploring Europe as a negotiation between tradition and innovation, memory and experimentation. Virtual exhibition.

calls.title: Candid — Carlotta Gallery

calls.title: Summer — Carlotta Gallery
calls.description: Summer photography virtual exhibition. Summer is experienced differently across the world — intensity, brightness, stillness, or transformation. Submit up to 3 images via email. Selected work shown in virtual exhibition with catalogue and certificate.
calls.summary: Summer experienced differently across the world — intensity, brightness, stillness. Virtual exhibition.
prose: Carlotta Gallery is a UK-based virtual photography gallery that runs themed open calls roughly bi-monthly. "Summer" is the gallery's seasonal call inviting photography that captures the season as it's experienced differently across the world — its intensity, brightness, stillness, or quiet transformation. Both literal and conceptual approaches are welcome.
The submission model is free to apply, pay-only-if-selected: £20 for one accepted artwork, £30 for two, or £35 for three. There are no cash prizes — selection is the recognition.

Selected work is shown in a virtual online exhibition for a minimum of six months and up to one year. Selected photographers also receive permanent placement on the Carlotta Gallery Collections page with their biography, a free PDF of the exhibition catalogue, a Certificate of Recognition, and potential feature on the gallery's Instagram account (@carlottagallery).

Eligibility is open globally to photographers aged 18 and over. Each photographer submits up to 3 JPG images by email, accompanied by name, Instagram handle, biography, artist statement, and artwork details. The 2026 deadline is June 10.

calls.title: Paradajs Photo Fest 2026 — Welcome to Paradise
calls.description: International photography open call exploring paradise in original, unconventional ways. Submit single photographs or series. Grand Prix winner receives €2,000, a one-month residency in Banská Štiavnica (fall 2026), production support, and a solo exhibition in 2027. 10 finalists shown in group exhibition.
calls.summary: Exploring paradise in unconventional ways. Grand Prix: €2,000 + one-month residency in Banská Štiavnica.

calls.title: Beautiful Bizarre Art Prize — MPB Photography Award 2026
calls.description: International art prize (9th year) for representational photography in analogue or digital media. Submit fine art photography with only minor digital post-processing. 1st prize receives $4,500 cash, exhibition at Modern Eden Gallery in San Francisco, artwork published in December 2026 issue, in-depth interview, and 12-month Artist Directory listing. 2nd prize $1,000, 3rd prize $500 — all winners exhibit at Modern Eden. No AI-generated work accepted.
calls.summary: Representational photography. $3,000 first prize + exhibition at Modern Eden Gallery, San Francisco. No AI.
prose: The Beautiful Bizarre Art Prize is an annual contest run by Beautiful Bizarre Magazine, an Australia-based publication, with the photography track now in its 9th year. The 2026 Photography Award is sponsored by MPB — the used-camera retailer founded in 2011 that recirculates over half a million cameras annually.

Eligible work is representational photography (analogue or digital), with only minor post-processing allowed; heavily manipulated work belongs in the prize's separate Digital Art track. AI-generated work of any kind is excluded — the prize publishes an unusually direct enforcement policy: AI violations result in forfeiture of prizes plus a five-year entry ban.

Cash prize structure: $3,000 first place, $1,000 second, $500 third. All three winners receive Epic Print printing credits sized to support an actual print order ($150–$250), exhibition at Modern Eden Gallery in San Francisco, a magazine feature in the December 2026 issue, an in-depth interview, a 12-month listing on the Beautiful Bizarre Artist Directory, and a magazine subscription. First-prize additionally receives a FocusPoint 30L backpack and a glass trophy.
Entry fee is $40. The 2026 deadline is July 17, with results announced in September. The current photography juror is photographer Franz Szony.

calls.title: FotoDoc Photo Contest 2026
calls.description: International documentary photography contest with three categories: Single Image (1–3 photos), Photo Essay (6–8 photos), and Portfolio (10–15 photos). Free to submit; $29 publication fee only if selected. 60 finalists published in festival catalog. 25 winners exhibited at FotoDoc Festival in São Paulo in November 2026. Overall Portfolio winner receives trophy, airfare, and accommodation to attend the festival. No AI-generated images accepted.
calls.summary: International documentary contest. Three categories. 25 winners exhibited at FotoDoc Festival, São Paulo.
prose: FotoDoc is an international documentary photography contest run by Vertente Edição, Impressão e Produção LTDA, with the festival itself held in São Paulo, Brazil each November. Submissions are accepted in three categories distinguished by sequence length: Single Image (1 to 3 photos), Photo Essay (6 to 8 photos), and Portfolio (10 to 15 photos).

The submission model is two-stage: initial submission is free, with a $29 USD (R$98 BRL) publication fee charged only after selection — finalists have seven days to confirm. Sixty finalists are selected and published in the festival catalog; from those, an in-person five-person professional jury chooses 25 winners who are exhibited at the FotoDoc Festival in November 2026. Selection runs on rolling evaluation as submissions arrive.

The Overall Portfolio winner receives a trophy plus airfare and accommodation to attend the festival in São Paulo with a presentation slot. All 25 winners receive exhibition and catalog publication; all 60 finalists receive catalog publication. Selected works also appear on the festival website and Instagram with dedicated photographer profile pages.

Eligibility is open to Brazilian and international photographers with no theme restrictions. AI-generated images are prohibited; AI editing is permitted with declaration. Authors retain all rights; the festival retains promotional and exhibition usage. The 2026 deadline is June 30 at 11:59 PM Brasília time.

calls.title: SUB(SCAPE) — Manifest Gallery Season 22
calls.description: Themed group exhibition exploring what lies beneath the visible — structural, psychological, geological, social, or conceptual systems that sustain or destabilize the world above. Open to all media including photography. Submit up to 3 entries for $45, $5 per additional. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 honorarium. One work selected for a $1,000 Grand Jury Award. Artists receive 70% on sales. Exhibition at Manifest Gallery in Cincinnati, July 10 – August 7, 2026. 22nd season of this nonprofit creative research gallery.
calls.summary: Themed exhibition exploring what lies beneath the visible — structural, psychological, or social systems. Cincinnati.

calls.title: Artadia Awards 2026 — New York City
calls.description: Unrestricted merit-based grants for contemporary visual artists including photographers. Three awardees receive $15,000 each. Artadia runs awards in 7 US cities throughout the year — NYC deadline April 1, with San Francisco (May–June), Boston (Aug–Sep), Atlanta (Sep–Oct), and Houston (Oct–Nov) following. Past awardees include artists featured in the Whitney Biennial and Prospect New Orleans.
calls.summary: Unrestricted $15,000 grants for contemporary visual artists in NYC. Two-round jury process with studio visits.

calls.title: XII Premio Internacional de Fotografía Jalón Ángel
calls.description: 12th edition of this international photography prize organized by Universidad San Jorge in Zaragoza, Spain. Three categories: Portrait (spontaneous or posed), Travel (landscapes, cultures, traditions), and Migration & Borders (human movement, territorial and cultural limits). One photograph per category. No AI, no heavy retouching, RAW files may be requested. Winners announced June 25. Named after Jalón Ángel (1898–1976), one of Spain's most celebrated portrait photographers.
calls.summary: Three categories: Portrait, Travel, Migration & Borders. One photo per category. No AI. Zaragoza, Spain.

calls.title: Bethany Arts Community — Fall Multidisciplinary Residency 2026
calls.description: Two-week artist residency in Ossining, New York (Sep 22 – Oct 6, 2026) for 12 artists across all disciplines including photography, visual arts, film, writing, and performance. Residents receive a $450 stipend, private studio, room and board, and 3 meals daily. Each artist facilitates one community program during the residency. calls.summary: Two-week residency in Ossining, NY. $450 stipend, private studio, room and board. 12 artists across all disciplines.

calls.title: Diane Dammeyer Fellowship in Photographic Arts and Social Issues 2026/27
calls.org: Museum of Contemporary Photography at Columbia
calls.description: Fellowship supporting socially engaged photographers in creating work within a community. The fellow partners with a Chicago-based community organization to address human rights, social, economic, or cultural issues through photography. September–June commitment with flexible hours. Culminates in a public exhibition and/or publication at MoCP. Preference for Chicago-based projects. Requires MFA in photography or related field, or BA with 5 years post-degree creative practice. Two professional references required.
calls.summary: Fellowship for socially engaged photographers partnering with a Chicago-based community organization.
prose: The Diane Dammeyer Fellowship in Photographic Arts and Social Issues is administered by Columbia College Chicago in partnership with the Museum of Contemporary Photography (MoCP). Founded in 2015 with Fereshteh Toosi as its first fellow, the fellowship supports socially engaged photographers producing new work in collaboration with a Chicago-based community partner organization.

The fellowship runs from September through June with flexible hours, structured to allow the fellow to maintain other professional commitments while embedded with their community partner. The work culminates in a public exhibition and/or publication at MoCP — the partnership between fellow and community organization is treated as the core of the fellowship rather than a transactional output.

Past fellows have addressed human rights, social, economic, and cultural issues across a wide range of communities: Ervin A. Johnson (2016–17), Anahid Ghorbani (2017–18), Sasha Phyars-Burgess (2018–19), Jonathan Michael Castillo (2019–21), Melissa Ann Pinney (2021–22), Dylan Yarbrough (2022–23), the joint Oscar B. Castillo & Wil Sands fellowship (2023–24), and Alessandro Bo (2024–25).

Eligibility requires either an MFA in photography or related field, or a BA plus five years of post-degree creative practice. Preference is given to Chicago-based projects. Two professional references are required. There is no application fee. Applications go through JotForm; the 2026/27 deadline is June 12, 2026.

prose: The Lenscratch Student Prize is the photography blog's annual prize for emerging student photographers, founded in 2013 and run by Lenscratch editor Aline Smithson. The prize is restricted to students currently enrolled in bachelor's or master's degree photography programs.

The first prize is unusually layered. The winner receives $2,000 in cash plus a year-long mentorship with Aline Smithson, portfolio review sessions with curators, seats at portfolio review events, museum memberships, a mini-exhibition on Lenscratch, a $500 gift certificate to Freestyle Photo, multiple book collections, and merchandise. The mentorship and review components are worth more than the cash for many recipients.
Second prize: $1,000 plus Lenscratch feature, mini-exhibition, and merchandise. Third: $750 with the same package. Four Honorable Mentions: $500 each.

Past winners include Jordan Tovin (2025), Mosfiqur Rahman Johan (2024), Christian K. Lee (2023), Drew Leventhal (2022), Allie Tsubota (2021), Raymond Thompson Jr. (2020), Guanyu Xu (2019), Zora J. Murff (2018), Shawn Bush (2017), Drew Nikonowicz (2016), and others — many have gone on to significant careers in editorial, museum, and gallery photography.

The 19-juror panel for 2026 includes Aline Smithson, Daniel George, Karen Haas (Lane Curator of Photographs at MFA Boston), Kris Graves (Kris Graves Projects), Hamidah Glasgow (former Director, Center for Fine Art Photography), Alexa Dilworth (former Publishing Director at CDS at Duke), Yorgos Efthymiadis (The Curated Fridge), and most of the past winners themselves. There is no entry fee. Submissions go through Google Form; the 2026 deadline is June 1; results announced July 13.

calls.summary: Online exhibition exploring fatherhood as an evolving role shaped by culture, responsibility, and tenderness.
prose: Lenscratch is one of the longest-running photography blogs and online platforms, with a regular schedule of online exhibitions accompanying its daily editorial coverage. The Fatherhood Exhibition is the platform's open call for photography that engages with the role of fathers — the brief frames fatherhood as an evolving role shaped by culture, responsibility, tenderness, and family expectations.

Lenscratch's open calls have a consistent format: a single themed exhibition publishes online by a fixed date, with one image accepted per photographer. The Fatherhood exhibition publishes June 21, 2026 — typically scheduled to coincide with U.S. Father's Day weekend.

Submissions are free, with one entry per photographer. Images are sized to 72dpi at 1000 pixels on the long side and submitted via Google Form. Caption format follows Lenscratch's standard: copyright, name, image title, Instagram handle, and website.

Selected work appears in the online group exhibition on Lenscratch — the platform itself functions as the prize, given Lenscratch's substantial readership in the photography community. The 2026 deadline is June 13.

calls.summary: Online exhibition examining tensions and transformations across America. Timed for July 4th.
prose: Lenscratch is one of the longest-running photography blogs and online platforms, edited by photographer Aline Smithson, with a regular schedule of online exhibitions accompanying its daily editorial coverage. "Fault Lines: America" is the platform's open call for photography examining tensions, fractures, and transformations across the United States — resistance, social change, protest, activism, justice, identity, power, and freedom.

The 2026 cycle is timed for the Fourth of July, with the online exhibition publishing on July 4. The call invites work that engages with civic engagement and the challenges facing democratic institutions. Selection is by Norm Diamond and Marcy Palmer; Diamond's stated framing for the call is direct: "What occupies my thoughts is the state of our country and its descent into fascism. This is the most important story of the 21st century."

Submissions are free, with one entry per photographer. Images are sized to 72dpi at 1000 pixels on the long side and submitted via Google Form. Caption format follows Lenscratch's standard: copyright, name, image title, Instagram handle, and website.

Selected work appears in the online group exhibition on Lenscratch — the platform itself functions as the prize, given Lenscratch's substantial readership in the photography community. The 2026 deadline is June 19; exhibition publishes July 4.

prose: photoED is a Canadian print photography magazine that publishes themed issues with each issue's content drawn from open call submissions. Issue #77 is themed "Home VS Away," inviting fine art photography projects that investigate the idea of home, the experience of being away, or the tension between the two — the brief is loose by design, with no preferred genre.

prose: F-Stop Magazine has been publishing themed photography issues online since 2004. Each issue centers on a single category — documentary, conceptual, portrait, landscape, color, abstract, alternative process, photobook — and runs as an open call to feature multiple photographers per issue. Issue 138 is a documentary photography issue.

The brief for the documentary issue is photography that records events, environments, or everyday life in a straightforward, accurate way. F-Stop draws an explicit distinction from photojournalism: documentary work has longer-term focus on a topic, place, or event, rather than newsworthy moments.

Submissions are free and limited to one per person per issue. Each submission can include up to 12 photographs with a project statement and/or descriptive captions. F-Stop publishes online — selected work appears on the magazine's website indefinitely as part of its archive.

prose: Roma E'Festival is an international street photography competition organized by Effe4.0 Street Photography, in its third edition for 2026. The festival proper runs October 16–18 in Rome, with finalists exhibited at Officine Fotografiche.

Submissions are split across five categories: Single Image (color/open), Black & White, Smartphone, Photographic Project (5 to 15 images), and AI-Generated images, which are judged separately under their own selection process — generative AI is explicitly excluded from the four conventional street categories. Multi-category passes provide a 50% discount: the EFFE4 PRO pass (€50) covers Street, B&W, and Smartphone; the EFFE4 FULL pass (€70) covers all categories.

Finalists receive a physical print and exhibition for the duration of the festival, inclusion in the official catalogue, a touring exhibition appearing alongside the main festival, and visibility through the festival's website and social channels. Top three finalists per category receive prizes from partners Fotodiego, Fowa, and Ricoh GR — equipment, monographs, solo exhibitions, and editorial reviews depending on category.

The jury comprises ten international photographers and editors: Rui Palha, Pau Buscató, Barbara Di Maio, Liliana Ranalletta, Mario Mencacci, Arez Prod, Claudio Palmisano, Dario Coletti, Sonia Simbolo, and Gianluca De Dominici.
