prose: FeelsZine is a Canadian independent zine that publishes biannually, alternating issues between thematic prompts. Issue 27, themed "Belonging," coincides with the magazine's 10th anniversary. Submissions are open across both writing and visual art, with a primarily Canadian editorial focus that also welcomes global contributors.

Accepted writing forms include poetry, personal essays, fiction, and interview proposals up to 1,200 words. Poetry and prose are limited to two pieces per submission unless part of a larger collection. Visual art submissions — photography, illustration, collage, typography — must be accompanied by a short artist statement, with 300dpi files requested if accepted.

Submissions are sent by email (submittofeels@gmail.com) as Word documents or Google Docs (no PDFs), with each entry including a short bio, work description, and country of origin. Previously published work is accepted as long as it is not simultaneously appearing in another Canadian independent magazine during FeelsZine's six-month publication window. prose: Zone is a photography-based publication that opens submissions to any visual artist, with no restrictions on age, medium, or approach. The submission format is unusual for the genre: artists send up to 20 JPG images bundled in a ZIP file, with a strict 20MB cap and no external links or WeTransfer accepted. There is no submission fee, and artists are explicitly invited to submit multiple times throughout the year.

Selected work appears primarily on the magazine's Instagram, where the editorial team curates the rollout — they reserve the right to select a subset from a series, reorder images, and occasionally crop. Some work is grouped with other artists in collective posts. Print publications are produced separately; recent print titles include Z3NE, Amongst the More Irritating Minor Ideas, and Alone Together.

The submission flow is deliberately low-friction. There is no themed brief; an optional bio, artist statement, and Instagram handle accompany the file. Artists receive no guarantee of feature, and the team does not provide individualized feedback on rejections.

calls.title: Burn Magazine — Open Submissions

calls.summary: Photography magazine founded by David Alan Harvey (Magnum). Photo essays and multimedia on any subject.
jury: David Alan Harvey, Founder & Magnum Photographer
prose: Burn was founded by David Alan Harvey in 2008 as an online photography magazine. It accepts work in any photographic genre — documentary, photojournalism, fashion, sports, science, natural history, art photography — with no curatorial preference for one over another. Submissions are sent as a PDF to submissions@burnmagazine.org, with images viewable in an online gallery (password-protected is fine), capped at 1080 pixels on the shortest side. A short explanatory text and artist statement accompany each submission.

Selected essays are published on the magazine's homepage and presented as multimedia pieces rather than flat galleries — slideshows, layered text, sequenced reveals. There is no fixed publication cadence; features run as they are accepted.

There is no submission fee and no eligibility restriction. Editorial leadership beyond Harvey has shifted in recent years, though the current editor is not publicly named. Burn does not run a formal prize or award alongside the open submission — homepage publication is the recognition.

calls.title: Phases Magazine — Open Submissions

calls.summary: International contemporary photography magazine publishing 3 portfolios per issue.
prose: Phases is an online photography magazine specializing in international contemporary work, founded in December 2012 by Jerome Montagne (France) and Alexis Vasilikos (Greece). The magazine has published 1,290 portfolios across irregular issues, with three portfolios featured per issue.

Submissions are open continuously, with no formal guidelines or themed brief. Artists send a link to their website, online work, or a few low-resolution attached images to submissions@phasesmag.com. The team receives high submission volume daily and cannot provide individualized responses or feedback — resubmission is encouraged if artists do not hear back.

There is no submission fee. Selected portfolios are published online; the magazine does not specify additional compensation or rights claims beyond publication. The editors' Greek and French base shows in recent contributor lists, with names like Mike Almiroudis, Yorgos Yatromanolakis, Yiannis Trifonopoulos, Gelly Siganou, and Georges Salameh appearing across recent and past selections.

calls.title: Noice Magazine — Open Submissions
calls.description: Print-to-order photography magazine with themed issues focusing on minimalism, social issues, and humor. Submit up to 10 images per themed call. Published as limited edition prints distributed worldwide.
calls.summary: Print-to-order magazine with themed issues. Minimalism, social issues, and humor. Limited editions.

calls.title: SIYU Award 2026
calls.description: Award for young Swiss photographers (formerly vfg Young Talent Award). Ten finalists exhibited in a group show at Photobastei Zurich with a published catalogue. Three cash prizes awarded through the Alois Ottiger Grant, in memory of Swiss photographer Alois Ottiger (1941–2025). Free theme, all fields of photography. Submissions must be anonymous.
calls.summary: Award for young Swiss photographers. Ten finalists exhibited at Photobastei Zurich with catalogue. Free theme.

calls.title: Alpine Fellowship Visual Art Prize 2026
calls.description: Annual visual art prize on the theme of JOY. Open to all visual art media including photography, painting, sculpture, video, and installation. One piece per entry, multiple entries allowed as separate submissions. Work must be entirely created without AI.
jury: Sue Grayson Ford MBE, Former Director, Serpentine Gallery & Photographers' Gallery London
Julian Spalding, Former Director of Art Galleries for Sheffield, Manchester & Glasgow
calls.summary: Annual prize on the theme of JOY. All visual art media including photography. No AI.
prose: The Alpine Fellowship Visual Art Prize is the visual art track of the Alpine Fellowship's annual symposium program. Each year carries a single thematic prompt — past themes have included "On Childhood," "On Identity," "On Forgiveness and Retribution," "On Untamed," "On Freedom," "On Language," "On Flourishing," and "On Fear." The 2026 theme is "JOY."

Cash prizes total £5,000 across three placements: £3,000 first place, £1,000 second place, and £1,000 third place. The 2026 jury comprises Sue Grayson Ford MBE (former Director of the Serpentine Gallery and Photographers' Gallery London) and Julian Spalding (former Director of Art Galleries for Sheffield, Manchester, and Glasgow).

The competition is open to all media — painting, sculpture, photography, video, installation — with videos capped at 8 minutes. Submissions are limited to one piece per entry, with multiple entries permitted as separate submissions. Each piece must include media type, date of creation, and dimensions where applicable.

Eligibility is open to all nationalities, with a minimum age of 18 at the time of entry. AI-generated work is explicitly excluded — applicants must confirm their work was created entirely without AI assistance at any stage. The entry fee is £10 per submission. The 2026 deadline is July 1.

calls.title: This Is a Person
calls.description: Portrait photography exploring interior life over surface identity. Seeking images that suggest psychological tension, ambiguity, vulnerability, or contradiction rather than likeness alone. Intentionally selective — approximately 10–12% acceptance rate. One image per selected artist exhibited.
calls.summary: Portrait photography exploring interior life over surface identity. ~10-12% acceptance rate.

calls.title: Monochrome Awards 2026
calls.description: International black and white photography competition with professional and amateur divisions across 14 categories including Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscapes, Nature, Portrait, Street, and Wildlife. Winners published in annual book and featured in online Winners Gallery.
calls.summary: International B&W competition with 14 categories. Professional and amateur divisions. Annual book.
prose: Monochrome Photography Awards is a competition exclusively for black-and-white photography, founded in 2014 and run annually. Entries are split between two main category groups — Professional and Amateur — with subcategories under each (Architecture, Fine Art, Photojournalism, Portrait, and others). Winners receive the titles "Monochrome Photographer of the Year" (Professional) and "Monochrome Discovery of the Year" (Amateur).

The cash prize pool is $3,000 across the two main categories, with category and subcategory medals stacking on top. Selected work is published in the Monochrome Photography Awards Annual Book — a print collection of first-, second-, and third-place winners plus honorable mention names — which functions as the long-term archive of each edition.

Submission requirements are tight: JPEG at 1200 pixels on the longest side, sRGB or Adobe98 8-bit, no watermarks or borders, no special characters in filenames. The entry portal is profile-based — applicants create an account, upload, and submit only after fees are paid. Early-deadline entries close July 5, 2026; final deadline runs through to November 15, with results announced January 3, 2027.

calls.title: Annual Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: International photography competition (8th edition) celebrating photographers of all levels. Five main categories — Architecture, Fine Art, Nature, People, and Special — with 25 subcategories. Accepts all formats, looking for bold and innovative approaches.
calls.summary: 8th edition. Five main categories, 25 subcategories. Looking for bold and innovative approaches.
prose: Now in its eighth edition, Annual Photography Awards is a worldwide competition open to professionals, amateurs, and students aged 18 and over. Submissions are accepted across five main categories — Architecture, Fine Art, Nature, People, and Special — with 25 subcategories in total. The Special category covers Aerial & Drone, Analog/Film, Minimalism, Night Photography, and Open; the People category includes Documentary, Portrait, Street, Body & Nudes, and Travel & Culture. Each subcategory has its own award track, so a photographer can be a category winner without competing across genres.

The cash prize pool is $5,000, distributed as a $2,500 Grand Prize plus five $500 Category Photographer of the Year awards. Beyond cash, winners and honorable mentions receive downloadable medals and certificates and inclusion in an online gallery on the awards site. Entries are judged anonymously by a panel of 20+ international photographers.

Entry fees follow a tiered structure: $25 for a single image or $35 for a series of up to 8 images at the early bird rate (deadline June 7, 2026), rising to $30 single / $40 series at final deadline (December 13, 2026). The contest is restricted to legal worldwide residents who are the original authors of submitted work. There is no nomination process; artists submit directly through the awards site.

calls.title: HER.SELF
calls.description: Online juried exhibit celebrating women in all their complexities — presence, resilience, beauty, and becoming. Open to all fine art mediums including photography. Artists receive 100% of sale price with no commission.
calls.summary: Celebrating women in all complexities — presence, resilience, beauty, becoming. 100% commission-free sales.
jury: Amy Matteson Neill, Creative Director, Art Fluent
prose: Art Fluent is a Boston-based curatorial platform (1 Washington Mall #1218, Boston, MA 02108) that runs themed online juried exhibitions across fine art mediums. "HER.SELF" is the platform's open call for work honoring women in all their complexities — the brief language emphasizes presence, resilience, beauty, and becoming, with no restriction on whether the artist or the subject is a woman.

Cash prizes total $1,250: a Best of Show award of $750 and two Director's Choice awards of $250 each. Beyond cash, all accepted work is displayed in the online gallery on art-fluent.com, with sales going through the platform at 100% commission to the artist. The selection is curated by Creative Director Amy Matteson Neill and an anonymous committee.

Entry fee is $25 for the first work and $10 each additional, up to 20 submissions per artist. Open globally to amateur and professional artists; AI-generated work is not accepted, and work made under instructor guidance or copied from other sources is excluded. Submissions go through CaFÉ (callforentry.org), which requires a free artist account.
Art Fluent does not provide individualized rejection feedback. The 2026 deadline is July 17 (midnight MST), with notification on August 21.

calls.title: Wider Skies Magazine — Issue 1
calls.description: New photo magazine exploring speculative futurism — not as science fiction, but as a way of noticing the near futures already forming around us. Submit up to 4 film photographs for the first issue. Looking for images that point to possible futures grounded in real life — moments of care, repair, survival, shared responsibility, quiet adaptation, or small signs of change. Film only. Free Kodak Pro 100 film available for those who need it.
calls.summary: New magazine exploring speculative futurism through film photography. Free Kodak film available for those who need it.

calls.title: Atlas of Ruins Vol.3 — Call for Photos
calls.description: Submit photographs of architectural ruins from anywhere in the world for the third edition of the Atlas of Ruins book. Photos can depict ruins from any historical period — abandoned buildings, crumbling monuments, forgotten infrastructure. Two registration tiers: Early (until Jul 9, €13/1 photo, €25/up to 10), Regular (until Oct 1, €16/€30). Fees exclude VAT. 1st €1,200, 2nd €500, 3rd €300. All participants receive an ebook copy. Best photos from each country featured in the printed book.
calls.summary: Photographs of architectural ruins from anywhere in the world for a printed book. Two registration tiers, prizes up to €1,200.
prose: Atlas of Ruins is a recurring photo book series published by Reuse Italy, a cultural benefit corporation focused on reusing historical heritage through partnerships with architects, institutions, and national organizations. Vol.3 follows two earlier volumes (Vol.1 and Vol.2), both available for purchase on the Reuse Italy site.

The theme is architectural ruins from any historical period and any location worldwide — the open geographical and historical scope means submissions span everything from Roman antiquity through twentieth-century industrial decay. Entries can come from photographers, amateurs, students, architects, or designers, and individuals or collectives may participate.

Cash prizes: 1st place €1,200, 2nd €500, 3rd €300. Country mentions go to the best photo from each represented nation, and all participants receive an ebook copy of the published volume regardless of selection. Selected work appears in the printed Atlas of Ruins — Vol.3 with critical texts from international scholars.

Entry fees follow a tiered structure: early registration (until July 9, 2026) costs €13 for one photo or €25 for 2–10; regular registration (until October 1, 2026) costs €16 for one or €30 for 2–10. VAT is added separately. Submissions are JPEG, minimum 1200 pixels on the longest side, under 5MB, with no logos or watermarks. Higher-resolution files and location data are requested after selection.

calls.title: SVĚTOVA 1 Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: One-month creative residency for an emerging visual artist in Prague. Includes private bedroom, shared 30m² studio in the gallery, production budget of approximately €820, round-trip travel, curatorial support, and opportunities for a public workshop, artist lecture, and exhibition. Open to residents of 39 European countries plus Tunisia. Must not be enrolled in educational programs during the residency. Residency runs November 1 – December 6, 2026.
calls.summary: One-month residency for emerging artists in Prague. Studio, production budget, travel, and exhibition opportunity.

calls.summary: Annual juried show in Ithaca, NY. Up to $1,000 in prizes. All photographic media accepted.

calls.summary: Revoke Collective's first zine on the theme of Defiance. Photographs that challenge, disrupt, or simply refuse.

calls.summary: Black-and-white photography for a print publication. Theme: imagining what seems impossible, a tomorrow.

calls.description: HAZEGALLERY, the curatorial platform of PURPLEHAZE Magazine, invites artists and image-makers to participate in a curated pop-up exhibition in Amsterdam alongside the launch of PURPLEHAZE Print Issue 012. Theme explores autonomy as identity, rituals of independence, intimacy turned inward, beauty chosen rather than granted, solitude as clarity, and desire as self-directed. Accepts fashion, fine art, and documentary photography, works on paper, fine art prints, and short looping video works. Selected artists participate in the June 2026 Amsterdam exhibition and may be published in the print issue.
jury: Irina Rusinovich, Founder & Curator, HAZE Gallery
calls.summary: Pop-up exhibition in Amsterdam exploring autonomy, intimacy turned inward, and self-directed desire. With PURPLEHAZE.

calls.summary: Annual group exhibition since 2013. Painting, sculpture, photography, film, and more. Two Berlin venues.

calls.title: KH7 Artspace — Exhibitions 2026
calls.description: Open call for solo or group exhibition proposals at KH7 Artspace in Aarhus, Denmark for the second half of 2026. Applicants from outside Denmark must cover their own transport and visa expenses. Submit project description (max 2 A4 pages with images) via email.
calls.summary: Solo or group exhibition proposals for the second half of 2026. All artistic disciplines welcome. Aarhus, Denmark.

calls.title: Ephemere Photo Journal Vol. 2 — Triplicities
calls.description: Submit text-driven photo features exploring "Triplicities: The Magic of Three" — Time's Arrow, The Life Cycle, The Dialectic. Accepted formats include personal essays, critical essays, photo-poetry, philosophical explorations, interviews, and reviews. Published in a collectible large-format newsprint journal printed in Japan. Shortlisted authors work directly with editors in a collaborative editing process.
calls.summary: Text-driven photo features exploring 'The Magic of Three.' Printed in a collectible large-format newsprint journal.

calls.title: European Landscapes Open Call
calls.description: Open call for photographs of European landscapes — lakes, rivers, sea, trees, sunsets, storms, gardens. Selected work published in a printed photo book. No collage, manipulated, or AI-generated photos accepted.
calls.summary: Photographs of European landscapes for a printed photo book. No manipulated or AI-generated photos.

calls.summary: Northern European natural and rural landscapes (no buildings) for a printed photo book. No AI-generated photos.

calls.title: Hasselblad Foundation Nature Photography Grant 2026
calls.description: Grant for photographic explorations of nature, landscape, and environment. Emphasis on originality, environmental issues, biodiversity, and human impact on nature and climate. Open to citizens of Nordic countries or permanent residents of the Nordic region. Projects should have a 1–3 year timeframe.
jury: Mats Björkman, Senior Lecturer, University of Gothenburg
Andréas Hagström, Archive/Library Manager, Hasselblad Foundation
Louise Wolthers, Head of Research/Curator, Hasselblad Foundation
calls.summary: Grant for photographic explorations of nature, landscape, and environment. Nordic citizens/residents. 1-3 year projects.

calls.title: Guest Room: Shana Lopes & Aspen Mays
calls.description: Open call curated by Shana Lopes (Assistant Curator of Photography, SFMOMA) and Aspen Mays (Associate Professor/Chair of Photography, California College of the Arts) exploring the theme "A Little Bit of Magic" — inviting work that engages with doubling, substitution, sleight of hand, constructed realities, staged impossibilities, and illusion in photography. Open to everyone. Selected work featured on Der Greif's platform with feedback session from the curators.
jury: Shana Lopes, Assistant Curator of Photography, SFMOMA
Aspen Mays, Artist and Associate Professor/Chair of Photography, California College of the Arts
calls.summary: Theme: "A Little Bit of Magic" — doubling, sleight of hand, constructed realities, illusion. Curated for Der Greif.

calls.title: Photobook Feature — In Focus
calls.description: Open call for photobooks to be featured in Der Greif's Articles section with a dedicated editorial write-up. No fixed theme. Seeks photobooks demonstrating strong conceptual thinking, thoughtful sequencing, and an engaged relationship to the medium of the book. Accepts self-published photobooks, artist books, zines, experimental publications, and small-edition press titles. Both recent releases and unpublished or in-progress projects eligible (if publication-ready).
calls.summary: Photobooks featured in Der Greif's Articles section with editorial write-up. Self-published and small-edition welcome.

calls.title: Jugend fotografiert Deutschland 2025
calls.description: German youth photography contest for ages 10–18, now in its 2025/26 edition. Theme: "Be you. Be seen. Be heard." Submit documentary photo stories on any personally relevant topic. Smartphones or cameras welcome, no prior experience required. Individuals or teams of up to 10 participants with optional coaches from schools, youth centers, or community organizations. Must be residents of Germany.
calls.summary: German youth contest ages 10-18. Documentary photo stories. "Be you. Be seen. Be heard." Teams welcome.

calls.title: Nikon Comedy Wildlife Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: Annual international competition celebrating the funniest moments in wildlife photography. Founded in 2015 by Paul Joynson-Hicks and Tom Sullam. Free to enter, open to everyone worldwide with any camera brand. Nine categories: Mammals, Birds, Reptiles/Amphibians/Insects, Fish & Aquatic Species, Nikon Young Photographer, Nikon Junior, Portfolio, Nikon Video, and People's Choice Award. Grand prize: week-long safari for two at Alex Walker's Serian in the Maasai Mara, Kenya. Category winners receive Nikon cameras and lenses plus handmade trophies. Over 10,000 entries from 100+ countries. Proceeds support wildlife conservation.
calls.prize: Kenya safari for 2 + Nikon gear + trophies
jury: Charlie Hamilton James, National Geographic Photographer
Cam Whitnall, Wildlife Photographer & TV Presenter
Will Travers OBE, Born Free Foundation
Hannah Stitfall, Wildlife Filmmaker & TV Presenter
calls.summary: Celebrating the funniest moments in wildlife photography. Free entry. Grand prize: Kenya safari for two.
prose: The Comedy Wildlife Photography Awards is an annual international competition for funny moments in wildlife photography, founded in 2015 by photographers Paul Joynson-Hicks (MBE) and Tom Sullam. Nikon is the title sponsor; proceeds from the program support wildlife conservation.

Submissions are accepted across nine categories: Mammals, Birds, Reptiles/Amphibians/Insects, Fish & Aquatic Species, Nikon Young Photographer, Nikon Junior, Portfolio, Nikon Video, and the People's Choice Award. The grand prize is a week-long safari for two at Alex Walker's Serian in the Maasai Mara, Kenya, plus a handmade trophy. Category winners receive Nikon cameras and lenses plus their own trophies.

Entry is free, with no fee at any stage. Eligibility is open globally — any camera brand, any career stage. Entries must be authentic moments from natural settings; AI-generated images are not accepted.

The 2026 jury comprises an unusually large panel of conservationists, wildlife photographers, and presenters: co-founders Paul Joynson-Hicks and Tom Sullam, with Kate Humble (TV presenter), Hugh Dennis (comedian), Will Burrard-Lucas, Daisy Gilardini, Charlie Hamilton James (National Geographic), Will Travers OBE (Born Free Foundation), Bella Lack (conservationist), Charlotte Kemsley (Regional Director, Nikon), and others.
Past cycles have drawn over 10,000 entries from 100+ countries. The 2026 deadline is June 30, with results announced November 2026.

calls.title: FLORA — Shutter Hub Editions Publication
calls.description: Open call for a printed photobook celebrating the diversity, resilience, subtleties, and poetry of growing things. Images should capture vegetation from mosses and ferns to forests, blossoms, vines, and roots — revealing the nuance of growth, patterns of nature's processes, and the quiet power of plant life in all environments. Selected images featured in a printed FLORA photobook, available through shutterhub.org.uk and selected stockists. Pay-what-you-can entry with £15 minimum donation. Free submissions available for photographers with limited income (email request required before entry). AI use must be disclosed.
calls.summary: Printed photobook celebrating plant life and natural growth. Pay-what-you-can entry, £15 minimum.
prose: FLORA is the next volume in Shutter Hub Editions' photobook series — published by Shutter Hub, the UK photography organization whose books are held in collections including the British Library, V&A, and Portuguese Center of Photography. The brief is plant life: vegetation from mosses and ferns through forests, blossoms, vines, and roots, with the call inviting work that captures the diversity, resilience, subtleties, and poetry of growing things.

The published book is portrait-oriented A5 (148×210mm). Selected photographers receive credit on a dedicated promotional page on the Shutter Hub site with a link to their portfolio or social media; the book itself is sold through Shutter Hub's shop and stockists. Photographers retain copyright. The publication does not pay royalties or send complimentary copies; it does forward commission inquiries directly to the photographer.

Submissions are pay-what-you-can with a £15 minimum donation; free submissions are available on request for photographers with limited income. Each photographer can submit up to 10 images as JPEGs (300dpi, CMYK, max 5MB), with filenames structured as lastname_firstname_imagetitle.jpg. Diptychs and triptychs are submitted as separate images.
AI use must be disclosed in the submission. Family-appropriate work only. The deadline is 5pm UK time on June 11, 2026; results are announced September 2026.

calls.title: Appalachian Nature Art & Photography Competition & Exhibition
calls.description: Regional competition celebrating the beauty of nature across the Appalachian region. Photography-specific awards include Best of Show Photography ($500), Best Landscape Photography ($250), and Best Living Thing Photography ($250), plus a People's Choice Award ($250). Two-dimensional artwork or photography depicting Appalachian nature — landscapes, plants, wildlife, and other natural subjects from any Appalachian state. Exhibition May 15 – June 20, 2026 at Arcadian Gallery in Cumberland, MD. Juried by Steven David Johnson (photography) and Terry Miller (art).
calls.summary: Appalachian nature photography. $500 Best of Show plus landscape and wildlife awards. MD, PA, VA, WV, DC residents.

calls.title: NOVA24 2026 Project Open Call
calls.description: Third edition of an indie photo and film festival in Detroit. Open call for photographers and filmmakers to present experimental and innovative work. Selected projects exhibited during the festival across indoor and outdoor projection galleries, mural installations, gallery exhibitions, film screenings, and artist talks. Festival runs June 26 – July 31, 2026 across multiple Detroit venues. Founded in 2023 to connect Detroit's lens-based creative community with international audiences.
calls.summary: Indie photo + film festival in Detroit. Projections, gallery shows, screenings. Experimental and innovative work. June–July 2026.

calls.title: Archifoto 2026 — Architecture & Landscape
calls.description: Eighth edition of the European architectural photography competition organised by La Chambre and Maison Européenne de l'Architecture – Rhin supérieur. Theme: Architecture & Landscape — photographs revealing complementarities or tensions between architecture and landscape, exploring how they shape territories and communities amid climate and demographic changes. Five nominees each receive €500 and are exhibited at La Chambre in Strasbourg in autumn 2026, with touring exhibitions across partner venues in the Upper Rhine region. Running since 2010, combining documentary and artistic perspectives on current architectural issues.
calls.summary: European architectural photography award, 8th edition. Theme: Architecture & Landscape. €500 per nominee + exhibition in Strasbourg.
prose: Archifoto is a European architectural photography competition founded in 2010 by La Chambre, the Strasbourg-based photography organization, in partnership with Maison Européenne de l'Architecture – Rhin supérieur. The competition is biennial and tied to the Les Journées de l'architecture festival in the Upper Rhine region.

The 2026 cycle is the 8th edition. The theme is "Architecture & Landscape" — the call invites photographs revealing complementarities or tensions between built and natural environments, exploring how they shape territories and communities amid climate and demographic change. Documentary and artistic approaches are equally welcome.

Five nominees are selected per edition. Each receives €500 plus exhibition at La Chambre in Strasbourg (4 place d'Austerlitz) in autumn 2026, with touring exhibitions across partner venues in the Upper Rhine region — meaning selected work appears across multiple French and German cities.

Eligibility is restricted to photographers based in Europe aged 18 and over. Entry fee is €10 per submission of up to 5 images. The 2026 deadline is June 1, 2026 at midnight; results announced June 2026.

calls.title: 2026 Booooooom Art & Photo Book Award
calls.description: Annual award selecting 6 book projects and 2 zine projects for fully funded publication in partnership with Bookmobile. Books up to 100 pages and 10×10 inches, printed in 100 copies. Zines up to 36 pages, 5×7 inches, printed in 25 copies. Open to all artists, illustrators, and photographers. Non-members may submit one free zine proposal or pay $20 for a book proposal. Members submit unlimited at no extra cost.
calls.summary: 8 projects (6 books, 2 zines) fully published for free. Books 100 copies, zines 25 copies. Free zine entry.
prose: Booooooom is the long-running art and photography platform run by Jeff Hamada. The Annual Art & Photo Book Award is its flagship publishing program, run in partnership with Bookmobile — the Minneapolis-based printing and distribution company founded in 1982.

The 2026 cycle selects 8 projects total: 6 for full book publication and 2 for perfect-bound zines. The book format is up to 100 pages at up to 10×10 inches, printed in editions of up to 100 copies. The zine format is up to 36 pages at 5×7 inches, printed in editions of 25 copies.

Books and zines are published at zero cost to the artist, and winners retain full creative control: "These will be your books, not ours, so each of you will have full control of the design and layout." The publishing partnership covers printing, with the artist retaining their print run for sale or distribution.

Submission requires 10 images of the proposed project at maximum 2500×2500 pixels with the filename format FIRSTNAME_LASTNAME_01.JPG. Non-members may submit one free zine proposal or pay $20 for a book proposal. Booooooom members may submit unlimited proposals at no additional cost. The 2026 deadline is June 5 at 11:59 PM PST; results announced August 2026 (selection takes a minimum of 8 weeks).

calls.title: Nachleben 2026
calls.description: Open call for the Nachleben photography festival in Verona, Italy, September 2026. Three photographers or collectives selected for exhibition. Selected artists receive two nights accommodation during opening weekend, meals, travel reimbursement up to €300, and a production budget of up to €1,000 for prints and installation. Open to photographers of any age. No thematic restrictions — jury selects on artistic merit.
jury: Aida Redžepagić, Founder & Director, Sarajevo Photography Festival
Jelena Janković, Program Director, Sarajevo Photography Festival
David Pujado, Founder, Belgrade Photo Month
Simone Azzoni, Co-founder & Artistic Director, Grenze
Francesca Marra, President & Co-Artistic Director, Grenze
calls.summary: Three photographers exhibited at September festival in Verona. €300 travel + €1,000 print budget + accommodation.

calls.title: Lucky Star Issue 5: Camera-Less
calls.description: Fifth issue of San Francisco indie photography magazine dedicated to camera-less and alternative photographic processes. Exploring experimental, often abstract methods including pinhole, lumen, cyanotype, chemigram, photogram, chlorophyll printing and more. Artists challenged to put down the camera and consider the physicality of making an image. Cohesive bodies or series of work encouraged and prioritised. Files must be at least 300 DPI, ready-to-print. Magazine printed at 6×9 inches with potential 9×12 inch full spreads. Artists whose work is accepted contacted via email within a week after deadline. Submissions from artists featured in previous issues considered last.
calls.summary: SF indie zine exploring camera-less photography — pinhole, cyanotype, chemigram, photogram, lumen and more. Free to submit.

calls.title: From Image to Meaning – Tirana
calls.description: Three full grants available for a seven-day intensive visual storytelling and writing workshop in Tirana, Albania (25–31 May 2026). Open to emerging and mid-career photographers, filmmakers, writers, and journalists working at the intersection of image and text. Led by documentary photographer Ilir Tsouko and writer Gabriel Proedl. Participants research, produce, edit, and present a short story combining photography, video (optional), and text. Culminates in a public group exhibition and presentation at Vila 31 x Art Explora. Selected projects (2–3) prepared for pitching to editors in Europe and the United States. Grants cover the full €750 participation fee (1 photographer, 1 writer, 1 filmmaker). Maximum 15 participants. Working language English, one-to-one mentoring also available in German and Greek/Albanian. Organised by Reporter Akademie (Germany) in partnership with Vila 31 x Art Explora (Tirana).
calls.summary: 3 full grants for a 7-day visual storytelling workshop in Tirana. Exhibition at Vila 31 x Art Explora. Projects pitched to editors.

calls.title: Creative Capital Award 2027
calls.description: Major annual grant supporting ambitious, risk-taking projects by individual artists across all disciplines including photography and visual arts. Now in its 27th year, Creative Capital has committed over $60 million to 750+ projects. Three-round application process: Round I project proposal, Round II detailed materials, Round III panel review. Main award provides $15,000–$50,000 in project funding plus advisory services and career development support. Additionally, the new State of the Art Prize awards $10,000 unrestricted grants to individual artists. Open to US citizens, permanent residents, Tribal ID holders, or O-1 visa holders aged 25+ with at least 5 years of professional artistic practice. Must not be enrolled in a degree-granting program. Round I deadline April 2, 2026 at 3 PM ET.
calls.summary: One of the US's largest arts grants. $15K–$50K for ambitious projects across all visual arts incl. photography. 5+ yrs experience required.

calls.title: La Napoule Art Foundation — Fall Residency 2026
calls.description: One-month international artist residency at a historic château on the French Riviera, overlooking the Mediterranean Sea. Open to emerging and established artists of all disciplines including photography, aged 18+, with no limitation on nationality. Residents receive accommodations in the château, a private studio workspace, daily breakfast, and most evening meals. Participants must communicate effectively in English or French. Residency dates October 6 – November 3, 2026. Applications evaluated on artistic vision, professional commitment, work quality, project significance, and collaborative willingness. Artists may apply once per calendar year; previous recipients may reapply but are given lower priority. Note: the historic château is not handicapped accessible.
calls.summary: One-month residency at a château on the French Riviera. Accommodation, meals, and private studio included. All disciplines welcome.

calls.title: Open Call for Emerging Artists
calls.description: Open call for emerging Maltese and Malta-based visual artists working in painting, sculpture, installation, video, ceramics, photography or across disciplines. An invitation to share current work and practice direction. Oriented towards work that can be exhibited and made available for sale. May lead to opportunities in upcoming exhibitions, projects or residencies from July 2026 onwards. Intended for emerging artists with some experience presenting work in exhibitions independently. Organised by Elyse Tonna, curator, architect and artistic director of axis_ art gallery in Malta.
calls.summary: Open call for emerging Maltese/Malta-based visual artists. Exhibition, project and residency opportunities from July 2026.

calls.title: UN World Oceans Day Photo Competition 2026
calls.description: 13th annual photo competition coordinated by the UN Division for Ocean Affairs and the Law of the Sea, DivePhotoGuide, UNESCO Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission, and Nausicaá. Free and open to all skill levels worldwide. Four categories: Connecting Oceans (images demonstrating connections between oceanic ecosystems, species and people), Big and Small Underwater Faces (marine life portraits), Underwater Seascapes (minimum 50% of image underwater), and Above Water Seascapes (ocean-dependent landscapes from above). One image per category. Winners announced June 8 at the UN World Oceans Day event in New York. Winning images printed for global exhibitions. Participants must comply with an ethics charter regarding animal welfare and environmental protection. JPEG format, 2,000–6,000px longest dimension, max 4.9 MB.
calls.summary: Free UN-backed ocean photography competition. 4 categories incl. above-water seascapes. Winners exhibited globally, announced at UN event.

calls.title: Anonymous Was A Woman Environmental Art Grants 2026
calls.description: Grants of up to $20,000 for environmental art projects led by women, transgender, and gender-nonconforming artists based in the United States or US territories. Over $470,000 in total funding for the 2026 cycle. All artistic disciplines eligible including photography and visual arts. Projects must already be in development at the time of application and must include a free public engagement component within the grant term. US citizenship not required but US residency is. Administered by the New York Foundation for the Arts (NYFA). One of the most significant arts grants available for women and gender-nonconforming artists working on environmental themes.
calls.summary: Up to $20K grants for environmental art by women/trans/GNC artists in the US. $470K+ total. All visual arts incl. photography.

calls.title: Black and White Photo Awards 2026
calls.description: International black-and-white photography competition now in its fifth edition. Six categories: Architecture, Street, Portrait, Fauna and Flora, Landscape, and a new Open Theme. Each €15 registration allows five images per chosen category. Absolute winner receives €1,500 cash, plus €200 for the best photograph in each category and 15 honourable mentions. Winning and finalist images published in the annual Black and White Photo Awards book. Open to all photographers worldwide aged 18+. Submissions via the official website.
calls.summary: International B&W competition — 6 categories incl. Architecture, Street, Landscape. €1,500 absolute winner + €200 per category.
prose: The Black and White Photo Awards is an international competition exclusively for black-and-white photography, now in its fifth edition. The total prize pool is over €5,500.

Submissions are accepted across six categories: Architecture, Street, Portrait, Fauna and Flora, Landscape, and Open Theme (new for 2026). Each €15 registration entitles the photographer to submit five images in one category, and applicants may submit to multiple categories with separate registrations.

Cash awards: an Absolute Winner receives €1,500, with each of the six category winners receiving €200. The Street and Portrait category winners additionally receive access to the Retouch4me photo editing suite. At least 15 honourable mentions are also recognized. Winning and finalist images are published in the annual Black and White Photo Awards book — the printed catalogue functions as the long-term archive of each year's selection.

The 2026 jury comprises Joel Tjintjelaar (B&W fine-art photographer), Julia Anna Gospodarou (architecture photographer), Charles Paul Azzopardi (President of the Malta Institute of Professional Photography), Kazutoshi Kawakami (IPA Awards winner), and Néstor Rodan (Victory Photo Serbia Awards winner).
AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility is open to professional and amateur photographers worldwide aged 18 or over. The 2026 deadline is June 15.

calls.title: British Wildlife Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: Annual photography competition celebrating the diversity and beauty of British wildlife, now in its fourteenth year. Open to photographers worldwide, but all images must be taken in Britain or the British Isles. Twelve categories including Animal Behaviour, Animal Portraits, Botanical Britain, Black and White, British Seasons, Coast and Marine, Habitat, Hidden Britain, Urban Wildlife, Wild Woods, Documentary Series, and Video. Photos must be taken after January 1, 2019. Youth competition (17 and under) is free to enter. Winners announced March 2027 and featured in the Collection 14 coffee table book and a UK touring exhibition. Post-processing permitted but no compositing, sky swapping, or object removal. Proceeds from auction of award-winning prints donated to Birds on the Brink charity. AI-generated images strictly prohibited.
calls.summary: UK wildlife photography awards — 12 categories. Winners in Collection 14 book + UK touring exhibition. Youth entry free.
jury: Lara Jackson, Conservation Biologist & Wildlife Photographer
Will Nicholls, BWPA Director & Wildlife Cameraman
prose: The British Wildlife Photography Awards (BWPA) is now in its 15th year and one of the more long-running UK wildlife photography competitions. The awards run with director Will Nicholls and cover the breadth of British nature photography across twelve categories.

Categories: Animal Behaviour, Animal Portraits, Botanical Britain, Black and White, British Seasons, Coast and Marine, Habitat, Hidden Britain, Urban Wildlife, Wild Woods, Documentary Series, and Video. The £10,000 main prize is awarded across the program. Photos must be taken in Britain or the British Isles, made after January 1, 2019, and the rules forbid compositing, sky swapping, or object removal — post-processing is permitted within those constraints. AI-generated work is strictly prohibited.

Eligibility is open globally — photographers from anywhere can submit, provided the images themselves were taken in the British Isles. The Youth competition (17 and under) is free to enter; the adult competition fee is £35 to £40 depending on category and entry tier.

Selected work tours the UK as a traveling exhibition and is published in the Collection 14 coffee-table book. Proceeds from the auction of award-winning prints are donated to Birds on the Brink charity.

The 2026 jury comprises wildlife photographers Ellie Rothnie, David Chapman, Lara Jackson (also a conservation biologist), Neil McIntyre, Danny Green, underwater photographer Gina Goodman, and BWPA Director and wildlife cameraman Will Nicholls. The 2026 deadline is June 7; winners announced March 2027.

calls.title: JGS Fellowship for Photography 2026
calls.org: New York Foundation for the Arts
calls.description: Annual fellowship awarding $8,000 each to five photographers working in New York State outside New York City. Supports traditional and experimental photography including light-based work, alternative processes, or any form in which photography or photographic techniques are pivotal. Applicants must be 25 or older, current full-time residents of eligible NY State regions for at least 12 months, and not enrolled in a degree-seeking programme. Past recipients are not eligible. Applications submitted via Submittable. Notification of results in summer 2026.
calls.summary: $8,000 fellowship for 5 NY State photographers (outside NYC). Supports traditional, experimental, and alternative process photography.

calls.title: 12th Annual International Open Call
calls.org: Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts
calls.description: International showcase for contemporary voices in photography with no theme or prompt, bringing together image makers from around the world to survey current photographic practice. Open to all photographers 18+ worldwide working in any photographic process or technique. Juried by Crista Dix, Executive Director of the Griffin Museum of Photography. Up to 15 photographs accepted per entry. Exhibition at RICPA gallery in Providence, Rhode Island from July 16 through August 15, 2026. Opening reception July 16. Members receive 20% discount on entry fees. Work must be exhibition-ready, maximum 48 inches including frame. Delivery of accepted work by July 11.
jury: Crista Dix, Executive Director, Griffin Museum of Photography
calls.summary: International open call — no theme. Juried by Crista Dix (Griffin Museum). Exhibition in Providence, RI. Cash prizes.

calls.title: Tulsa Artist Fellowship 2027–2029
calls.description: Three-year fellowship for visual artists in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Ten fellows selected from an open call. Each receives a $150,000 project development stipend, $36,000 housing stipend, fully subsidized private studio (337–583 sq ft), $3,600 studio assistant stipend, and $3,600 health/wellness stipend. Access to shared ceramics studio, woodshop, metal equipment, media lab, archival printer, performance space, and podcast studio. Fellows must relocate to Tulsa for the full three-year term (January 2027–December 2029). Applicants must be 25+ with at least five years of experience in the arts and a project proposal with community engagement focus. U.S. citizens, permanent residents, O-1 visa holders, or Tribal ID holders eligible. Applications open April 7, 2026.
calls.summary: Three-year fellowship: $150,000 stipend, housing, and studio in Tulsa. Ten fellows selected. Age 25+, must relocate.

calls.title: Women's Studio Workshop — Studio Workspace Residency
calls.description: 4–6 week residency for artists at any career stage at Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, NY. Choose from five studios: intaglio, letterpress, papermaking, screenprinting, or darkroom photography. Housing and studio space fully subsidized. Staff assistance available. Artists work independently and provide their own materials. Residencies take place September through June, 1–2 years after application.
calls.summary: 4–6 week residency with free housing and studio. Darkroom, letterpress, intaglio, screenprint, or papermaking.

calls.title: PowerLines Documentary Photography Fellowship
calls.description: Three-month documentary photography fellowship from PowerLines, a national nonprofit focused on modernizing public utilities. The fellow documents the human experience of rising utility costs across the United States. $30,000 stipend distributed over three months (May 15 – August 15, 2026). Joint ownership of all images produced. Fellows may accept non-conflicting external assignments during the fellowship. Applicants must have at least three years of professional documentary or photojournalism experience.
calls.summary: $30,000 documentary fellowship. Three months documenting the impact of rising utility costs on US communities.

calls.title: Global Peace Photo Award 2026
calls.description: Annual international award recognizing photographs that express the idea of peaceful coexistence. Open to all photographers worldwide. Winners receive the Alfred Fried Peace Medal, cash prizes, and travel and accommodation to the award ceremony at the Austrian Parliament in Vienna (September 24, 2026). Submissions may be single photographs or photo projects with up to 12 images per project. All submissions may be included in international exhibitions. Separate Children's Peace Image category for photographers under 15.
jury: Lars Boering, Managing Director, European Journalism Centre
Pablo Corral Vega, Photographer & Founder, POY Latam
Cyril Drouhet, Director of Photography, Le Figaro Magazine
Magdalena Herrera, Director of Photography, GEO
Gerd Ludwig, Photographer, National Geographic Creative
Lois Lammerhuber, Photographer & Publisher, Edition Lammerhuber
calls.summary: Free award for photos of peaceful coexistence. €11,000 in prizes, Alfred Fried Peace Medal, Vienna ceremony.

calls.title: Working Assumptions Project Grants 2026
calls.description: Six $10,000 unrestricted grants awarded annually to support photography-based projects that inspire audiences to look at family in new, meaningful ways. Proposals may employ photography or photo-based art for journalistic, artistic, therapeutic, educational, or research purposes. Projects must have been initiated prior to the application deadline. Grant period runs October 2026 to June 2027. Application window opens May 1, 2026.
calls.summary: Six $10,000 grants for photography projects exploring family. Unrestricted funding for journalistic, artistic, or educational work.
prose: Working Assumptions is a Berkeley-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit foundation focused on supporting visual storytelling about family — broadly defined. The organization funds photography and photo-based art that engages with family across journalistic, artistic, therapeutic, educational, and research purposes.

The Project Grants program awards six unrestricted $10,000 grants annually. The grant is genuinely unrestricted — recipients are free to use the funds for any aspect of project execution, with no required reporting against specific budget categories.

Eligibility requires that projects be intended for public consumption and that the work has begun prior to the application deadline (the foundation supports projects in progress rather than purely speculative proposals). Creative approach is unrestricted.

The 2026 grant period runs October 2026 through June 2027. The application window opens May 1, 2026 and closes June 1, 2026, with results announced September 2026. Specific entry fees, jury composition, and detailed eligibility criteria are not disclosed on the public landing page; applicants should consult the linked grant-information page or email grants@workingassumptions.org for current details before applying.

calls.title: Barbara Spohr Memorial Award for Photography 2027
calls.org: Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity
calls.description: Annual award supporting Canadian contemporary photography. One mid-career photographer receives a fully funded month-long self-directed residency at Banff Centre (January 18 – February 12, 2027). Access to the Crich Studio with private black and white analogue darkroom, facilitated digital print production, and technical photography support. Full scholarship covering tuition, single accommodation, and meal plan ($7,600 CAD value). $1,000 CAD materials allowance plus travel bursary. Applicants must have a minimum of ten exhibitions in a professional context and 8–15 years of professional arts experience.
calls.summary: Fully funded month-long photography residency at Banff Centre. $1,000 materials + travel bursary. For mid-career Canadian photographers.
prose: The Barbara Spohr Memorial Award is administered by the Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity in Banff, Alberta, established by the friends and family of the late artist Barbara Spohr. The award supports Canadian contemporary photography through a fully funded, self-directed month-long residency at Banff's Leighton Artists Studios complex.

The 2027 residency runs January 18 through February 12 (with arrival January 17 and departure February 13). The selected photographer works in the Crich Studio, which includes private black-and-white analogue darkroom facilities; digital print production and on-site technical photography support are also available. Studio access is 24/7, with full access to the Banff Centre's broader campus facilities including fitness center and library.

Funding covers tuition, single accommodation, and meal plan — a 100% scholarship valued at approximately $7,600.95 CAD. The award also includes a $1,000 CAD materials allowance (issued as a cheque) and a travel bursary with regional maximums.

Eligibility is restricted: Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or Jay Treaty eligible; aged 18 or over; mid-career, defined as a minimum of 10 exhibitions in a professional context and 8 to 15 years of professional photography experience. Strong darkroom proficiency is required. Previous recipients of this specific residency are not eligible to apply again. The application fee is $35 CAD (non-refundable). Applications go through SlideRoom; the deadline is June 17, 2026 at 11:59 PM MST.

calls.title: Joy and the Everyday 2026
calls.description: Themed exhibition exploring how photographers capture joy in everyday moments. Juried by Emilia Mickevicius, Ph.D., Norton Family Assistant Curator of Photography at the Center for Creative Photography. 24 images selected for print exhibition in the Maloof Gallery at APG, Atlanta, June 16 – July 17, 2026. Open to APG members. Scholarships available.
calls.summary: Themed exhibition on everyday joy. 24 prints selected for APG Maloof Gallery, Atlanta. Juried by CCP curator.
jury: Emilia Mickevicius, Ph.D., Center for Creative Photography

calls.title: #filmisnotdead 2026
calls.description: Juried exhibition celebrating analog photography. Open to all traditional processes including film, wet plate, cyanotype, and other analog techniques. No theme — open subject matter. Juried by Michael Behlen, Founder and Publisher of Analog Forever Magazine. 30 images selected for the Main Gallery at APG, Atlanta, June 16 – July 17, 2026. Open to APG members. Scholarships available.
calls.summary: Analog photography exhibition, open subject. 30 prints selected for APG Main Gallery, Atlanta. Juried by Analog Forever Magazine.

calls.title: Apparently in America — Artist Award 2026
calls.description: Photography award exploring the myth and meaning of American identity today. Submit 10–20 images reflecting on cultural, political, and personal dimensions of U.S. identity. $500 prize for selected artist plus up to three honorable mentions. Fee waivers available for those experiencing financial hardship. Founded by curator Francesca Hummler.
calls.summary: Photography award on American identity. $500 prize. Fee waivers available. Founded by curator Francesca Hummler.
jury: Cali M. Banks, Light Work / Syracuse University
Francesca Hummler, Apparently in America / Der Greif
prose: Apparently, in America is a photography award founded by curator Francesca Hummler that explores the myth and meaning of American-ness through a single rhetorical prompt. Photographers complete the phrase "Apparently, in America…" through both their work and project description — submissions must include the literal phrase as part of their statement.

One artist receives the $500 main prize plus featured placement on the Apparently in America platform; up to three honorable mentions are also selected. Selection criteria are explicit: conceptual strength, visual coherence, and how thoughtfully the work engages with the theme of American identity in cultural, political, and personal dimensions.

Submissions require 10 to 20 images per applicant, all original work not previously featured by the initiative. The entry fee is $10, with waivers available by email request for those experiencing financial hardship. Open internationally to photographers.

The 2026 jury comprises Cali M. Banks (Light Work / Syracuse University), Leah DeVun (Rutgers University), William Camargo (Pasadena City College), and Francesca Hummler (founder, also affiliated with Der Greif). The deadline is July 4, 2026 at 9:59 PM; results announced September 1.

calls.title: Project Space Residency 2027
calls.description: Four-week residency for photographers, filmmakers, and media artists in Rochester, NY. Up to 12 residents selected annually. $1,000 stipend, $250 supply budget, $500 travel budget for non-local residents. Private studio with 24/7 access, analog darkroom, digital printing, and accessible housing. Curator consultations and public engagement opportunities. Over 50 years of supporting experimental work. Fee waivers available.
calls.summary: Four-week residency with $1,000 stipend, studio, darkroom, and housing. For photographers, filmmakers, media artists.
jury: Aspen Mays, Artist, California College of Art
Le'Andra LeSeur, Artist, Tulsa Artist Fellow

calls.title: Delfina Foundation — India Residency 2026
calls.description: Twelve-week fully funded residency at the Delfina Foundation in London for contemporary visual artists based in India. Supported by The Charles Wallace India Trust and The Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation. Residency runs January 5 to March 28, 2027 (winter season). Apply via Cognito Forms — read the Guidance Notes document before applying.
calls.summary: Fully funded 12-week residency in London for visual artists based in India. Winter 2027 season.

calls.title: The Flow 2026 Photo Contest
calls.description: Annual photo contest presented by Kodak with $50,000 in total prizes across five categories: Film, Surf, Nature, Energy, and Oneness. Grand prize of $4,000 per category, plus finalist and honorable mention awards. Open to professional and amateur photographers worldwide. All entries considered for publication in The Photo Issue of Flow Trip Magazine. Winners announced June 2026. AI-generated or AI-altered images not accepted.
calls.summary: Kodak-presented contest. $50,000 in prizes across 5 categories (Film, Surf, Nature, Energy, Oneness). $6/image.

calls.title: Artadia Awards 2026 — San Francisco Bay Area
calls.description: Unrestricted merit-based grants for contemporary visual artists including photographers. Three awardees receive $15,000 each. Two-round jury process: curators review applications, then conduct 45-minute virtual studio visits with finalists. Applicants must have resided in one of nine Bay Area counties for at least two years. Cannot be enrolled in an art degree program or have previously received Artadia awards of $10,000 or more. Application period: May 1 – June 1, 2026.
calls.summary: Unrestricted $15,000 grants for contemporary visual artists in SF Bay Area. Two-round jury with studio visits.

calls.title: Fieldwork Photo Journal — Issue Two: The Embodied Weight of Place
calls.description: Print publication exploring how place is not experienced neutrally — landscapes, interiors, and built environments carry histories that shape how they are felt. Featured photographer: Kristine Potter. Up to 30 photographers selected. First 6 images included in fee, additional images $5 each (max 12). JPG only, longest edge 1500px at 150 dpi. Publication date: Fall/Winter 2026.
calls.summary: Print publication on place, memory, and history. Featured: Kristine Potter. Up to 30 photographers selected.
jury: Sam Angel, Founder, Fieldwork Photo Journal

calls.title: Pearl Press — Issue No. 28: Utopia
calls.description: Online publication open call themed 'Utopia' — escapism, joy, acceptance, community. Submit via email with name, short bio, title and description of work. Visual work must be at least 300 dpi. No min or max on number of submissions. Selected work published in Issue No. 28 and featured on Instagram.
calls.summary: Free digital publication themed 'Utopia.' Submit visual or written work via email. No limit on submissions.

calls.title: Mangrove Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: Annual international conservation photography competition celebrating the beauty and importance of mangrove ecosystems. Six categories: Wildlife, People, Landscape, Threats, Underwater, and Conservation Stories (portfolio of 6 images). Overall Mangrove Photographer of the Year receives $1,000; category winners $250–$750. Young Mangrove Photographer of the Year for entrants aged 23 and under. People's Choice Award announced in August. Free entry, open to all photographers worldwide, any age and skill level. Judged by Esther Horvath, Karine Aigner, and Dhritiman Mukherjee.
calls.summary: Free conservation photography awards — 6 categories. $1,000 Photographer of the Year + category prizes. Young photographer award.

calls.title: Better Photography Magazine Photographer of the Year 2026
calls.description: 19th edition of Australia's premier photography competition. Four categories: Emotive Portraiture, Classic Landscapes, Revealing Nature, and Open. Every entry professionally scored by three AIPP Grand Masters of Photography with written feedback. Bronze, Silver, and Gold designations awarded based on quality. Category winners receive AUD $750 each; overall Photographer of the Year receives AUD $2,000. Entrants with four or more images eligible for the overall award. International entries welcome.
calls.summary: 19th edition. Four categories judged by AIPP Grand Masters with individual feedback. AUD $5,000 total prizes.
jury: Tony Hewitt, AIPP Grand Master of Photography
David Oliver, AIPP Grand Master of Photography
Peter Eastway, Publisher of Better Photography Magazine

calls.title: nice;04
calls.description: Fourth annual Midwest Nice Art national juried exhibition. Open theme — a survey of contemporary artists exploring personal and social narratives. Juried by co-founders Tim Rickett and Epiphany Knedler. First prize $300, second $200, third $100, four honorable mentions at $50 each. Physical exhibition at JFAC Gallery, Northern State University, Aberdeen, South Dakota (July 13–September 11, 2026). Work must be framed and ready for exhibition.
jury: Tim Rickett, Co-founder, Midwest Nice Art
Epiphany Knedler, Co-founder, Midwest Nice Art
calls.summary: 4th annual national juried exhibition. $800 in total prizes. JFAC Gallery, Northern State University, SD.

calls.title: Photo of the Season — Worth a Thousand Words
calls.description: Seasonal photography competition inviting powerful standalone images that tell a compelling story. Theme: Worth a Thousand Words — narrative, emotion, and storytelling. Open worldwide. First prize $150, second $100, third $50 plus two honorable mentions. All winners featured in gallery, newsletter, website, and social media. Accepts film, digital, alternative process, and printmaking.
calls.summary: Seasonal competition for narrative-driven images. $150 first prize. The Image Flow gallery, San Anselmo, CA.
prose: The Image Flow is a Bay Area photography gallery and education space at 328 Sir Francis Drake Boulevard in San Anselmo, California. "Photo of the Season" is the gallery's quarterly themed competition for standalone images. The 2026 spring/summer cycle theme is "Worth a Thousand Words" — narrative-driven photography that carries emotional or conceptual depth in a single frame.

Cash prizes are modest but useful: $150 first place, $100 second, $50 third, plus two honorable mentions. The four seasonal competitions of 2026 culminate in a 2027 group exhibition at The Image Flow, in which selected images from across the year are exhibited together — submission to any one season also enters the work into consideration for the year-end show.

Entry fee is $15 for up to three images. Eligibility is open globally to original work. Accepted media include film, digital, alternative process, and printmaking; mixed media, film/video, and AI-generated images are excluded. Selection is by The Image Flow's in-house team, judging on composition, color, contrast, technical quality, point of view, and narrative strength.
Winners are featured on The Image Flow's website, newsletter, and social channels. The 2026 deadline for the "Worth a Thousand Words" cycle is June 20.

calls.title: AAP Magazine #57 Portrait
calls.description: Portrait photography competition exploring humanity through portraiture. Winners receive $1,000 cash, publication in AAP Magazine #57, and global recognition. All styles welcome including studio, candid, self-portraits, and conceptual work. Open to professional and amateur photographers aged 18+. Submit a cohesive body of work or portfolio. Judged on creativity, originality, and visual impact.
jury: Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, Founder & Editor, All About Photo
calls.summary: Portrait photography competition. $1,000 cash prize, publication in AAP Magazine, and global recognition.

calls.title: Dodho Magazine #37
calls.description: International open call for print edition #37 of Dodho Magazine. Conceived as an artistic and curatorial volume rather than a traditional magazine. Each selected photographer receives 20 full pages with visual rhythm, curatorial text, and breathing room for images. Two submission modes: Magazine Mode for a full portfolio feature, or Cover Mode for the front page. International distribution across galleries, festivals, museums, and institutions. 36 prior editions featuring 216 photographers from 32 countries.
calls.summary: Print edition #37. 20 full pages per selected photographer. Distributed to galleries, festivals, and institutions worldwide.
jury: Marcel Kollen, Director, Rotterdam Photo Festival
Paris Chong, Gallery Director & Curator, Leica Gallery Los Angeles

calls.title: Odesa Workshop — Environmental Consequences of War in Ukraine
calls.description: 7-month hybrid workshop for Ukrainian or Ukraine-based documentary photographers documenting the environmental consequences of war. 10–12 participants selected. Program includes online lectures (June 2026), live sessions with international editors and experts, a 3-day in-person lab in Odesa (September 11–13, 2026), and individual mentorship through November 2026. One participant receives a €1,500 production grant. Supported by JournalismFund Europe.
calls.summary: Free 7-month hybrid workshop for Ukrainian photographers on war's environmental impact. €1,500 production grant.
jury: Roman Pilipey, AFP Chief Photographer, Ukraine
Irynka Hromotska, Photo Editor, Kyiv Independent

calls.title: Photobook Open Call
calls.description: Open call for a fully-funded photobook from the Sonntag Grant for Photography, in collaboration with Replika Publishing. One FLINTA (female, lesbian, inter, non-binary, trans, agender) artist is selected to produce a photobook with Replika Publishing (350+ copies, 50 to artist). Book launch at Bildband Berlin with travel up to €300 and accommodation covered. Projects should be finished or at an advanced stage. Berlin-based grant launched in 2025. Open globally.
calls.summary: Photobook open call for FLINTA artists with Replika Publishing. 350+ copy print run. Book launch at Bildband Berlin.

calls.title: After Dark: Night, Sky, and Shadow
calls.description: Juried exhibition of photographs created between dusk and dawn. Night and astrophotography, urban and street scenes, long exposures, light painting, and experimental techniques welcome. Juror: Lance Keimig. Up to 35 images in physical gallery, 40 in online gallery, all in printed catalog.
calls.summary: Night photography exhibition — dusk to dawn. Long exposures, astrophotography, light painting, urban scenes. Middlebury, VT.

calls.title: Camera Work: Shadow and Light
calls.description: Juried group show exploring contemporary interpretations of shadow and light. 26 photographs selected for physical exhibition in Portland, OR; 50 additional for online gallery. All 76 images in purchasable catalog. Free printing, matting, and framing for selected works.
jury: Todd Johnson, Founder & Director, Black Box Gallery
calls.summary: Juried group show exploring shadow and light. 26 prints exhibited in Portland, OR, 50 more online. Free framing.

calls.title: Abundance
calls.description: Exhibition exploring abundance as both presence and paradox — accumulation and scarcity, fullness and absence, wealth and waste. Seeking photographic responses through documentary, staged, abstract, or experimental approaches. Selections based on thematic relevance, technical quality, originality, and artistic vision. Selected artists may have work printed on Canon ImageProGraf Pro-1100 for an additional fee. Exhibition May 1–30, 2026 with opening reception May 1.
calls.summary: Exhibition exploring abundance as presence and paradox. Documentary, staged, abstract, or experimental approaches welcome.

calls.title: XVIII Festival di Fotografia a Capri — Viaggi e Miraggi
calls.description: 18th edition of the annual photography festival at Capri organized by Fondazione Capri. Theme: Viaggi e Miraggi (Journeys and Mirages) — inspired by the 200th anniversary of the rediscovery of the Blue Grotto. Exploring journeys both physical and imagined, where photography becomes a gateway between memory and imagination. Winning project exhibited at Certosa di San Giacomo. Production and installation covered by the foundation. Winners announced July 13. Festival in August 2026, with workshops and educational activities in October 2026. Open to photographers worldwide, professionals and amateurs.
calls.summary: Free photography festival on Capri. Theme: Journeys and Mirages. Winning project exhibited at Certosa di San Giacomo. Open worldwide.
prose: Festival di Fotografia a Capri is an annual photography festival on the island of Capri organized by Fondazione Capri, now in its 18th edition. The 2026 theme is Viaggi e Miraggi — "Journeys and Mirages" — chosen to mark the 200th anniversary of the rediscovery of the Blue Grotto, the sea cave that became the symbol of Romantic-era travel to Capri. The brief invites work that treats photography as the medium between physical journey and imagined place: pilgrimages, returns, displacements, and image-making as a kind of mirage in itself.

Submissions are free. The winning project is exhibited at the Certosa di San Giacomo, the 14th-century Carthusian monastery that serves as Capri's main cultural venue. Production and installation costs are covered by Fondazione Capri.

The festival proper takes place in August 2026, with workshops and educational programming following in October. The selection is curated by Denis Curti — a longtime Italian photography critic and curator who also sits on the Le Stanze della Fotografia jury — and Fondazione Capri's program team.

Open to photographers worldwide, both professionals and amateurs. Submissions are made by email as a single PDF in a .zip archive (maximum 10MB). The 2026 deadline is July 5; winners are announced July 13.

calls.title: Eddie Adams Workshop 2026
calls.description: One of the most prestigious photojournalism programs in the world. 100 emerging photographers selected annually — evenly split between college students and early-career professionals — for a free 4-day seminar in Jeffersonville, NY. Participants work in teams led by top photographers and editors. Late entry available through May 31 at $55. Applicants must be at least 20 years old and have less than six years of full-time professional experience. Photographers holding staff positions at major publications for more than six years are ineligible.
calls.summary: Legendary 4-day photojournalism seminar. 100 selected from emerging photographers. Free once accepted.

calls.title: Marilyn Stafford FotoReportage Award 2026
calls.description: 10th edition. Annual award for professional female photographers towards the completion of a compelling documentary photo essay addressing important social, environmental, economic, or cultural issues. Supported by Nikon. Winner receives £4,000 to support the project. Special celebration of 10 years of the prize in September at POST, Brighton & Hove's new centre for photography. Open globally to female or female-identifying photographers aged 18+ at any career stage. Must have completed at least one previous documentary photo essay and have already started the submitted project.
jury: Andrea Bruce, Photojournalist, NOOR Photo Agency co-owner, Nikon Ambassador
Donna De Cesare, Photojournalist, Associate Professor, University of Texas at Austin
Nina Emett, Director of FotoDocument, Documentary Photographer, Curator
Neo Ntsoma, Photojournalist, Founder of Neo Ntsoma Productions
Isabella Franceschini, 2024 Marilyn Stafford FotoReportage Award winner
calls.summary: £4,000 grant for female documentary photographers. 10th edition. For photo essays on social, environmental, or cultural issues.

calls.title: JGS Fellowship for Photography 2026
calls.org: New York Foundation for the Arts
calls.description: Five $8,000 unrestricted cash grants for artists working in traditional and experimental photography, including light-based work, alternative processes, or any form in which photography or photographic techniques are pivotal. Open to New York State photography artists living and working outside of New York City. Notifications in summer 2026.
calls.summary: Five $8,000 unrestricted grants for photographers in NY State outside NYC. Traditional and experimental photography.

calls.title: Light Work Artist-in-Residence 2027
calls.description: One-month creative residency in Syracuse, New York. Selected artists receive a $7,500 stipend, a furnished artist apartment, 24-hour access to state-of-the-art facilities, and staff support. Work published in a special edition of Contact Sheet: The Light Work Annual with a commissioned essay. Open to all artists working in photography or image-based media from any country. 12–15 artists selected annually. Notifications by December 2026.
calls.summary: One-month residency with $7,500 stipend and furnished apartment. Published in Contact Sheet. Open worldwide.
prose: Light Work is a non-profit photography center in Syracuse, New York, founded in 1973. Its Artist-in-Residence program — running for over five decades and counting more than 400 alumni — is one of the longest-running photography residencies in the United States. Past residents have included photographers who went on to MacArthur Fellowships, museum acquisitions, and major editorial careers; the alumni list is treated as part of the program's identity.

Each cycle, twelve to fifteen artists are selected for a one-month residency at Light Work's facility (316 Waverly Avenue, Syracuse). Residents receive a $7,500 stipend, a furnished apartment near campus, 24-hour access to Light Work's digital lab and darkroom, and on-staff support. Each resident's work is published in Contact Sheet, Light Work's annual publication, with a commissioned essay.

Eligibility is open globally to artists working in photography or image-based media. There is no application fee. The program is in partnership with Autograph ABP and the Darryl Chappell Foundation, which jointly support specific residency lines for British photographers and Black photographers respectively.

Applications are submitted through SlideRoom (with a physical mail option for those who require it). The 2027 cycle deadline is July 1, 2026. The selection committee reviews applications in late fall, with notifications sent in December.

calls.title: Doug Pensinger Photography Fund 2026
calls.description: Seven $5,000 grants plus yearlong mentorships from industry professionals for emerging sports photographers. The only nonprofit dedicated to providing career development opportunities to emerging sports photographers. Past grantees range from high school students to recent graduates working as freelancers or interns. Applications close May 1.
calls.summary: Seven $5,000 grants plus mentorships for emerging sports photographers. Only nonprofit dedicated to sports photography careers.

calls.title: The Paula Riff Award 2026
calls.description: Annual award honoring artist Paula Riff's legacy, recognizing artists who challenge conventional photography through lensless photography, historical/alternative photographic processes, or physical intervention such as cutting, sewing, and collage. Created in 2021 by the Center for Photographic Art and Lenscratch. $1,000 prize plus featured on Lenscratch and the CPA website. Related group exhibition Changing the Narrative: the First 5 Years of Paula Riff Award Winners opens June 20 at CPA in Carmel. Open internationally to artists working at any career stage.
jury: Tarrah von Lintel, Von Lintel Gallery
calls.summary: Award for alternative/experimental photography — lensless, historical processes, physical intervention. $1,000 + Lenscratch feature.

calls.title: Dek Unu Magazine — June & July 2026 Issue
calls.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online paperback. All fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome. One artist selected for the combined June/July double issue. Technical excellence paired with artistic vision and conceptual intent.
calls.summary: Not-for-profit journal publishing one artist per issue in print and online. June/July double issue. Free, email submissions.

calls.title: Shutter Hub Editions Photobook Award 2026
calls.description: Photobook award from Shutter Hub Editions celebrating bold storytelling and compelling visual narratives. Particularly welcomes photographers creating their first book. Selected by Karen Harvey MBE, Founder and Creative Director of Shutter Hub. A shortlist of six photographers will be celebrated with a dedicated feature, and selected photographers are invited to contribute a Close Up feature, reaching an audience of over 500,000 people. Winning book published by Shutter Hub Editions with 40% commission on profits paid to the photographer. Submit a written proposal and a PDF with 20+ images.
jury: Karen Harvey MBE, Founder & Creative Director, Shutter Hub
calls.summary: Photobook award from Shutter Hub Editions. First-book photographers welcome. Publication + Close Up feature to 500K audience.

calls.title: VCCA Phillip and Edith Leonian Foundation Fellowship in Photography
calls.org: Virginia Center for the Creative Arts
calls.description: Two-week fully-funded residency at Mt. San Angelo in Amherst, Virginia for US citizens or permanent residents. Supported by the Phillip and Edith Leonian Foundation, established in 2009 to support photographic education and documentary photography. Includes private bedroom with en-suite bath, individual studio space plus darkroom access, and three meals daily in a cross-disciplinary community. Residency dates available May 1 – August 31, 2027. Applications open June 1, 2026. Fee waivers available on request by September 10, 2026. Apply via SlideRoom.
