calls.summary: Two-week fully-funded photography residency at Mt. San Angelo, Virginia. Private studio + darkroom. Meals and housing included.
prose: The Phillip and Edith Leonian Foundation Fellowship is a fully-funded two-week photography residency at Mt. San Angelo, the Virginia Center for the Creative Arts (VCCA) campus in Amherst, Virginia. The fellowship is supported by the Leonian Foundation, established in 2009 to fund photographic education and documentary photography. Recent fellows include Bing Guan and Sha Luo.

Each fellow receives a private bedroom with en-suite bathroom, an individual studio plus access to VCCA's darkroom, and three meals daily prepared by the campus kitchen. The residency runs in a cross-disciplinary cohort — photographers stay alongside writers, composers, and visual artists working in other media — which VCCA treats as part of the program rather than incidental to it.

The fellowship is restricted to U.S. citizens and permanent residents whose primary discipline is photography. Residency dates available for the 2027 cycle run May 1 through August 31. Applications open June 1, 2026 and close September 15, 2026; fellows are notified December 31, 2026.

The application fee is $30, with waivers available upon request (waiver requests must be emailed by September 10). Applications go through SlideRoom under "Application for Mt. San Angelo Residencies, VCCA in Virginia – Summer 2027."

calls.title: VISUAL Carlow 2027 Exhibition Open Call
calls.description: Open call for exhibition proposals at VISUAL Centre for Contemporary Art in Carlow, Ireland, for a new commission in September 2027. Open to artists of all career stages working in any media, locally, in Ireland, or internationally — duos and groups welcome. Winning applicant receives a generous artist fee, significant production budget, and curatorial, production, technical, and marketing support. Shortlisted artists receive expansion fees to develop extended proposals. Four gallery spaces available (Main, Link, Studio, Digital). New commission only — existing work ineligible. Shortlist announced end of June 2026; expanded proposals due end of August 2026; winner announced September 2026.
jury: Aileen Nolan, Carlow County Arts Officer
Benjamin Stafford, Visual Arts Curator, VISUAL
Sepake Angiama, Artistic Director, Institute of International Visual Arts
calls.summary: Major new commission for 2027 exhibition at VISUAL Carlow. Any medium. Artist fee + significant production budget.

calls.title: Nordic Artists' Centre Dale 2027 Residency
calls.description: Two-to-four-month residency in 2027 at NKD, a non-profit centre funded by the Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality in the village of Dale, Fjaler on Norway's west coast. Established 1998. Residents receive a monthly grant of NOK 11,000, up to NOK 5,000 in travel reimbursement, and free accommodation in a private residence house plus a 50m² studio with 6-metre ceilings and north-lit panorama windows. Open to professional visual artists, designers, and architects (photographers welcome). Not available to students or practitioners in music, writing, dance, or theatre. Residents give a presentation and participate in an open studio day.
calls.summary: 2–4 month residency in Dale, Norway. Monthly grant NOK 11,000, travel covered, free private house and 50m² studio.

calls.title: Cavendish Arts Science Fellowship 2026–27
calls.description: Annual fellowship in partnership with Girton College, Cambridge, supporting artists to engage with physicists and others at the Cavendish Laboratory. Runs October 2026 – October 2027 with a Cambridge residency of 6–12 months (can be split across visits). Includes £10,000 stipend, £10,000 production budget, up to £3,000 travel support, rent-free accommodation and meals at Girton College, and a studio/creative workspace plus flexible working spaces at the Cavendish Laboratory. Open internationally to artists of any medium or nationality — no prior science experience required. Must be 18+ and out of full-time education by October 2026. Joint applications accepted.
calls.summary: Year-long art-science fellowship at Girton College, Cambridge. £23,000 total funding + accommodation. All media.

calls.title: Chester Photo Festival 2026 — Making Voices Heard
calls.description: Second edition of the annual Chester Photo Festival, running 16–29 October 2026 across University of Chester, Picturehouse, churches, and a museum. Theme: Making Voices Heard — exploring photography through myths, feelings, memories, and personal narratives. Free entry of up to 5 works; selection fees only apply if chosen (£45/work early deadline 15 May, £60/work late deadline 15 June, covering printing and standard framing). Open to photographers of all experience levels internationally. Accepts photography, moving image (online link + still), and artist books (PDF). Selected works included in the exhibition book and displayed across Chester venues. Late entries close when 300 works are selected. Organised by academics and researchers including Dr Alexandru Modoi and Professor Erik Knudsen.
calls.summary: 2nd edition photo festival across Chester venues. Free entry; selection fee only. Exhibition + festival book.
prose: Chester Photo Festival is a UK photography festival held in Chester, England, with the second edition running October 16–29, 2026 across six city center venues: University of Chester, Chester Picturehouse, St Werburgh's Church, St John's Church, the Grosvenor Museum, and one additional space. The festival was founded in 2023 with its inaugural edition in May 2025.

The 2026 theme is "Making Voices Heard," exploring photography through myths, feelings, memories, and personal narratives. Submissions are accepted across photography (up to 5 JPEGs per artist), moving images and short films (online link plus still), and artist books or zines (as PDF).

The fee structure is unusual: submission is free for up to 5 works, with fees charged only if the work is selected. Selected work pays £45 at the early deadline (May 15) or £60 (£45 for students) at the late deadline (July 15), at which point selection closes once 300 works have been accepted.

Selected work is exhibited across the Chester venues with standard framing provided in three sizes (50×40, 40×30, 30×30 cm), published in the festival book, and the artist receives a participation certificate plus invitations to networking events and artist talks. AI-generated work is accepted.

The festival is open to photographers at all experience levels with international submissions welcome. Selection is overseen by academics and researchers including Dr Alexandru Modoi and Professor Erik Knudsen.

calls.title: Abbott Watts Photography Residency — Fall 2026
calls.description: Dedicated photography residency at Monson Arts in Maine, with access to the photography studio and darkroom of Todd Watts in nearby Blanchard — adjacent to the former home of Berenice Abbott. Darkroom accommodates silver gelatin printing up to 40"×50" from 35mm to 8×10 negatives, plus alternative analog processes. Digital studio with PC workstations, 34" monitors, Adobe Creative Cloud, and a 44" Epson printer. Residents receive a private bedroom in shared housing in Monson, all meals, and a stipend ($250 for 2-week, $500 for 4-week). Fall 2026 sessions: September 14–24 (2-week) and October 28 – November 19 (4-week). Residents must supply their own materials and have a car (8-minute drive to studio). Open to photographers at any career stage worldwide.
calls.summary: Photography residency in Maine with full darkroom (up to 40×50 silver gelatin) and digital studio. Housing, meals, and stipend included.

calls.title: Peyton Evans Artist Residency (PEAR) 2026–2027
calls.description: One-month residency program on Key West, Florida. Photographers apply under Media Arts. Residencies run the 2nd day of the month to the last day, between October 2026 and August 2027. Residents receive accommodation at the PEAR House (live/work space), a bike to get around the island, and access to shared kitchen facilities. No residency fee once accepted; artists cover their own travel, living expenses, and materials. Founded in 2006, The Studios has hosted hundreds of writers and artists; selection committees are comprised of working artists and professionals across Visual Arts, Literary Arts, Media Arts, Musical Arts, and Performing Arts. Apply via SlideRoom.
calls.summary: One-month live/work residency on Key West. PEAR House accommodation, bike, and shared kitchen. No residency fee once accepted.

calls.title: Eco-Process Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: One-month summer residency at Blue Cabin Floating Artist Residency in Metro Vancouver (August 2026) for emerging lens-based artists. Program focuses on eco-processing and alternative photographic techniques such as phytogram, lumen printing, cyanotype, and other sustainable photographic processes. Up to 3 mentorship sessions with interdisciplinary artist Morgan Sears-Williams. Blue Cabin is situated on the traditional territories of the Musqueam, Squamish, and Tsleil-Waututh Nations. Priority given to LGBTQ+ 2S emerging artists with some photo/lens-based experience. Open to emerging artists in Metro Vancouver and Indigenous territories/reserves connected to the region. Produced by grunt gallery in collaboration with Blue Cabin Cooperative.
calls.summary: One-month Blue Cabin residency for emerging lens-based artists. Alt process mentorship (cyanotype, lumen, phytogram). LGBTQ+ 2S priority.

calls.title: 2026 National Juried Photography Exhibition
calls.description: Juried photography exhibition at the Academy Center of the Arts in Lynchburg, Virginia. Open to U.S. residents aged 18+. Photographs must be original work completed after January 1, 2021, not previously exhibited in a Lynchburg juried photography show. Juror Kiera Hight, photographer and filmmaker from Asheville, NC, selects work after installation. Exhibition runs September 4–25, 2026 with an opening reception on September 4. Digital submissions accepted via email or flash drive; JPEG, 300 DPI, minimum 4×6".
calls.summary: National juried exhibition at Academy Center of the Arts, Lynchburg VA. $1,000 Best in Show. Juror: Kiera Hight.
prose: The Academy Center of the Arts in Lynchburg, Virginia (600 Main Street) runs an annual National Juried Photography Exhibition open to photographers across the United States. The 2026 cycle is juried by Kiera Hight, a photographer and filmmaker based in Asheville, North Carolina, who specializes in editorial, documentary, and creative work.

Cash prizes include the Best in Show award of $1,000, with additional cash awards given at the juror's discretion based on the installed exhibition. Selection is unusual: rather than judging from digital files alone, the juror selects work after installation — the physical hang influences the awards.

Selected work is exhibited September 4 through 25, 2026, with an opening reception on September 4. The Academy Center provides insurance coverage during the exhibition period and includes selected work in a full-color exhibition catalog. Sales are processed through the gallery, which retains a 35% commission.

Eligibility is restricted to U.S. residents aged 18 or over. Submitted photographs must be original work completed after January 1, 2021 and cannot have been previously exhibited in a Lynchburg juried photography show. The entry fee is $45 per artist for up to three submissions. Submissions are JPEG at 300 DPI, minimum 4×6 inches, accepted via email or flash drive. The 2026 deadline is June 30; results announced July 14.

calls.title: Recology San Francisco Artist-in-Residence Program 2027
calls.description: Four-month Artist-in-Residence program at the Recology San Francisco Recycling and Transfer Center, where artists source materials from the Public Reuse and Recycling Area to make work from discarded items. Three sessions run February–May, June–September, and October–January, with six artists awarded residencies annually beginning February 2027. Residents receive a monthly stipend, 24/7 access to a dedicated on-site studio, and support from Recology's Sustainability Education Program. Artists interact with visiting school and adult groups throughout their residency and exhibit at the end. Open to emerging, mid-career, and established artists in all disciplines including photography, new media, video, painting, performance, sculpture, and installation. Applicants must currently live within a one-hour drive of the San Francisco Transfer Station (401 Tunnel Ave) — no housing provided. A mandatory on-site tour is required before applying.
calls.summary: Four-month residency at SF's recycling center — artists make work from discarded materials. Monthly stipend, studio access. Bay Area only.
prose: The Recology Artist-in-Residence Program is a four-month residency at the San Francisco Recycling and Transfer Center — a 47-acre site on Tunnel Avenue where the city's discarded materials are sorted and processed. Founded in 1990 by Jo Hanson and described as the first program of its kind in the United States, the AIR program lets artists source materials directly from the Public Reuse and Recycling Area on site, producing work that engages with discarded objects and waste streams.

Six artists are awarded residencies each year, split across three sessions: February–May, June–September, and October–January. Each resident receives a monthly stipend, 24/7 access to a dedicated on-site studio, and support from Recology's Sustainability Education Program. Artists give regular talks to school groups and adult visitors during facility tours, integrating studio practice with public education. Each residency concludes with a public exhibition and artist talk; selected works enter Recology AIR's permanent collection.

Eligibility is restricted to artists who currently live within a one-hour drive of the San Francisco Transfer Station (401 Tunnel Ave); housing is not provided. The program is open to emerging, mid-career, and established artists across all disciplines — photography, new media, video, painting, performance, sculpture, installation. A mandatory on-site tour is required before applying.

Over its 35-year history the program has hosted more than 190 professional artists and 60 college and university student artists. The advisory board for selection includes Michael Arcega, Charmin Roundtree-Baaqee, JD Beltran, Terry Berlier, Kevin B. Chen, Elena Gross, Jamil Hellu, and Jonathan Carver Moore. The 2027 cycle deadline is September 1, 2026.

calls.title: Tasweer 2026 Project Award
calls.description: Annual grant from Tasweer, Qatar's leading photo festival organised by Qatar Museums. Open to photographers aged 18+ currently residing in the Western Asia and North Africa (WANA) region — Algeria, Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Turkey, UAE, and Yemen. The award provides 30,000 QAR (~$8,200) per awardee to support the initiation, development, or completion of a photographic project. Winners receive opportunities to exhibit at Tasweer Photo Festival Qatar and participate in public and digital programming. Applicants may apply simultaneously to the Single Image Award. Submit one PDF file containing 20 images with titles and captions.
calls.summary: Qatar Museums grant for photographers in WANA region. 30,000 QAR to develop a photographic project. Exhibition at Tasweer Photo Festival.

calls.title: Tasweer 2026 Single Image Award
calls.description: Annual single-image competition from Tasweer, Qatar's photo festival organised by Qatar Museums. Open to photographers aged 18+ currently residing in the Western Asia and North Africa (WANA) region. Each photographer submits one image representing their personal narrative and experience. Winners receive 2,000 QAR per awardee, with selected images showcased in an online exhibition and featured as part of Tasweer Photo Festival Qatar's public and digital programme. Submit one JPEG or TIFF, 3000 pixels max on longest side, 3–8 MB.
calls.summary: Single image award from Qatar Museums for WANA region photographers. 2,000 QAR prize plus online exhibition at Tasweer Photo Festival.

calls.title: Al & Mickey Quinlan Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: Eight-week residency at the Dome House — a twin-lobed concrete structure built into sand dunes on Lake Michigan adjacent to Whitefish Dunes State Park on Wisconsin's Door Peninsula. Open to one artist residing in the Midwest US (Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota) working in drawing, painting, printmaking, photography or related fine-art mediums. 2026 residency runs August 2 – September 27. Semi-private loft living quarters and adjacent studio/workspace provided, fully furnished. Resident must provide a minimum of 5 hours/week of educational outreach (workshops, artist talks, demonstrations). Partnership between the Quinlan family and the Miller Art Museum.
calls.summary: 8-week residency at Door Peninsula's Dome House for Midwest US artists. $500 stipend, housing, studio. Photography welcome.

calls.title: Illuminations Grant 2026
calls.description: Annual grant supporting Black trans women and trans femmes working in visual art. One winner receives $10,000; four finalists each receive $1,250. Winners also receive professional development resources and studio visits with rotating panel judges. Developed in partnership with photographer Mariette Pathy Allen, activist Aaryn Lang, and artist Serena Jara. Accepted media include photography, drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, ceramics, and fiber arts. Open to self-identified Black trans women and trans femmes in early-career visual-art practice, based in the United States. Apply via SlideRoom with up to 12 work samples, two short statements on artistic practice, CV, and two professional references.
calls.summary: Annual $10,000 grant for Black trans women visual artists including photographers. Four finalists get $1,250 each. US-based, early-career.
jury: Jordyn Jay, Founder & Executive Director, Black Trans Femmes in the Arts Collective
Isis Awad, Curator & Editor, Participant Inc
prose: The Illuminations Grant is administered by Queer|Art and funded entirely by visual artist Mariette Pathy Allen. Now in its seventh year (launched circa 2019), the grant supports self-identified Black trans women and trans femmes working in early-career visual art practice and based in the United States.

The grant structure is one main award of $10,000 plus four finalist awards of $1,250 each, for a total of five recipients. Beyond the cash, all recipients receive professional development resources and studio visits with the rotating panel of judges — meaning the grant operates as both financial support and a curatorial introduction.

Eligible media span photography, drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, ceramics, and fiber arts. The grant was developed in collaboration with Mariette Pathy Allen, activist Aaryn Lang, and artist Serena Jara.

There is no application fee. Applications go through SlideRoom with up to 12 work samples, two short statements on artistic practice, a CV, and two professional references. The 2026 deadline is July 2, with results announced in October. The 2026 jury comprises Jordyn Jay (Founder & Executive Director of Black Trans Femmes in the Arts Collective), Isis Awad (Curator & Editor at Participant Inc), and visual artist Utē Petit.

calls.title: Ucross Foundation Spring 2027 Residency
calls.description: 2–6 week residency on a 20,000-acre ranch in northern Wyoming. Private studio, living quarters, chef-prepared meals Monday–Friday, and weekly housekeeping. No stipend — residents provide their own materials and travel. Application portal opens May 1 and closes July 15, 2026 for the Spring 2027 session (February – early June 2027). Approximately 115 artists hosted annually, with up to 10 in residence at any time. Open to visual artists (including photographers), writers, composers, choreographers, interdisciplinary and performance artists, and collaborative teams. Both emerging and established artists of professional standing are welcome. Notification approximately 16 weeks after the deadline.
calls.summary: 2–6 week residency on a 20,000-acre Wyoming ranch. Studio and meals; no stipend. Photography eligible. Portal opens May 1.
prose: The Ucross Foundation runs an artist residency on a 20,000-acre working ranch in northeastern Wyoming. The program was founded in 1981 with the first residency in 1983, and now hosts approximately 115 residents annually across two sessions: Fall (August through early December) and Spring (February through early June). Residencies run between two and six weeks; up to ten artists are in residence at any time, typically split as four writers, four visual artists, and two composers.

There is no residency fee. Residents receive private living accommodations, dedicated work space, all weekday meals prepared by the in-house chef (with self-catering provisions for weekends and breakfasts), weekly housekeeping, linens, and wireless internet. There is no stipend — artists provide their own materials and arrange their own travel to Sheridan, Wyoming, the nearest airport.

Eligibility is open globally to visual artists, writers, composers, choreographers, interdisciplinary and performance artists, and collaborative teams, at both established and emerging career stages. Applicants must demonstrate professional standing, with both U.S. and international applicants welcome.

The application fee is $40, with no waivers available. Spring 2027 applications are accepted through Submittable from May 1 through July 15, 2026; Fall applications open later in the year (November 1 through January 15). Decisions are typically released within several months of each deadline.

calls.title: Create! Magazine Issue #58 — In Full Color
calls.description: Open call for Issue No. 58, 'In Full Color.' Artists respond to the concept of color in any artistic interpretation — hue, cultural expression, emotion, or otherwise. Photography welcomed alongside painting, sculpture, installation, and other media. Selected artists receive a four-page professional spread in the print and digital editions of the fall 2026 issue, plus social media features and a complimentary digital issue. Juried by Liz Lidgett (art advisor and gallery owner, Des Moines, Iowa). Submit up to 10 works (cohesive bodies or series encouraged). Open to all artists worldwide, no formal education or gallery representation required. No AI-generated work.
calls.summary: Fall 2026 'In Full Color' issue. 4-page print + digital spread. Juried by Liz Lidgett. Open worldwide, no AI.
jury: Liz Lidgett, art advisor and gallery owner, Des Moines, Iowa

calls.title: UNSTAGED Journal — Impermanence
calls.description: New themed issue of UNSTAGED, an independent photography journal dedicated to lens-based inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity. This call, guest curated by Benjamin Osborne, explores the theme Impermanence — the fleeting, the ephemeral, shadows and transient forms that open doors to imagination. Issue 03 featuring 11 artists including Alena Solomonova, Nova Doria, and Mari Saxon was just released. Submit 5–10 photographs as JPG files (long edge 2000px) with a project description. Upload work to Google Drive and send the link to reach@arek-ratai.com. Name files Name_Series_Title_01. Free entry, free print publication for selected photographers.
calls.summary: Free indie photography journal on authenticity. Theme: Impermanence. Guest curated by Benjamin Osborne. Print publication.

calls.title: UNSTAGED Journal — Instant Photography
calls.description: Themed issue of UNSTAGED, an independent photography journal dedicated to lens-based inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity. Guest curated by Dani (@d.m.terblanche), this call invites personal stories told through instant photography (Polaroid, Instax, etc.) — focused on everyday moments rather than perfection. Tagline: 'You don't have to be good.' Submissions can include single images, diptychs, triptychs, or mixed-media approaches; lens-based instant photography only. Submit 5–10 photographs as JPG files (long edge 2000px, 300 DPI) with a project description (max 500 words). Upload work to a public Google Drive and send the link (with description as PDF) to reach@arek-ratai.com. Name files Name_ProjectTitle_01. Emails with attachments will be deleted. Free entry, free print publication for selected photographers.
calls.summary: Free indie photography journal on authenticity. Theme: Instant photography (Polaroid, Instax). Guest curated by Dani. Print publication.

calls.title: Slow Exposures 2026 — Main Exhibition
calls.description: Annual juried exhibition celebrating photography of the contemporary American South. Work must be taken in one of 16 Southern states: Alabama, Arkansas, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, and West Virginia. Selected photographs shown first at the historic R.F. Strickland Building in downtown Concord, GA, then move to the Cochran Gallery in LaGrange, GA. 30% commission on sales. Festival weekend September 18–20, 2026 in Zebulon, Georgia. Submit up to 6 images via Formsite. 23rd edition.
calls.summary: Annual exhibition celebrating photography of the rural American South. 23rd edition. Two-venue show in Pike County, Georgia.

calls.title: ABANDONED Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Exploring traces of human presence and absence — forgotten structures, deserted landscapes, personal relics, and emotional remnants. 26 selected images exhibited at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe, NM, July 3–31, 2026. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Luster paper and 24×24 black museum-quality framing. 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers.
jury: Holly Hart, Fine Art Photographer & Founder, Dusk Gallery
calls.summary: Traces of human presence and absence — forgotten structures and personal relics. Free pro printing & framing. Santa Fe, NM.

calls.title: The Life of Color
calls.description: International juried photography exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis exploring how color operates as signal — amplifying, unifying, or destabilizing what is seen. Photographers encouraged to use hue, saturation, and value deliberately to construct meaning. Up to 38 photographs selected. Awards include Directors' Choice (free entry to two future calls) and five honorable mentions. Members and artists experiencing financial hardship receive discounted or free entries. Exhibition June 20 – July 11, 2026.
calls.summary: Color as signal — amplifying, unifying, destabilizing. Up to 38 works selected. Praxis Gallery Minneapolis.

calls.title: imagined
calls.description: Online juried exhibition exploring the imaginative — visionary, poetic, fanciful, dreamlike, fictional. Juror Susan Burnstine, an award-winning fine art photographer known for creating homemade cameras and lenses. Up to 47 images selected. Awards: Juror's Award (solo online exhibition, hardbound book, blog feature), Director's Award (hardbound book and blog feature), Visitor's Award ($100 for most Instagram likes). Exhibition June 19 – July 30, 2026. Photographers submitting 13+ images receive a complimentary 30-minute portfolio review.
calls.summary: Visionary, poetic, fanciful, dreamlike, fictional. Juror Susan Burnstine. 47 images selected for online exhibition.

calls.title: Remnants — Spring 2026 Online Exhibition
calls.description: Online group exhibition exploring photography's relationship to loss and absence — family members, homes, ways of life, places, objects, and memories. Curated by Michael Behlen, founder of Analog Forever Magazine. Open to photographers working with film and analog processes. Optional but encouraged: a paragraph on what the subject means to you and why. Exhibition launches online May 29, 2026.
jury: Michael Behlen, Founder, Analog Forever Magazine
calls.summary: Online exhibition on loss and absence — film/analog photographers. Curated by Michael Behlen. Exhibition launches May 29.

calls.title: The House & Garden Show
calls.description: Online exhibition exploring shelter and nature through intimate interiors, domestic moments, wild backyards, and cultivated landscapes. Literal, abstract, or imaginary interpretations welcome. Part of Blue Sky Gallery's 50th anniversary celebration featuring 12 monthly themed online exhibitions. No membership required. Juried by a special committee. Virtual exhibition launches June 4, 2026.
calls.summary: Online exhibition on shelter and nature — intimate interiors, wild backyards. Blue Sky Gallery 50th anniversary series.

calls.title: Pamplemousse Magazine Issue 13
calls.description: Issue 13 of Pamplemousse Magazine, an independent contemporary film photography print magazine based in San Francisco. This call invites artists to respond to provided curated vernacular photographs — exploring the intersection of snapshot and fine art photography. Only original film photography (35mm, 120, large format, polaroid, or alt-process) created in response to one of the provided found photos is accepted. A project statement of 100–300 words is required. Files named FIRSTNAME_LASTNAME_01.
calls.summary: Film photography print magazine. Issue 13 invites work responding to curated vernacular photos. Analog only, no AI.

calls.title: see-zeen Issue 20 Open Call
calls.description: Independent online magazine curating contemporary photography by international emerging artists, based in NYC and Berlin. Open theme — any style, genre, or approach (portraiture, landscape, documentary, fashion, abstraction, experimental, conceptual, hybrid). Selected work published on website and social media; unpublished submissions still considered for Instagram. Submit a project statement (max 300 words), work description (max 100 words), bio with contact, and website/Instagram links.
calls.summary: Independent online magazine curating contemporary emerging photography. Open theme. Free, worldwide.

calls.title: Photo Trouvée Magazine Issue 20 — Print Call
calls.description: Print Issue 20 open call for artists who work with or are inspired by vintage found or family photographs. Any media accepted. Selected artists receive a designated page spread with artist statement, complimentary digital issue, 15% discount code for the print magazine, plus website, newsletter, and social media listings reaching 23.2K+ people. No theme. International submissions welcome.
calls.summary: Print Issue 20 for artists working with vintage found or family photographs. Any media. Free submission.
jury: Juliana Naufel, Co-Founder, Photo Trouvée Magazine
Twiggy Boyer, Co-Founder, Photo Trouvée Magazine
prose: Photo Trouvée Magazine is a print and digital publication based in São Paulo, Brazil, focused specifically on artists who work with or are inspired by vintage found or family photographs — what's known in French as photo trouvée, found photography. The magazine is co-founded and edited by Juliana Naufel and Twiggy Boyer.

Issue 20 has no fixed theme: any approach to working with found or family photographs is welcome, and submissions can be in any media. AI-generated work is not accepted, and the magazine prioritizes artist statements written without AI assistance.

Selected artists receive a designated page spread in the print issue with their artist statement and images, a complimentary digital issue, a 15% discount code for the print magazine, and listings on the magazine's website, newsletter, and social media — reaching approximately 23,200 people across channels. The magazine also distributes to galleries in São Paulo and Coral Springs, Florida.

Submissions require 4 to 6 high-resolution JPEGs at 300 DPI, named in the format ARTISTNAME_TITLE_. Initial submission is free; selected artists pay a $40 publishing fee due in the first week of July 2026. Submissions go through JotForm only — no email submissions accepted. The Issue 20 deadline is June 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST.

calls.title: Watershed
calls.description: Themed juried exhibition exploring water as subject, symbol, tool, and essential aspect of life. Juried by Luther Smith, photographic artist and Emeritus Professor of Art Photography at Texas Christian University, with work in the Amon Carter Museum, Library of Congress, Dallas Museum of Art, and other major institutions. Exhibition at Pool Gallery, Fort Worth, July 3–25, 2026, with closing reception July 25. $400 first place, $250 second, $150 third, plus up to 5 honorable mentions. Open internationally to all skill levels.
jury: Luther Smith, Emeritus Professor of Art Photography, Texas Christian University
calls.summary: Themed juried photo exhibition on water. Juried by Luther Smith (TCU). Exhibition at Pool Gallery, Fort Worth. $400 first prize.

calls.title: Vicinity 2026: What's Going On?
calls.description: 9th Annual Juried Exhibition. Inspired by Marvin Gaye's 1971 album exploring social conflict, the show invites artists to respond to 'What's going on?' through inner landscapes or broader human conditions — social, cultural, environmental. Juried by Jan Tichy, professor at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago in Photography and Art & Technology/Sound Practices, with work in MoMA and Israel Museum collections. Open only to photographers based in the Chicago area able to deliver work in person. Exhibition July 2–26, 2026 at Perspective Gallery, Evanston, IL.
jury: Jan Tichy, School of the Art Institute of Chicago
calls.summary: 9th annual juried photo exhibition on social conflict. Juried by Jan Tichy (SAIC). Chicago-area only.

calls.title: Young Greek Photographers 2026
calls.org: Athens Photo Festival / Hellenic Centre for Photography
calls.description: Annual exhibition organized since 1987 by the Hellenic Centre for Photography as part of Athens Photo Festival. Open to artists up to 35 years old residing permanently in Greece or Greek artists residing abroad. Selected works exhibited at the Benaki Museum / Pireos 138, Athens (June 10 – July 26, 2026), then traveling to Thessaloniki. Production costs covered, festival catalogue inclusion, portfolio reviews with international professionals, and nominations for international festivals. Two finalists join the Photoxenia artist residency program in Crete. Up to two projects per applicant, separate forms required.
calls.summary: Exhibition at Benaki Museum, Athens. For Greek artists/diaspora under 35. Free. Production covered + Crete residency for 2 finalists.
jury: Natasha Christia, Independent Curator, Writer, Educator
Stamatis Schizakis, Curator of Photography and New Media, National Museum of Contemporary Art Athens
Marilia Fotopoulou, Head of Programming, Athens Photo Festival

calls.title: CCI + WOPHA Fellowship 2026
calls.description: Joint fellowship from PAMM's Caribbean Cultural Institute (CCI) and Women Photographers International Archive (WOPHA), for emerging and mid-career women and non-binary photographers from the Caribbean and its diaspora. Hybrid program runs September–November 2026, with an in-person residency at El Espacio 23 in Miami during September. Fellow receives a stipend, production funds up to $4,000, and round-trip airfare to Miami if not currently based there. Photographic practice broadly defined to include cameraless, computational, and augmented processes, as well as image archiving and circulation. Includes mentorship, curatorial resources, and engagement with the academic community at FIU-LACC.
calls.summary: Fellowship for women & non-binary photographers from Caribbean and diaspora. Miami residency at El Espacio 23 + production funds.

calls.title: Passage Art-Residency-Programme 2026
calls.description: Four-week artist-in-residence programme in the Wittenberg region of Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, dedicated to photography and film. Two themed residencies for October 2026: Topic 1 at Ferropolis (the historic Zschornewitz coal-fired power station — energy production, post-industrial landscapes); Topic 2 at the Reformationsgeschichtliche Forschungsbibliothek Wittenberg (a Reformation-era research library — knowledge, visual representation). €5,000 grant per residency, plus €1,000 supplement for artists with children. On-site accommodation, research support, and curatorial guidance provided. Open to national and international artists aged 18+; students not eligible. Notification of results from 20 June 2026.
calls.summary: Four-week residency in Wittenberg region for photographers and filmmakers. €5,000 grant + accommodation. Two themed sites.

calls.title: Monochromatic Awards 2026
calls.description: Fifth edition of the Dodho Monochromatic Awards, celebrating monochromatic photography in all interpretations — traditional black and white, grayscale, sepia, cyanotype, or any single-tone variation. Jury looks for clear vision, defined intention, and strong execution. Winners and finalists are featured in the Monochromatic Awards 2026 annual printed book (30×30 cm, premium matte paper). The top winner receives 'Photographer of the Year' recognition. Three category prizes plus two honorable mentions receive certificates and editorial visibility. Open globally, individuals or collectives.
calls.prize: Photographer of the Year + annual book inclusion
calls.summary: 5th edition. All interpretations of monochromatic photography. Finalists in a 30×30 cm annual printed book.
prose: The Monochromatic Awards is Dodho Magazine's annual prize for monochromatic photography, now in its 5th edition. The interpretation of "monochromatic" is unusually broad: traditional black and white, grayscale, sepia, cyanotype, or any other variation based on a single tone is accepted. Color photographs reduced to single-tone palettes qualify alongside historical alternative-process work.

Selection is not divided by genre. Instead the jury evaluates work on "clear vision and a defined intention," with no separate tracks for portrait, landscape, documentary, or fine art. The jury comprises winners from previous editions: Carl Doghouse (2025, UK), Luca Onnis (2024, Italy), Zhenhuan Zhou (2023, Canada), and Ian Pettigrew (2022, Canada) — a structural choice that lineages the award through its own history.

Entry fees scale by image count: €30 for 3 images, €45 for 6, €60 for 12. The first prize winner is recognized as "Photographer of the Year." The top five (1st, 2nd, 3rd, plus two honorable mentions) receive prominent editorial coverage on Dodho's site. All 100 finalists are included in the annual printed volume, a 30×30 cm hardcover on premium matte paper.

Eligibility is open globally to individuals and collectives. Previously published work is accepted, and there is no restriction on when the images were created. The 2026 deadline is July 15, with results announced late July.

calls.title: 2026 Book Awards
calls.description: Three photobook awards: Author's Book Award (subjective artistic practice), Historical Book Award (documentation/archive), and Photo-Text Book Award (text-image relationship, supported by Fondation Jan Michalski). Each category €6,000. Books must have been published between May 13, 2025 and May 13, 2026. Self-published books without ISBN are eligible; reissues allowed if the first print run was under 150 copies. Shortlisted and winning works are exhibited at Rencontres d'Arles (July 6 – October 4, 2026) and at Jimei x Arles in Xiamen, China.
calls.summary: Three €6,000 awards for photobooks (Author's, Historical, Photo-Text). Winners exhibited at Rencontres d'Arles and Jimei x Arles.

calls.title: E·CO/26 — About Time
calls.description: Joint open call from VIST Foundation, AECID (Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation), and NEWF, supporting collective visual projects from Latin America and Africa. Theme: About Time — exploring the relationship between past, present, and future, with attention to ancestral knowledge, memory, territorial connections, and future imaginaries. Twelve collective projects will be selected (six from each region), each receiving a €5,000 production grant. Open to existing or newly-formed groups of three or more people; international projects spanning multiple countries are welcome. Visual, audiovisual, and transmedia formats accepted. Selected groups join a collective production process with virtual mentorship from specialists; final works are presented through travelling exhibitions and the digital platforms of VIST Foundation, NEWF, AECID, and Spanish Cultural Centers. Collective meeting in November 2026 in South Africa.
calls.summary: €5,000 production grant for 12 collectives from Latin America and Africa. Theme: time, memory, ancestral knowledge. Free.

calls.title: Ian Parry Photojournalism Grant 2026
calls.description: Photojournalism grant honoring Ian Parry, who died at 24 covering the Romanian Revolution in 1989 for The Sunday Times. Open to photographers aged 24 or under, or any age with proof of full-time enrollment in a photographic course. Winner receives £10,000, a year-long mentorship with photojournalist Giles Duley, Canon equipment loans for one year, publication in The Guardian, inclusion in the Hamburg Portfolio Review, and potential safety equipment/hostile environment training via the Gentex Corp award. Partners include Canon, The Guardian, and Legacy of War Foundation. Patron: Sir Don McCullin. Founded over four decades ago.
calls.summary: £10,000 + Giles Duley mentorship for photojournalists 24 or under (or full-time photo students). Patron: Sir Don McCullin.
prose: The Ian Parry Photojournalism Grant honors Ian Parry, a British photojournalist who died at age 24 in 1989 while on assignment for The Sunday Times during the Romanian revolution. The grant was established in his memory and has run for over three decades, with Sir Don McCullin as patron. Past recipients include Simon Roberts (1998), Nanna Heitmann, Maisie Crow, and Marcelo Pérez del Carpio — several of whom went on to establish significant photojournalism careers.
Eligibility is restricted to photographers aged 24 or under, or to photographers of any age currently enrolled full-time in a photographic course. There is no application fee.

The winner receives £10,000 in cash plus a year-long mentorship with photojournalist Giles Duley, Canon equipment loans for one year, publication in The Guardian, inclusion in the Hamburg Portfolio Review, and potential safety equipment and hostile-environment training via the Gentex Corp award. The combination is built to support a recipient through the year following the grant rather than just commemorate the win.

Selection draws on a 40+ member advisory committee of photography professionals, editors, and curators. Current institutional partners include Canon, The Guardian, and the Legacy of War Foundation. The 2026 cycle is administered through Picter (site.picter.com/ian-parry-photojournalism-grant-2026); the deadline is August 31, 2026, and results are announced October 30, 2026.

calls.title: Seen / Unseen
calls.description: Photography exhibition exploring the visible and the implied — works that engage with what is shown, suggested, or hidden. Online curated exhibition with published catalog, social media and newsletter promotion, certificate of participation, and digital badge. First place receives a solo webpage exhibition. Open to photographers worldwide aged 18+. $1,000 total cash awards.
calls.summary: Online photography exhibition on the visible and the implied. Juror Ann M. Jastrab. $1,000 total awards.
prose: Decagon Gallery is an online curatorial platform that runs themed photography exhibitions with published catalogs and social distribution. "Seen / Unseen" is the gallery's open call for work that engages with the relationship between what is shown and what is implied — exploring presence, absence, suggestion, concealment, and the visual languages that point at things without quite revealing them.

The selection structure is online-first. Selected photographers are featured in a curated online exhibition with a published catalog distributed through Decagon's mailing list and social channels. All accepted artists receive a certificate of participation and a digital badge for portfolio use. The first-place winner additionally receives a solo webpage exhibition on the gallery site.
Cash awards total $1,000 across the top placements. The 2026 cycle is juried by Ann M. Jastrab. Eligibility is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over.
Entry fee is $25 per submission of up to 8 images. The 2026 deadline is July 8, with results announced July 21.

calls.title: Manifest Season 23 Photo-Solo Exhibit Proposals
calls.description: Open call for solo exhibition proposals at Manifest Creative Research Gallery during the 2026/27 season, coinciding with the FotoFocus Biennial in Cincinnati. Approximately one-third of seasonal programming is dedicated to solo exhibitions of original lens-based work. Each exhibiting artist receives a $100 honorarium plus a $1,000 Grand Jury Award for one jury-selected work. Open internationally to artists working in traditional or non-traditional photographic media.
calls.summary: Solo lens-based exhibition proposals at Manifest Gallery during the 2026/27 FotoFocus Biennial. $1,000 Grand Jury Award.

calls.title: Solstice Magazine Issue 72 — Editorial Submissions
calls.description: Submit fashion and editorial photography for publication in Issue 72 of Solstice Magazine, a London-based fashion publication. First-round deadline May 18; second-round June 18 if space remains. Issue release June 21, 2026. Editorials must be unpublished. Send via PDF, Dropbox, or WeTransfer.
calls.summary: Fashion and editorial photography for Issue 72 of this London fashion magazine. Issue releases June 21, 2026.

calls.title: Photoworks Guest Issue 4 — Rituals
calls.description: Fourth edition of Photoworks Guest, a community photo zine published by Photoworks SF in San Francisco. Theme: Rituals — exploring the relationship between rituals and photography. Examples include daily commutes, ceremonies, holiday traditions, cooking, or anything you do every day. Selected work appears in the print magazine; longer features with interviews are also available for projects that fit the theme.
calls.summary: Community photo zine from Photoworks SF. Theme: Rituals. Free print publication, 1–3 images per submission.

calls.title: Łódź Photo-Match 2026 Portfolio Review
calls.description: Two-day portfolio review at Fotofestiwal in Łódź, June 19–20, 2026. Twenty selected photographers each get up to four one-on-one meetings with European curators, editors, and gallery directors based on a matching process. Day 1 features public presentations; Day 2 holds private reviews at Alfred Biedermann's Palace. Open internationally, including artistic duos. Physical attendance required. Reviewers from Spain, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, UK, Finland, Netherlands, Sweden, Austria, and Chile.
calls.summary: Free two-day portfolio review at Fotofestiwal Łódź. Twenty photographers meet 20 European curators.

calls.title: No-Type Monograph No. 01
calls.description: Open call from No-Type, an independent Chicago photography publisher, for the inaugural artist monograph. The selected photographer receives a fully-funded monograph dedicated entirely to their work — editing, design, printing, and marketing all covered, plus 20% of the printed edition. A shortlist of six artists will be interviewed on No-Type's website, and all applicants are considered for inclusion in an Editor's Choice issue of the magazine. Open to lens-based projects of any subject, genre, or process; submissions must be a cohesive body of work ready for book form.
calls.summary: Fully-funded monograph publication from independent Chicago photo publisher No-Type. Shortlist gets website interviews.

calls.title: Photo Shoot 2026
calls.description: Open call from Black Box Gallery in Portland, OR. 26 photographs selected for in-gallery exhibition (July 1–25, 2026); 50 additional photographs included in an online gallery annex. All 76 selected works featured in a printed Blurb catalog. Free printing, matting, and framing for selected works. 50% commission to gallery on sales. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide. Juried by Todd Johnson (founder/director of Black Box Gallery, MFA San Francisco Art Institute).
jury: Todd Johnson, Founder & Director, Black Box Gallery
calls.summary: Black Box Gallery Portland open theme show. 26 prints exhibited + 50 online + Blurb catalog. Free framing.
prose: Photo Shoot is Black Box Gallery's open-theme themed exhibition — the gallery's catch-all call where any photographic style or genre is welcome. Black Box is a Portland, Oregon photography gallery directed by Todd Johnson, who holds an MFA in Photography from the San Francisco Art Institute and serves as juror for the gallery's calls.

The selection structure is two-part: 26 photographs are chosen for the physical gallery exhibition, with 50 additional photographs included in an online gallery annex. All 76 selected works are reproduced in a printed Blurb catalog.

What's unusual: the gallery covers all printing, matting, and framing for selected work. Archival printing is on Epson Premium Luster Photo paper. After the exhibition closes, prints are retained in the gallery's flat files for further promotion.

Entry fee is $40 per submission of up to 5 photos. Submissions are JPEG, max 1200 pixels, 72 PPI, under 5MB. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Sales terms: 50% gallery commission, photographer retains all rights. The exhibition runs July 1–25, 2026; submission deadline is June 12, 2026.

calls.title: SCAN Tarragona — Full Contact Award 2026
calls.description: Open call from SCAN, the international photography festival organized by Tarragona City Council. 12 projects selected for Full Contact, a professional meeting space at Teatret del Port in El Serrallo, Tarragona on October 17, 2026. From these 12, one artist receives the Full Contact Award: a solo exhibition in 2027 as part of SCAN's official program plus €900 fee for exhibition and communication rights. Open to EU and UK residents of legal age. Submit any photo series that tells a story, on any subject. Maximum 16 photographs from a single series.
calls.summary: Free open call from SCAN Tarragona. 12 projects to Full Contact meeting; winner gets 2027 solo show + €900.

calls.title: Photography+ Emerging Talent 2026
calls.description: International open call from Photography+, Photoworks' digital platform exploring how photography intersects with everyday life. Open to BA and MA graduates and image-based artists within their first five years of practice or graduation. 10 awardees featured in Photography+ online magazine and showcased in an evening projection at Kranj Foto Fest. One artist receives a year-long Photoworks membership plus curatorial and editorial mentoring; another receives a £200 Spectrum Photographic printing voucher and an Instagram takeover. Submit up to 15 images from a single project with a statement of up to 200 words.
jury: Emma Bowkett, Director of Photography, Financial Times
Fernanda Prado Verčič, Founding Director, Kranj Foto Fest
Maryam Wahid, Head of Programs, Tasweer Photography Festival
calls.summary: Free international call for early-career photographers. 10 awardees featured in Photography+ magazine and Kranj Foto Fest projection.
prose: Photoworks is a Brighton-based UK registered charity and Arts Council England National Portfolio organization, one of the longstanding institutions in British photography. "Photography+ Emerging Talent" is the open call for Photography+, Photoworks' digital platform exploring how photography intersects with everyday life.

The call is open internationally to BA and MA graduates and to image-based artists within the first five years of their practice and/or their graduation. Submission is free. Each applicant submits up to 15 images from a single project with a statement of no more than 200 words; only one project per applicant.

Ten awardees are selected. All ten are featured in the Photography+ online magazine and showcased in an evening projection at the Kranj Foto Fest in Slovenia. One awardee additionally receives a one-year Photoworks membership plus curatorial and editorial mentoring; another receives a £200 Spectrum Photographic printing voucher plus an Instagram takeover on the Photoworks account.

The 2026 jury comprises Emma Bowkett (Director of Photography, Financial Times), Louise Fedotov-Clements (Director, Photoworks), Fernanda Prado Verčič (Founding Director, Kranj Foto Fest), Maryam Wahid (Head of Programs, Tasweer Photography Festival), and Amin Yousefi (Assistant Curator/Editor, Photography+). Submissions go through Picter; the deadline is June 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM.

calls.title: Transforming Landscapes — 20/20 Photo Festival 2026
calls.description: International juried exhibition for analog photographers exploring how American landscapes have evolved over 250 years — physical, technological, societal, political, scientific, and artistic. Open exclusively to work made with analog photographic methods including film types (color negative, black-and-white, slide, instant) and formats (35mm, 120, 4×5 large format, 110, 126). Selected works exhibited at Cherry Street Pier during the 20/20 Photo Festival in Philadelphia, September 10–13, 2026. Juried by photographer Andrew Piccone.
calls.summary: Analog-only juried festival exhibition exploring 250 years of American landscapes. Cherry Street Pier, Philadelphia. Juror: Andrew Piccone.

calls.title: Lens Work: Trees and Water
calls.description: Juried group exhibition exploring trees and water as subjects in contemporary photography — dynamic and diverse imagery, including 'magical and poetic pictures' celebrating visual composition and contemporary photographic technique. Selected work shown in physical gallery and online annex; included in printed catalog. Free printing, matting, and framing for accepted artists. 50/50 sales commission. Exhibition August 1–25, 2026 in Portland, OR. Juror: Todd Johnson, Black Box Gallery founder. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers.
calls.summary: Black Box Gallery juried exhibition exploring trees and water. Free printing/framing. Portland, OR. Juror: Todd Johnson.
jury: Todd Johnson, Founder, Black Box Gallery
prose: Black Box Gallery is a Portland, Oregon photography gallery directed by Todd Johnson, who holds an MFA in Photography from the San Francisco Art Institute and serves as juror for the gallery's calls. "Lens Work: Trees and Water" is the gallery's themed call for 2026, focused on contemporary photography of trees and water — both as separate subjects and in combination.

The selection structure is two-part: 26 photographs are chosen for the physical gallery exhibition, with 50 additional photographs included in an online gallery annex. All 76 selected works are reproduced in a purchasable catalog.

What's unusual: the gallery covers all printing, matting, and framing for selected work. Prints are displayed in 18×24 inch black frames with white mats. After the exhibition closes, prints are retained in the gallery's flat files for two years for future promotion and sales.

Entry fee is $40 per submission of up to 5 photos. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Sales terms: 50% gallery commission, photographer retains copyright and approves all sales. The exhibition runs August 1–25, 2026; submission deadline is July 10, 2026.

calls.title: The Midnight Garden
calls.description: Four-day NYC pop-up exhibition curated by Jessica Libor (founder/director of Era Contemporary). Theme centers on cultivation, transformation, and unseen processes of growth — both in nature and within ourselves — exploring blooming, decay, renewal, and the balance between control and wildness. Open to U.S.-based visual artists in all 2D and 3D media including photography. Exhibition August 20–23, 2026 at 61 Atlantic Ave, Brooklyn. Selected artists featured in New Visionary Magazine and listed on Artsy through Warnes Contemporary gallery.
calls.summary: NYC pop-up curated by Jessica Libor on cultivation, transformation, and growth. Magazine feature + Artsy listing via Warnes Contemporary.
jury: Jessica Libor, Founder & Director, Era Contemporary

calls.title: 2nd Street Photo Festival 2026
calls.description: International street photography open call for the 2nd edition, hosted at the Athens School of Fine Arts. Submit 1–3 high-resolution photographs (minimum 4000 px on the long side, JPG or TIFF) via WeTransfer or cloud service to contest@streetphotofestival.gr, accompanied by a Word document with contact info, country, Instagram and website. Selected photographers contribute €50 toward festival expenses. Selected works exhibited at Athens School of Fine Arts December 12–20, 2026. All selected photographers receive a Certificate of Participation and Achievement.
calls.summary: Street photography call for Athens festival exhibition Dec 12–20. Free entry; €400/€300/€200 prizes; €50 if selected.

calls.title: XXIV Eurostars Grand Marina Photography Award — Josep Juanpere 2026
calls.description: 24th edition of this international photography prize organized by Hotusa Group in Barcelona. 2026 theme: Barcelona, World Capital of Architecture, marking the city's UNESCO designation. Submit up to three photographic triptychs that form a cohesive visual narrative on the city's architectural identity. Named in memory of architect Josep Juanpere (1953–2025), designer of Hotel Grand Marina. First prize: €5,000 + trophy. Second prize: €3,000 + trophy. Eight finalists receive trophies and free stays at Eurostars hotels.
calls.summary: 24th edition. Theme: Barcelona, World Capital of Architecture. €5,000 first prize. Submit photographic triptychs.
prose: The Eurostars Grand Marina Photography Award is now in its 24th edition, organized by Eurostars Hotel Company (part of Grupo Hotusa) at the Grand Marina hotel in Moll de Barcelona. The award is named in memory of Josep Juanpere (1953–2025), the architect behind the hotel's interior design and the historical president of the prize's jury — the award has long sat at the intersection of photography and architectural sensibility, and that crossover defines its thematic frame each year.

The 2026 theme is "Barcelona, World Capital of Architecture," chosen to mark UNESCO's designation of Barcelona for that year. Submissions take an unusual format: each participant submits up to three photographic triptychs, with each set forming a single unified work rather than three independent images. File size is capped at 6 MB per submission, and the deadline is October 20, 2026.

Prizes are substantial. First Prize: €5,000 plus a trophy. Second Prize: €3,000 (the Grupo Hotusa Prize) plus a trophy. Eight honorable mentions receive trophies and complimentary stays at Eurostars properties. There is no entry fee. Eligibility is open to professionals and amateurs aged 18 or over, with no nationality restriction.

calls.title: Life Framer — Street Life
calls.description: Monthly photography competition judged by Shana Lopes (Assistant Curator of Photography, SFMOMA). Theme: street photography, urbanscapes, observational moments, chance encounters. Winners exhibited at international galleries in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles.
jury: Shana Lopes, Assistant Curator of Photography, SFMOMA
calls.summary: Monthly competition judged by Shana Lopes (SFMOMA). Winners exhibited in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles.
prose: Life Framer runs as a monthly themed photography competition with a different juror each round. The "Street Life" call covers street photography, urbanscapes, observational moments, and chance encounters — broadly, photography that documents public life as it unfolds. The 2026 cycle of this theme is judged by Shana Lopes, Assistant Curator of Photography at the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art (SFMOMA).

The main prize is $2,000, with additional category awards and inclusion in Life Framer's online archive. Selected work is exhibited at Life Framer's partner galleries in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles — a touring physical presence that runs alongside the online platform.

Entry fees are tiered between $20 and $100 depending on the number of images submitted (up to 10 maximum per applicant). AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 or over.

The Street Life theme deadline is June 30, 2026, with results announced in mid-July. Other Life Framer themes follow on a rolling monthly schedule, each with a different jury and slightly different focus.

calls.title: Life Framer — Planet Earth
calls.description: Monthly photography competition judged by Myrtille Delamarche (Editor-in-Chief, GEO Magazine). Theme: nature, landscapes, the planet's beauty and humanity's influence on it — landscapes, conceptual, aerial, documentary. Winners exhibited at international galleries in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles.
calls.summary: Monthly competition judged by Myrtille Delamarche (GEO Magazine). Winners exhibited in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles.
prose: Life Framer runs as a monthly themed photography competition with a different juror each round. The "Planet Earth" call covers nature, landscape, environmental documentary, and aerial work — broadly, photography that engages with the planet itself rather than its inhabitants. The 2026 cycle of this theme is judged by Myrtille Delamarche, Editor-in-Chief of GEO Magazine.

The main prize is $2,000, with additional category awards and inclusion in Life Framer's online archive. Selected work is exhibited at Life Framer's partner galleries in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles — a touring physical presence that runs alongside the online platform.

Entry fees are tiered between $20 and $100 depending on the number of images submitted (up to 10 maximum per applicant). AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 or over. The Planet Earth theme deadline is July 31, 2026, with results announced in mid-August. Other Life Framer themes follow on a rolling monthly schedule, each with a different jury and slightly different focus.

calls.title: Wassaic Project 2027 Artist Residency
calls.description: 2–4 week residency at the Wassaic Project in the foothills of the Berkshires, two hours north of NYC. Summer sessions (3–4 weeks, June–September) take place in the Luther Barn studio building; winter sessions (2–4 weeks, January–March) in Maxon Mills. Open to individual artists, collaborative teams, and groups in any medium — photography eligible alongside painting, sculpture, installation, sound, video, and writing. Includes private bedroom in shared house, dedicated studio space (200–300 sq ft summer; ~100 sq ft winter), access to print shop and wood shop, studio visits with critics, and group programming. Need-blind sliding scale of $0–$900 per session covers most program costs. $25 application fee, waivable for hardship. Notifications by early October 2026.
calls.summary: 2–4 week summer or winter residency in upstate NY. Photography eligible. Sliding-scale fee $0–$900; private bedroom + studio.
jury: Will Hutnick, Director of Artistic Programming
Danielle Klebes, Assistant Director of Exhibitions and Residency
prose: The Wassaic Project is a rural artist residency in the foothills of the Berkshires, two hours north of New York City in the small Hudson Valley hamlet of Wassaic. The 2027 program offers two seasonal tracks: summer sessions (3 to 4 weeks, June through September) in the Luther Barn studio building, and winter sessions (2 to 4 weeks, January through March) in the historic Maxon Mills.

Residents receive a private bedroom in a shared house with common spaces, a dedicated studio (200–300 square feet in summer; approximately 100 square feet in winter), 24-hour studio access, and use of the campus print shop and wood shop. Programming includes studio visits with visiting critics and curators, group critiques, and one-on-one studio visits.

Eligibility is unusually broad: individual artists, collaborative teams, groups of two or more, and family-residency applicants are all welcome. Media accepted include photography alongside painting, sculpture, installation, sound, video, and writing.

Cost is on a need-blind sliding scale from $0 to $900 per session, covering most program costs. The application fee is $25 (waivable for financial hardship). Selection is by a panel including the three Wassaic Project Co-Directors (Eve Biddle, Bowie Zunino, Jeff Barnett-Winsby), the Director of Artistic Programming (Will Hutnick), and the Assistant Director of Exhibitions and Residency (Danielle Klebes). The 2027 cycle deadline is July 1, 2026; notifications by early October.

calls.title: RAK Art Festival 2027 — Lost in Translation
calls.description: 14th edition of the Ras Al Khaimah Art Festival, organized by the Sheikh Saud bin Saqr Al Qasimi Foundation for Policy Research at the Al Jazeera Al Hamra Heritage Village in the UAE. Theme: Lost in Translation — exploring displacement, migration, cultural adaptation, and the search for belonging across linguistic and cultural boundaries. Open to international artists across four categories: Emerging Artists, Established Artists, Filmmakers, and Students (ages 6–19). All nationalities welcome. Photography eligible alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, installation, video art, and short film. Submit up to four artworks across two mediums maximum, with a 100-word artist statement and 200-word biography. Grand Jury Prize: AED 12,000 + trophy. Photography category prizes: AED 6,000 (1st) and AED 4,000 (2nd). Notifications: July 30, 2026; festival opens January 22, 2027.
calls.location: Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates
calls.summary: 14th edition Ras Al Khaimah Art Festival in UAE. Free entry. AED 12,000 Grand Jury Prize + AED 4,000–6,000 photography category prizes.
prose: The RAK Art Festival is held annually at the Al Jazeera Al Hamra Heritage Village in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates — a restored coastal village that serves as the festival's permanent venue. The 2027 edition marks the festival's 14th year (founded 2013), organized by the Sheikh Saud bin Saqr Al Qasimi Foundation for Policy Research.

The 2027 theme is "Lost in Translation," exploring displacement, migration, cultural adaptation, and the search for belonging across linguistic and cultural boundaries. The brief draws on the experience of being in between languages, cultures, and identities.

The festival accepts work across four eligibility categories: Emerging Artists, Established Artists (minimum two solo exhibitions), Filmmakers, and Students aged 6 to 19. Eligible media include photography, painting and drawing, sculpture and installation, video art, and short films. Each applicant submits up to four artworks total, with no more than two per medium across no more than two mediums.

Cash awards are denominated in UAE dirham. The Grand Jury Prize is AED 12,000 plus a trophy. Photography, Painting, and Drawing category awards are AED 6,000 (1st) and AED 4,000 (2nd). Sculpture/Installation, Video Art, and short film categories carry AED 6,000 awards. Best Student Artwork prizes are AED 2,000 per age category. Submission is free of charge. Selection is overseen by curator Sharon Toval and Festival Director Suqrat Bin Bisher. The 2026 deadline is June 5; results announced July 30, 2026; festival opens January 22, 2027.

calls.title: FiiLTHY GLO Issue 5 — SONDER
calls.description: Independent zine for the strange and unusual seeking work for Issue 5 — SONDER, exploring the intricately layered, sparsely noticed connections that intertwine us across society. Photography accepted alongside painting, collage, mixed media, digital art, sculpture, comic strips, prose, and short stories. Submit 1–5 original works related to the theme. Visual works should be cleanly presented (well-lit, minimal background); writing capped at 900 words per piece. Files named ArtistName_Title_Year. Submit via Google Form linked on the submissions page.
calls.summary: Indie zine for the strange and unusual. Issue 5 theme: SONDER. Photography accepted. Free, worldwide.
prose: FiiLTHY GLO is an independent zine for work in the strange and unusual register, drawing from across visual art and writing. Issue 5 is themed "SONDER" — the constructed word for the realization that every passerby is living a life as vivid and complex as one's own. The brief asks for work that engages with the layered, sparsely noticed connections that intertwine people across society.

Submissions are interdisciplinary: photography is accepted alongside painting, collage, mixed media, digital art, sculpture, comic strips, prose, opinion writing, and short stories. Each artist may submit 1 to 5 original works. Visual works should be cleanly presented — well-lit, minimal background clutter. Writing is capped at 900 words per piece, submitted as PDF.

Filenames follow the format ArtistName_Title_Year. Submissions are made via a Google Form linked on the FiiLTHY GLO submissions page. There is no submission fee, and AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility requires applicants to be 18 years or older and to submit original work only.

The Issue 5 deadline is June 20, 2026. The zine does not publicly specify what selected contributors receive — applicants should email the zine directly to confirm contributor copies, payment, and other compensation details before submitting.

calls.title: Stanley Greene Foundation Emerging Photographers Grant 2026–2027
calls.description: Annual grant from the Stanley Greene Foundation providing a $10,000 award to emerging visual storytellers at the beginning of their careers to develop impactful visual narratives. The program places particular emphasis on photographers from underserved and diverse communities, expanding access to resources and opportunities to bring their stories to life. Award disbursed in two parts: $8,000 upon award and $2,000 upon submission of final materials. Application requires biography (max 1,500 characters), project description (max 2,000 characters), project proposal (max 3,000 characters), and up to 25 images (72 dpi JPG, minimum 1,500 pixels long dimension, sRGB). Submissions reviewed by three Foundation board members in two rounds. Recipients must provide 15 final digital images and a report detailing fund usage; these materials become part of the Foundation's collection. Open to applicants 18+; current students not eligible (graduating before announcement may apply). Honoring the legacy of war photographer and Noor Images co-founder Stanley Greene.
calls.summary: $10,000 grant for emerging visual storytellers, with emphasis on underserved and diverse communities. Honors Stanley Greene's legacy.
prose: The Stanley Greene Foundation Emerging Photographers Grant honors war photographer Stanley Greene, a co-founder of Noor Images who covered conflict zones from Chechnya through West Africa. The Foundation administers the grant in his name, with explicit emphasis on supporting visual storytellers from underserved and diverse communities at the beginning of their careers.

The grant is $10,000, paid in two installments: $8,000 upon award and $2,000 upon completion of the project, contingent on submission of 15 final digital images and a written report detailing how the funds were used. The completion materials become part of the Foundation's archive. The two-stage payment is designed to ensure projects are actually carried through.

Eligibility requires applicants to be 18 or older and not currently enrolled as students at the time of submission, though those graduating before the decision date may apply. One proposal per person; collaborators are accepted. AI-generated imagery is not permitted in the work samples.

Applications are made through Picter and require a biography (up to 1,500 characters), project description (up to 2,000 characters), project proposal (up to 3,000 characters), and up to 25 images at 72 dpi JPG, sRGB, minimum 1,500 pixels on the long dimension. Selection is by a three-member jury drawn from the Stanley Greene Foundation Board, which meets twice — first for finalists, then for the final decision. Applications open May 1, 2026 and close July 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM EDT. Winners announced August 10, 2026.

calls.title: Quinn Emanuel Los Angeles Artist-in-Residence 2026
calls.description: Four-month studio residency at Quinn Emanuel's Los Angeles office for emerging and mid-career artists working in any discipline, including photography. The selected artist receives $5,000 per month for four months ($20,000 total) plus an art materials allowance of up to $1,500. The residency runs September–December 2026, followed by a one-month exhibition. The studio is located within the Quinn Emanuel LA office with 24/7 keycard access, parking, and full firm support. At least one work from the residency will be incorporated into the firm's permanent collection. Open to artists living in greater Los Angeles only; international applicants accepted if they secure their own visas. Preference given to underrepresented artists in early/mid-career stages. Submit a CV, an 8–10 image PDF portfolio, and a project proposal (one PDF, max 20MB) by 11:59pm PST May 14, 2026.
calls.summary: $20,000 + $1,500 materials. 4-month studio residency at Quinn Emanuel LA office. Open to all media including photography. Greater LA only.

calls.title: Fundación Botín Art Grants 2026/2027
calls.description: Six annual visual arts grants of €23,000 each to support a research project or training in the visual arts. Photography is explicitly included alongside drawing, film/video/new media, mixed-media, painting, sculpture, and craft. Grants run for nine months and cover living expenses, travel, accommodation, studio rental, equipment, and production costs, plus medical insurance for recipients travelling outside their country of residence. One grant prioritizes Spanish artists or Spain residents (5+ years) under age 30 relocating abroad. Applications open to individual artists of any nationality; project must involve practical artistic work, not theoretical study. Online registration is followed by postal submission of up to 40 single-sided A4 pages including ID, CV (3 pages max), project description (10 pages max), and graphic documentation. Applications must be postmarked by Friday, May 8, 2026 (received until May 22 if postmarked by deadline). Results announced before July 17, 2026. Public exhibition at Centro Botín; possible acquisitions for the Foundation's Collection.
calls.summary: Six €23,000 nine-month research grants for international visual artists, photography included. Postal application postmarked by May 8.

calls.title: 24th DongGang International Photo Festival 2026 Open Call
calls.description: Open call for the 24th DongGang International Photo Festival, held July 17 – October 11, 2026 in Yeongwol, South Korea. Theme: 'The Silence that Shapes' — exploring how humans interpret nature and what we project onto landscapes versus what nature actually reveals. 15–20 artists are selected by the festival's curatorial team, including one 'Artist of the Year' who receives a solo exhibition with production support and travel/accommodation to attend the opening. Other selected artists receive outdoor exhibition space, production assistance, and inclusion in the festival catalog and press. Open to individual artists and collectives worldwide. Submit 8–12 images (JPEG or TIFF, minimum 4000 px on long side) plus CV and an artist statement under 400 words by email or WeTransfer. Notification by June 10, 2026.
calls.summary: 24th DIPF Yeongwol, South Korea. Theme: The Silence that Shapes. 15–20 artists selected. Artist of the Year solo show + travel.

calls.title: Inner Landscapes
calls.description: Open call for Mental Health Awareness Month inviting lens-based artists to reflect on mental health and its relationship to everyday life. Considers how internal experiences are shaped by social, cultural, and environmental conditions and expressed through image-making. Welcomes work engaging with care, fatigue, stability, imbalance, support systems, and personal coping strategies. Selected works featured in a one-month online exhibition on Der Greif's homepage (May 15 – June 15, 2026), plus participation in small-group online critique sessions through Der Greif's Face-to-Face program. Selected artists may also be invited to submit their portfolio to Der Greif Studio. Voluntary €5 or €10 donation; financial assistance available on request.
calls.summary: Mental health theme. One-month online exhibition at Der Greif + roundtable critique session with peers. Voluntary fee, vouchers available.
